lead: Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide to prevent intraoperative carcinoid crisis, and never let it delay fluids and vasopressors.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide to prevent intraoperative carcinoid crisis, and never let it delay fluids and vasopressors. Why Why Be ready to manage crisis with fluids and vasopressors — vasopressin, phenylephrine — as well as octreotide, and treat preparedness rather than prophylaxis as the safeguard. Additional cautions Additional cautions NCCN states prophylactic octreotide is likely ineffective in preventing intraoperative carcinoid crisis, NANETS 2017 says prevention has not been established, and NANETS 2020 calls the role of analogues in preventing crisis in pancreatic NET undefined. Evidence & sources The roadmap's quoted 1 to 2% incidence during 177Lu-dotatate comes from a narrative review whose authors state the diagnosis lacks agreed criteria and whose own 127 administrations over five years produced no crisis at all — its single adverse event was bronchospasm in a patient with endobronchial carcinoid, attributed to crisis or not on clinical reasoning alone. Surgical series cited by NANETS report intraoperative event rates of 24 to 30% despite octreotide, with liver metastases the strongest predictor in one of them. The NANETS 2017 octreotide recommendation is internally conflicted, stating that the literature does not support prophylaxis while sanctioning an intraoperative infusion of 100 to 500 micrograms per hour as harmless practice. Whether §7 is reframed as crisis preparedness for every patient with neuroendocrine liver metastases is alignment area 11. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Maintain complete allocation/renewal records with a named coordinator and physician sign-off. Required record elements are listed in the information panel.
text: Standard Evidence D Maintain complete allocation/renewal records with a named coordinator and physician sign-off. Required record elements are listed in the information panel. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × Maintain the allocation record and assign responsibility for renewals from the start: diagnosis and histology, baseline burden, primary and last-treatment dates, serial response imaging, extrahepatic staging, request and extension dates, score route, and named coordinator and physician sign-off. Indications Preferred when Every candidate from first submission. MMaT means median MELD at transplant for the donor hospital used in the match run, not a fixed national score; an MMaT-relative exception below 15 is assigned 15 under Policy 9.4.E, and exceptions generally require 90-day extensions under 9.4.C. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let the imaging-timing wording drift. The guidance requires radiologic workup for extrahepatic disease 'at least 3 months prior to initial or extension MELD exception request (submit date)', including somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy or Ga-68 imaging or PET; that wording is reproduced rather than changed to 'within three months', and the intended timing is confirmed with the review process before filing while current clinical staging is kept. Evidence & sources Reassess eligibility at progression, recurrence, new extrahepatic findings and each extension. Exploratory laparoscopy or laparotomy is not required for the exception. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Offer transplantation only within a trial or prospective registry, under restrictive criteria, through the nonstandard Adult Transplant Oncology Review Board route scored at MMaT-3.
text: Reasonable Evidence C PROTOCOL REGISTRY Offer transplantation only within a trial or prospective registry, under restrictive criteria, through the nonstandard Adult Transplant Oncology Review Board route scored at MMaT-3. Indications Preferred when A young patient with liver-limited, unresectable, well-differentiated disease whose primary has been out for at least six months without recurrence, who has shown stability under observation, and who will be entered in the registry. In the Milan series 280 referrals produced 88 patients meeting Milan-NET criteria, of whom 42 were transplanted and 46 were not, the split driven by waiting-list capacity, age and patient refusal: 5- and 10-year overall survival were 97.2% and 88.8% with transplantation versus 50.9% and 22.4% without, median not reached versus 62 months. A later single-centre comparison from the same unit, 104 Milan-in patients of whom 48 were transplanted and 56 resected, found 10-year survival 93% versus 75% and disease-free survival 52% versus 18%. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Allocation eligibility does not establish routine clinical benefit, and NCCN deems liver transplantation investigational, acknowledging the considerable associated risks. Neuroendocrine liver metastasis is not a standardised OPTN MELD exception: use the nonstandard 'other liver cancer or tumour, specify' pathway with a written narrative, and confirm the current OPTN policy text before any listing decision. Evidence & sources Read the evidence with its selection in view. Allocation in the Milan series was non-randomised, recipients were 15 years younger (median 40.5 versus 55.5 years) in a cohort where age was itself an independent predictor of death, and 18 of the 22 patients who declined transplant did so because they judged their own health normal, so the comparison arm is self-selected on wellbeing. Propensity score could not be matched on in 88 patients and entered only as a covariate; the adjusted transplant survival benefit was 6.82 months at 5 years (95% CI 1.10–12.54) rising to 38.43 months at 10 years (21.41–55.45), with an adjusted hazard ratio for death without transplant of 7.4 (2.4–23.0). The non-transplant arm predates current therapy — 8.7% had PRRT, 2.2% targeted agents, none had cytoreductive liver resection — and WHO 2010 review reclassified 8.7% of them as G3 against 0% of recipients. 37 of 42 grafts (88%) were marginal quality. The resection comparison reports univariate analysis only, with transplant recipients younger, more heavily involved (59% versus 21% above 25% liver involvement), higher Ki-67, node-positive primaries in 79% versus 18%, and selected by a test of time — median 38.5 months from primary resection to liver surgery versus 6.5 months — while the resection arm had no routine lymphadenectomy and 11% R1. Six of the nine deaths after transplantation were attributed to transplant sequelae rather than cancer. Sufficient to justify a protocol; not sufficient to make transplantation a routine option. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Milan series, non-randomised: 5-/10-y OS 97.2%/88.8% with LT (n=42) vs 50.9%/22.4% without (n=46); adjusted HR for death without LT 7.4 (2.4–23.0) Recipients 15 y younger; comparison arm self-selected and predates current therapy
Same unit, Milan-in, univariate: 10-y survival 93% LT (n=48) vs 75% resection (n=56); DFS 52 vs 18% LT arm selected by time (38.5 vs 6.5 mo to liver surgery); resection arm 11% R1

lead: Where disease is limited enough to clear, compare resection and cytoreduction against transplantation at the same board before listing.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Where disease is limited enough to clear, compare resection and cytoreduction against transplantation at the same board before listing. Indications Preferred when Favourable-biology patients are often cytoreduction candidates too, and organ scarcity limits transplantation; ENETS 2024 reduces transplantation to a rare consideration in selected individuals after resecting the primary to leave liver-only disease. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not list a patient whose disease a hepatectomy would clear — limited disease amenable to curative liver resection excluded 75 of 280 referrals in the Milan series. Evidence & sources Recurrence after transplantation is predominantly extrahepatic and late (median disease-free interval 78 months, with the liver involved in 2 of 25 recurrences) while after resection it is intrahepatic and early (24 months, liver involved in 37 of 42); 17 of 19 resection deaths were cancer-related, almost all from intrahepatic progression to liver failure. That contrast is the strongest argument for transplantation on this page, and it comes from an unadjusted comparison of two cohorts accrued over 36 years. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not list G3 disease or neuroendocrine carcinoma, any extrahepatic disease, a patient whose primary is still in place, a patient with no documented observation period, or a patient not entered in the registry.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not list G3 disease or neuroendocrine carcinoma, any extrahepatic disease, a patient whose primary is still in place, a patient with no documented observation period, or a patient not entered in the registry. Why Why Local policy, stated as policy rather than as evidence. Extrahepatic progression, including new Ga-68-positive lymph nodes, calls for delisting; reconsideration may be possible after all extrahepatic disease is resected and absent for at least six months, while extrahepatic solid-organ metastases such as lung or bone are described as permanent exclusion. Additional cautions Additional cautions Do not treat a local complete response after liver-directed therapy as an automatic transplant exception, and record bridge or downstaging separately from definitive local treatment. Evidence & sources Any centre age or hepatic tumour-burden cutoff must be labelled local or attributed to its selection framework — the supplied guidance specifies none, while the Milan criteria carry an age limit under 60 and under 50% liver involvement and ESMO quotes age under 60 and Ki-67 under 10%. Whether the programme opens a NELM transplant protocol at all is unresolved approval item 5. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not take the published series' criteria as evidence-derived thresholds.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not take the published series' criteria as evidence-derived thresholds. Why Why They are protocol conditions: well-differentiated G1–G2 disease, portal-drained primary already resected, liver-only disease, hepatic involvement below a defined threshold, an age limit, and a documented period of stability before listing. Additional cautions Additional cautions Reading them as a selection rule validated against outcome. The Milan-NET criteria were proposed in 2007, before the cohort they are now quoted from, so the 2016 analysis measures the outcome of patients chosen by the criteria rather than testing the criteria themselves. They do not include nodal status of the primary, yet nodal involvement was the only independent predictor of post-transplant survival in the resection comparison (hazard ratio 5.7, 1.3–24) while liver involvement above 50% and G3 tumour were not — the criteria may be selecting on the wrong variable. ESMO's version of the same thresholds carries level IV evidence and is tighter than several published series. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Resection comparison: nodal involvement the only independent predictor of post-transplant survival, HR 5.7 (1.3–24); liver involvement >50% and G3 were not None

lead: WHO 2019: unequivocal hepatocytic AND cholangiocytic differentiation within one tumor on H&E. Immunostains are supportive, not essential.
text: Standard Evidence C WHO 2019: unequivocal hepatocytic AND cholangiocytic differentiation within one tumor on H&E. Immunostains are supportive, not essential. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × The diagnosis is histological. WHO 2019 requires unequivocal hepatocytic and cholangiocytic differentiation within a single tumour, made on routine haematoxylin and eosin, with immunostains supportive rather than essential. Indications Preferred when Every case. The international consensus that fed the WHO fifth edition is explicit that diagnosis rests on routine histopathology and that immunostains are supportive, not essential — which matters because a tumour can be biphenotypic at the level of the individual cell rather than containing two separate areas. The fifth edition's own summary states the requirement the same way and lists what is now outside the category: the Allen double-cancer and combined types, and the Goodman collision and fibrolamellar types. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not make this diagnosis on imaging, on tumour markers, or on an immunohistochemical panel alone. NCCN states plainly that diagnosis through imaging is difficult because the features are a mixture of both, that misdiagnosis may occur, and that thorough pathology review is recommended where cHCC-CCA is suspected. Evidence & sources WHO 2019 dropped the stem-cell subtypes of the 2010 classification and reassigned cholangiolocarcinoma, formerly the cholangiolocellular subtype, to small-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma unless an unequivocal HCC component coexists. It keeps the classical type and recognises intermediate cell carcinoma as a named subtype. Downgraded from B to C on the full-text read for two reasons the documents themselves supply: the 2018 consensus carries no evidence grading and set no threshold for how much of each component is required, and when the resulting definition is applied in practice agreement between the model and pathologist dominant-component reclassification was kappa 0.19, and between two pathologists was kappa 0.37, across 405 already-diagnosed cHCC-CCA cases. The definition is the right one to use; it is not a reproducible measurement. See the quick reference for what moved where. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Treat an LR-M read as a reason to get tissue, not as a diagnosis — LR-M means definite or probable malignancy not specific for HCC, and it is a category that deliberately gives up specificity for the mixed tumour.
text: Standard Evidence C Treat an LR-M read as a reason to get tissue, not as a diagnosis — LR-M means definite or probable malignancy not specific for HCC, and it is a category that deliberately gives up specificity for the mixed tumour. Indications Preferred when Any at-risk patient whose observation is categorised LR-M, and any patient in whom one LR-M feature appears alongside otherwise HCC-like enhancement. On gadoxetate-enhanced MRI in 33 cHCC-CCA against 66 HCC, at least one LR-M feature was present in 93.9% of cHCC-CCA but also in 51.5% of HCC, so specificity was 48.5%. Note that the same paper reports the HCC figure as 48.5% in one place and 51.5% in another; both cannot be right and the direction of the finding — that half of true HCC carries an LR-M feature — is unaffected. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not read LR-M as 'this is cHCC-CCA', and do not read its absence as exclusion. Requiring three or more LR-M features raises accuracy to 80.8% but drops sensitivity to 54.5%, so that rule misses nearly half of these tumours. And targetoid appearance on its own is close to useless here: it was present in 75.8% of cHCC-CCA but also in 65.2% of the HCC controls. There is no threshold that both finds and confirms this tumour. Evidence & sources The policy-relevant figure is the other way round. In 105 HCC and 73 non-HCC malignancies read at two transplant centres, LR-5 was 89–90% specific but only 55–66% sensitive for HCC, and cHCC-CCA made up 63–86% of the false-positive LR-5 reads; LR-M and LR-TIV together identified only 70.8% and 62.3% of cHCC-CCA against 88% and 92% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. LI-RADS protects the HCC diagnosis and detects iCCA as non-HCC; it does not keep this tumour out of an imaging-based HCC pathway. Both case-control series down-sampled HCC relative to true prevalence, so only sensitivity and specificity transfer. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Draw AFP and CA 19-9 together at baseline and record the date and the biliary and inflammatory state at which each was taken; a discrepancy between the markers and the enhancement pattern is itself the signal.
text: Standard Evidence C Draw AFP and CA 19-9 together at baseline and record the date and the biliary and inflammatory state at which each was taken; a discrepancy between the markers and the enhancement pattern is itself the signal. Indications Preferred when Every new liver mass in which cHCC-CCA is on the differential. In a 137-patient three-centre gadoxetate study separating 52 cHCC-CCA from 85 mass-forming iCCA, all in hepatitis B infection or HBV cirrhosis, AFP above 100 ng/mL was the only independent predictor of cHCC-CCA (OR 3.42, p=0.012); AFP was raised in 69.2% of cHCC-CCA against 31.8% of iCCA (p<0.001) while CA 19-9 was raised in 50.0% against 70.6% (p=0.019). AFP above 100 ng/mL alone gave an AUC of 0.687 (sensitivity 69.2%, specificity 68.2%); adding targetoid diffusion restriction raised it to 0.807 (sensitivity 88.5%, specificity 64.7%, Z=3.196, p=0.001). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not expect dual marker elevation to make the diagnosis, and do not quote a single figure for how often it happens: the review literature puts simultaneous AFP and CA 19-9 elevation at about 15% and at about 20% of patients, while a 21-patient Japanese cohort using a wider definition — any HCC marker with any biliary marker — reported 57.1%. Do not use a normal AFP to exclude the diagnosis either: in the Japanese nationwide survey AFP was under 10 ng/mL in 46.2% and CA 19-9 under 37 U/mL in 60.0%, and NCCN notes AFP levels in cHCC-CCA do not differ significantly from those in HCC. A normal CA 19-9 is equally unhelpful — it was in the normal range in 57.9% of 19 transplant recipients whose explants showed cHCC-CCA. Evidence & sources NCCN's Principles of Core Needle Biopsy lists raised CA 19-9 or CEA with suspicion of iCCA or cHCC-CCA as an indication for biopsy even when the lesion meets imaging criteria for HCC. That footnote is the practical trigger this assessment turns on. What the marker work cannot do is the thing that matters most for a transplant pathway: the 137-patient study had no HCC comparator group at all, so it says nothing about the error of calling a cHCC-CCA an HCC and listing it. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Three-centre study, cHCC-CCA vs iCCA: AFP >100 ng/mL only independent predictor of cHCC-CCA, OR 3.42, p=0.012; AUC 0.687 alone, 0.807 with targetoid diffusion restriction HBV-only cohort (52 vs 85); no HCC comparator group

lead: Gadoxetate-enhanced MRI, read against the LR-M feature set The most studied single test. Rim arterial phase hyperenhancement, peripheral washout, delayed central enhancement and targetoid diffusion restriction are the features that pull a tumour out of the HCC algorithm. Targetoid appearance alone was present in 75.8% of cHCC-CCA — but also in 65.2% of matched HCC, so by itself it separates almost nothing.
text: Gadoxetate-enhanced MRI, read against the LR-M feature set Evidence C The most studied single test. Rim arterial phase hyperenhancement, peripheral washout, delayed central enhancement and targetoid diffusion restriction are the features that pull a tumour out of the HCC algorithm. Targetoid appearance alone was present in 75.8% of cHCC-CCA — but also in 65.2% of matched HCC, so by itself it separates almost nothing. Indications Preferred when The at-risk patient with an indeterminate or targetoid mass where the question is whether to biopsy and whether to involve the transplant team before anyone does. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not expect it to separate cHCC-CCA from iCCA. In the three-centre study of tumours with rim or progressive enhancement, progressive enhancement (OR 0.283, p=0.013), targetoid appearance on hepatobiliary phase (OR 0.196, p=0.001) and targetoid diffusion restriction (OR 0.157, p<0.001) all predicted iCCA rather than cHCC-CCA, and only raised AFP went the other way. The best combination still mislabels about a third of iCCA as cHCC-CCA, at 64.7% specificity. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Three-centre study: progressive enhancement OR 0.283, targetoid HBP OR 0.196, targetoid diffusion restriction OR 0.157 all predicted iCCA rather than cHCC-CCA Best combination specificity only 64.7%, mislabelling about a third of iCCA

lead: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound with tumour markers In 134 pathologically confirmed lesions including 35 cHCC-CCA, 74.3% of cHCC-CCA were assigned LR-M on contrast-enhanced ultrasound and the rest were not — 25.7% were assigned LR-5.
text: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound with tumour markers Evidence C In 134 pathologically confirmed lesions including 35 cHCC-CCA, 74.3% of cHCC-CCA were assigned LR-M on contrast-enhanced ultrasound and the rest were not — 25.7% were assigned LR-5. Indications Preferred when A problem-solving tool at a centre with the expertise, in a patient in whom MRI is contraindicated or non-diagnostic. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Not for whole-liver assessment, surveillance or staging — NCCN does not recommend it for those. And read the performance figures, not the LR-M proportion: the CEUS LI-RADS criteria for cHCC-CCA were 40.0% sensitive and 89.9% specific with an AUC of 0.649, and the authors recalculated the positive predictive value at realistic disease prevalence as 1.6% to 39.6%. A positive read is wrong most of the time. A quarter of these tumours reading LR-5 is the failure mode that puts a cHCC-CCA onto an HCC transplant pathway undetected. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Diagnostic series, 134 lesions (35 cHCC-CCA): LR-M 74.3%, LR-5 25.7%; CEUS LI-RADS cHCC-CCA criteria sensitivity 40.0%, specificity 89.9%, AUC 0.649 PPV at realistic prevalence only 1.6% to 39.6%

lead: Accept an atypical pattern as the finding and move to tissue In 30 pathology-proven cHCC-CCA from 891 consecutive liver resections, 70% showed imaging atypical for HCC — which is to say the pre-operative read did not identify HCC in most of them, and did in the remaining 30%.
text: Accept an atypical pattern as the finding and move to tissue Evidence C In 30 pathology-proven cHCC-CCA from 891 consecutive liver resections, 70% showed imaging atypical for HCC — which is to say the pre-operative read did not identify HCC in most of them, and did in the remaining 30%. Indications Preferred when Most patients. The useful output of imaging in this disease is 'this does not behave like HCC', which is a decision to biopsy and to involve pathology, not a diagnosis. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not keep repeating imaging in the hope of a pattern that will not come. And do not over-read the 70%: it was derived retrospectively with the pathology already known, which inflates how readily atypia is spotted prospectively. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not accept "imaging characteristics consistent with intrahepatic mixed hepato-cholangiocarcinoma on CT or MRI" as a diagnostic criterion. There is no such imaging phenotype.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not accept "imaging characteristics consistent with intrahepatic mixed hepato-cholangiocarcinoma on CT or MRI" as a diagnostic criterion. There is no such imaging phenotype. Why Why Replace it with a histological criterion. The local Mixed Hepatocholangiocarcinoma CPG of 11 April 2022 states that criterion verbatim and then asks only for 'biopsy or cytology results demonstrating malignancy' — which is a criterion for cancer, not for this cancer. The OPTN review-board pathway that now governs the allocation request requires biopsy-proven mixed HCC-iCCA. Additional cautions Additional cautions The practical consequence of the current wording is that a patient can satisfy the local protocol without any evidence of cholangiocytic differentiation at all, and then be submitted for an exception that requires it. Evidence & sources The 2019 WHO change made this worse rather than better: because subtypes with stem-cell features were redistributed to HCC and iCCA, the tumours now called cHCC-CCA are a narrower set than the ones most of the imaging literature describes. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not call two separate tumours — one HCC, one iCCA — in the same liver a cHCC-CCA.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not call two separate tumours — one HCC, one iCCA — in the same liver a cHCC-CCA. Why Why Report it as what it is: synchronous primary liver cancers. The WHO definition is one tumour containing both differentiations, and the fifth edition explicitly excludes the double-cancer and collision types from the category. In the 19-patient multicentre transplant series, the 8 patients with genuinely mixed tumours had a mean survival of 61.6 months against 15.5 months in the 11 with separate HCC and cholangiocarcinoma lesions (p=0.025) — on 8 and 11 patients, which is as readily a chance finding as a biological one. Additional cautions Additional cautions The international very-early-iCCA study made mixed hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma in the same nodule an explicit exclusion criterion, and analysed 48 of the 81 explant cholangiocarcinomas it found among 25,016 transplants. Mixing true mixed tumours with separate synchronous primaries is the commonest way the published outcome figures in this disease become uninterpretable — and, as clinical decision 5 says, that same paper is the one whose 3 cm threshold now governs cHCC-CCA listing. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not let a radiomic or deep-learning classifier stand in for histology, however good its published performance.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not let a radiomic or deep-learning classifier stand in for histology, however good its published performance. Why Why Treat these as research tools that may eventually tell you which component drives behaviour. A deep-learning model trained on HCC and iCCA whole-slide images reclassified 405 cHCC-CCA tumours as HCC-like or iCCA-like, and in the liver transplant subset the iCCA-like tumours had 5-year overall survival of 45.4% against 76.4% for the HCC-like ones, HR 2.69 (95% CI 1.15–6.31). Additional cautions Additional cautions No such model is validated for a listing decision, an operative decision or a regimen choice, and none has been tested prospectively. There is also no ground truth: the model was trained on pathologist-assigned labels in a paper that simultaneously showed dominant-component reclassification has kappa 0.19 for model versus pathologist and 0.37 between pathologists, and the reclassification is done on resection or explant slides, which do not exist at listing. Nothing on this page should be done on a model output. Evidence & sources What the result does mean is uncomfortable and belongs at the board: if the entity splits into two groups 31 percentage points apart in 5-year post-transplant survival, then every pooled cHCC-CCA survival figure on this page is a weighted average of two diseases in unknown proportions. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Deep-learning reclassification of 405 cHCC-CCA: LT subset 5-y OS 45.4% vs 76.4%, iCCA-like vs HCC-like, HR 2.69 (95% CI 1.15–6.31) Not tested prospectively; needs resection/explant slides; pathologist kappa 0.19–0.37

lead: A biopsy showing only HCC, or only cholangiocarcinoma, does not exclude the other component — the sampling problem is the central diagnostic fact of this disease.
text: Standard Evidence C A biopsy showing only HCC, or only cholangiocarcinoma, does not exclude the other component — the sampling problem is the central diagnostic fact of this disease. Indications Preferred when Say this out loud at the board whenever a biopsy result is being used to route a patient. In 21 resected cHCC-CCA with pre-operative imaging and biopsy, a mixed imaging pattern was 48% sensitive and 81% specific, biopsy alone was 48% sensitive and 100% specific, and either test positive gave 60% sensitivity and 82% specificity. The mechanism is in the same paper: CK19 was positive in 33% of the biopsies but 84% of the corresponding surgical specimens, so the needle systematically under-detects the cholangiocytic component. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not treat a single-component biopsy as a settled histology in a patient who is about to be listed, resected or started on a regimen chosen for that histology. NCCN says it directly: needle biopsies will not necessarily show both elements of the malignancy. In the 19-patient multicentre transplant series only 4 patients were biopsied before transplantation and all 4 were read as HCC — a sensitivity of 0 in that series. Evidence & sources A specificity of 100% with a sensitivity of 48% means the result you can act on is a positive one. A biopsy reporting cHCC-CCA is almost certainly right; a biopsy reporting pure HCC in a tumour that looks wrong on imaging has told you very little. Both figures come from 21 cases against 21 controls, so the confidence intervals are wide and the 1:1 construction means the predictive values do not transfer to a surveillance population in which this tumour is 1–5% of nodules. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: 21 resected cHCC-CCA: biopsy sensitivity 48%, specificity 100%; mixed imaging 48%/81%; either test 60%/82%; CK19+ in 33% of biopsies vs 84% of specimens 21 cases vs 21 controls; wide CIs; predictive values do not transfer

lead: Transplant assessment requires biopsy-proven mixed HCC–iCCA. The pCCA transperitoneal-biopsy prohibition does not apply here.
text: Standard Evidence D Transplant assessment requires biopsy-proven mixed HCC–iCCA. The pCCA transperitoneal-biopsy prohibition does not apply here. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × If the transplant pathway is in play, tissue is mandatory, not optional — the OPTN review-board criteria require biopsy-proven mixed HCC-iCCA, and the transperitoneal-route prohibition you apply in perihilar disease does not carry over here. Indications Preferred when Discuss the route with the transplant team before the needle, as NCCN's HCC algorithm advises, but obtain the tissue. The 2024 ILTS-ILCA consensus recommends biopsy in HCC transplant candidates specifically to rule out cholangiocarcinoma or a mixed tumour because it changes eligibility, prognosis and treatment (weak evidence, moderate strength). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not import the perihilar cholangiocarcinoma rule — there, avoidance of transperitoneal biopsy is a condition of OPTN Policy 9.5.A and the Mayo protocol, and this is the perihilar CCA pathway's constraint, not this one. The local CPG's position, that transperitoneal aspiration or biopsy 'should be minimized but are not excluded', is the defensible one and is now reinforced by the requirement for biopsy proof. Evidence & sources Grade D because no study measures seeding risk after biopsy of a cHCC-CCA, and none compares routes. The requirement for tissue is a policy fact; the safety of the route is an extrapolation from HCC and iCCA biopsy practice. The ILTS-ILCA statement is cited here from its abstract and the guidance table reproduced in the 2026 transplant overview, not from a full-text read. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Send multigene panel testing on the diagnostic specimen in any patient whose disease is advanced, recurrent or likely to need systemic therapy.
text: Standard Evidence C Send multigene panel testing on the diagnostic specimen in any patient whose disease is advanced, recurrent or likely to need systemic therapy. Indications Preferred when Every advanced case, and preferably on the diagnostic rather than the explant specimen. NCCN states that panel testing should be considered in all patients with advanced-stage mixed tumours to identify targetable alterations associated with cholangiocarcinoma. In the largest genomic series — 150 cHCC-CCA against 2,372 HCC profiled commercially — potentially actionable alterations were found in 52 of 150 (34.7%) against 462 of 2,372 HCC (19.5%), the 59 alterations comprising IDH1 or IDH2 in 16, FGFR2 in 11, BRCA1 or BRCA2 in 7, ERBB2 in 5, BRAF in 4 and MET in 3. In a separate 72-case series FGFR2 alteration was found in 26.4% and strong HER2 protein expression in 8.3%, on 19 and 6 patients respectively. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not expect microsatellite instability or mismatch-repair deficiency to be the answer, and do not make them the only test ordered: all 72 tumours in one series were mismatch-repair proficient, no deficiency was found in any of 24 cHCC-CCA in another (2 of 97 primary liver carcinomas overall, both iCCA), and only 4 of 150 (2.7%) were tumour-mutational-burden high at a median burden of 2.5 mutations per megabase. Note what 0 of 24 actually licenses: an upper 95% bound of about 14%, so this is uncommon rather than absent. Evidence & sources The genomic argument that cHCC-CCA is 'really HCC' has to be stated more carefully after the large series. TERT promoter and TP53 alterations do predominate — TP53 60.0% in cHCC-CCA against 36.9% in HCC, TERT promoter 50.0% against 59.3% — and in 20 microdissected tumours TERT promoter mutation was present in both components, establishing clonal common origin. But CTNNB1, the classic HCC driver, was under 7% against over 34% in HCC, and the iCCA-typical drivers are present at low frequency: IDH1 8.0% against 0.3%, IDH2 2.7% against 0.04% and FGFR2 7.3% against 0.3%. That directly contradicts the 20-tumour series that found no IDH1, IDH2, FGFR2 or BAP1 at all, which with 20 cases could not exclude frequencies below about 15%. Cite both. The practical point is that a biliary target is uncommon but real, and you will not find it without the panel. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Core needle biopsy of the index lesion NCCN lists raised CA 19-9 or CEA with suspicion of iCCA or cHCC-CCA as an indication for core needle biopsy even in a lesion that meets imaging criteria for HCC, and lists biopsy for any lesion highly suspicious for malignancy that does not meet HCC imaging features.
text: Core needle biopsy of the index lesion Evidence C NCCN lists raised CA 19-9 or CEA with suspicion of iCCA or cHCC-CCA as an indication for core needle biopsy even in a lesion that meets imaging criteria for HCC, and lists biopsy for any lesion highly suspicious for malignancy that does not meet HCC imaging features. Indications Preferred when The patient whose destination depends on histology: a transplant pathway candidate, a patient in whom a systemic regimen must be chosen, a non-cirrhotic patient with an LR-5 pattern. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Obtain it before ablation if ablation is contemplated, because the opportunity closes. A negative result for the second component changes nothing. lead: Proceed to resection without tissue NCCN's Principles of Surgery for intrahepatic biliary disease state that a pre-operative biopsy is not always necessary before a definitive potentially curative resection, and that a suspicious mass in the proper clinical setting should be treated as malignant. Surgical resection without core needle biopsy should be considered with multidisciplinary review.
text: Proceed to resection without tissue Evidence C NCCN's Principles of Surgery for intrahepatic biliary disease state that a pre-operative biopsy is not always necessary before a definitive potentially curative resection, and that a suspicious mass in the proper clinical setting should be treated as malignant. Surgical resection without core needle biopsy should be considered with multidisciplinary review. Indications Preferred when The fit patient with a resectable mass in whom the operation would not change whichever histology came back — because the operation this page recommends, anatomical resection with regional lymphadenectomy, covers both components. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not use it to skip the transplant question in a cirrhotic patient with a small tumour, and do not use it when the plan includes an extent of lymphadenectomy that depends on the answer. A resection done without tissue makes the diagnosis but forfeits the option of starting on the NLRB guidance route (nonstandard review), which needs biopsy proof and six months of stability. lead: Repeat biopsy at recurrence or progression NCCN recommends considering repeat biopsy in metastatic or locally advanced recurrence after prior resection or local therapy, to establish the dominant histology at recurrence, and again at progression where areas of response and progression are discordant.
text: Repeat biopsy at recurrence or progression Evidence C NCCN recommends considering repeat biopsy in metastatic or locally advanced recurrence after prior resection or local therapy, to establish the dominant histology at recurrence, and again at progression where areas of response and progression are discordant. Indications Preferred when Any recurrence in which an isolated HCC or cholangiocarcinoma component would change the regimen, in a patient still fit for further systemic therapy. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not re-biopsy when the result would not change the plan, and do not assume the recurrence carries the same component mix as the primary. The sampling problem of this assessment applies unchanged to the recurrence, and no study has measured how often a recurrence biopsy in this disease reproduces the primary's histology. lead: Do not accept a fine-needle aspirate reporting malignancy as the histological basis for a cHCC-CCA diagnosis.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not accept a fine-needle aspirate reporting malignancy as the histological basis for a cHCC-CCA diagnosis. Why Why Core needle biopsy, with architecture, and with the pathologist told what the question is. The diagnosis is morphological and depends on seeing two differentiations in one tumour, which a cytological preparation is poorly placed to show, and the consensus that created the definition is a pathology document that says so. Additional cautions Additional cautions The local CPG's diagnostic criterion accepts cytology showing malignancy. That satisfies neither the WHO definition nor the OPTN requirement for biopsy-proven mixed histology, and it is the single wording on the local document most likely to produce a declined exception request. lead: Stage with the AJCC 8th edition intrahepatic bile duct system: it explicitly covers combined hepatocellular cholangiocarcinoma, and it is the system that has a nodal category.
text: Standard Evidence C Stage with the AJCC 8th edition intrahepatic bile duct system: it explicitly covers combined hepatocellular cholangiocarcinoma, and it is the system that has a nodal category. Indications Preferred when Every case, from the first board. The 8th edition states that all intrahepatic bile duct carcinomas, including combined hepatocellular cholangiocarcinomas, are covered by that staging system, and the NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers guideline reproduces the tables. T1a is a solitary tumour 5 cm or less without vascular invasion; T1b solitary above 5 cm; T2 solitary with intrahepatic vascular invasion or multiple tumours; T3 perforation of the visceral peritoneum; T4 direct invasion of local extrahepatic structures. Any N1 is stage IIIB. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not stage this with BCLC and stop — BCLC has no nodal category at all, and nodal disease is one of the two findings that most changes what you can offer. But do not treat the AJCC stage as the prognosis either. In the 40-recipient Korean registry series neither pre-transplant Milan status, nor tumour number, nor maximum tumour size predicted overall or recurrence-free survival, while perineural invasion (HR 5.14, 95% CI 1.07–24.69), portal vein tumour thrombosis (HR 13.43, 95% CI 2.17–83.21) and microvascular invasion (HR 4.56, 95% CI 1.36–15.22) did — all of them explant findings. Record the stage and the pathological variables separately. Evidence & sources Regional nodes for the intrahepatic bile duct system are those associated with the hilar hepatic artery, portal vein and cystic duct, and the inferior phrenic, gastrohepatic, periduodenal and peripancreatic regions. Downgraded from B to C on the full-text read: the sentence covering combined tumours was confirmed only from NCCN's reproduction of the AJCC tables and not from the manual, and no study has validated this staging system in this histology. The hazard ratios above rest on 4, 3 and 19 patients respectively and are directional only. See the quick reference. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Registry, 40 recipients, HRs (95% CI): perineural invasion 5.14 (1.07–24.69), PVTT 13.43 (2.17–83.21), MVI 4.56 (1.36–15.22); Milan status not predictive HRs rest on 4, 3 and 19 patients — directional only; all explant findings

lead: Image the chest, and look specifically for nodal disease — the lymph node is the second commonest site of first recurrence in this tumour, which is not true of HCC.
text: Standard Evidence C Image the chest, and look specifically for nodal disease — the lymph node is the second commonest site of first recurrence in this tumour, which is not true of HCC. Indications Preferred when Every case. In a single-centre Japanese series of 19 resected cHCC-CCA, the tumour behaved like a biliary cancer in this respect: the liver was the commonest recurrence site but the lymph node was second, where in HCC it is not, and biliary invasion was present in 36.8% against 5.0% of the institution's HCC resections. The narrative surgical literature puts nodal metastasis in cHCC-CCA at 25–35%. Where nodal recurrence happens, it concentrates proximally: in a mapping study of 53 patients whose first recurrence after resection of a primary liver cancer was in regional nodes, the hepatic hilum was involved in 62.3% and the portal vein–vena cava region in 39.6%. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not accept a staging package built for HCC. A liver-only protocol with no chest imaging and no deliberate nodal assessment will miss the two findings that most often change the plan. And read the mapping study for what it is: only 11 of its 53 patients had cHCC-CCA, the denominator is patients who recurred in nodes rather than patients at risk, so the percentages describe where disease goes and not how likely it is to go there, and the median node count at the original operation was 6. Evidence & sources The local CPG asks for CT of the chest, contrasted liver-protocol MR of the abdomen and pelvis, and an MR bone survey, with FDG-PET added where CA 19-9 is raised and other imaging shows no metastasis. The chest and liver imaging are standard practice; the routine MR bone survey appears in no guideline and is not supported by comparative data — see the limited-evidence section. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Mapping study, nodal first recurrence (n=53): hepatic hilum involved in 62.3%, portal vein–vena cava region in 39.6% Only 11 of 53 cHCC-CCA; denominator is nodal recurrences, not patients at risk

lead: Record which component predominates, with a proportion where the specimen allows it, because the proportion tracks outcome.
text: Standard Evidence C Record which component predominates, with a proportion where the specimen allows it, because the proportion tracks outcome. Indications Preferred when Every resection and explant report. In a four-centre cohort of 306 resected tumours classified by three blinded pathologists on a standardised sampling protocol and split at 70%, median recurrence-free survival was 1.02 years in the 93 HCC-dominant patients, 0.36 years in the 101 balanced and 0.30 years in the 112 CCA-dominant, with median overall survival 3.16, 1.93 and 1.86 years and 5-year overall survival 46.1%, 26.1% and 28.3%. Component proportion stayed independent for recurrence-free survival (balanced HR 1.495, CCA-dominant HR 1.487) and overall survival (HR 1.428 and 1.447), C-index 0.712 and 0.650. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not treat the proportion as a validated classifier, and do not present it as three groups. The only significant contrasts were HCC-dominant against the other two; balanced and CCA-dominant were indistinguishable (recurrence-free survival p=0.592, overall survival p=0.822), so the finding is really binary. WHO 2019 sets no proportion threshold, the 2018 consensus deliberately set none, the 70% cut-off was borrowed from conventions in mixed neuroendocrine, breast and myeloproliferative neoplasms rather than derived here, and the 30% cholangiocytic cut-off from a 72-case series was derived by ROC on the same cohort it was then tested in, at AUC 0.717. They are different numbers from different datasets and they will not agree on the same tumour. Evidence & sources The proportion is the most promising available handle on which backbone to borrow in systemic therapy, and it is the reason to ask for it on every report even while it is not yet a decision rule. Two limits are worth saying out loud: it can only be measured on a resected specimen, so it cannot inform the pre-operative decision; and in the one advanced-disease cohort that tested it, HCC-dominant and iCCA-dominant tumours treated identically did not differ in survival at any threshold from 20% to 80%. Prognostic is not predictive. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Add FDG-PET where CA 19-9 is raised and cross-sectional imaging shows no metastatic disease, and biopsy a suspicious extrahepatic lesion rather than assuming it.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Add FDG-PET where CA 19-9 is raised and cross-sectional imaging shows no metastatic disease, and biopsy a suspicious extrahepatic lesion rather than assuming it. Indications Preferred when The patient about to enter a six-month transplant pathway or a major hepatectomy, in whom an occult extrahepatic deposit would change everything. This is the local CPG's own position and it is a reasonable use of a test with poor performance in HCC and better performance in biliary disease. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not use PET to make the primary diagnosis, and do not treat a negative PET as exclusion of nodal disease. NCCN does not recommend FDG-PET for routine staging in HCC, and no study has measured its performance in cHCC-CCA specifically. Evidence & sources Grade D, and on the full-text read this item now carries no primary citation at all, because the paper previously attached to it is a contrast-enhanced ultrasound study with no PET content. The recommendation is the local document's requirement plus mechanistic reasoning from biliary disease, with no comparative outcome data in this histology and none in any histology reported here. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Sample a radiologically suspicious regional node by endoscopic ultrasound before committing to a six-month transplant pathway.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Sample a radiologically suspicious regional node by endoscopic ultrasound before committing to a six-month transplant pathway. Indications Preferred when A potential transplant pathway candidate with suspicious porta hepatis nodes. Nodal disease is an exclusion in the local protocol and in every published series, so a positive nodal result does not cost candidacy that existed — it identifies a patient who was never a candidate, before six months of therapy and a workup are spent. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let a nodal pass become a pass at the primary if you have reason to keep the primary untouched; they are different sampling targets with different consequences. And note there are no morphological criteria that reliably identify a malignant node, so a 'suspicious node' trigger is a soft one. Evidence & sources This is the local CPG's requirement, written as 'if possible'. It is sound logic with no comparative data behind it, and the ILTS-ILCA consensus attached to it is cited from its abstract rather than from a full-text read. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not use the Milan criteria as a stage.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not use the Milan criteria as a stage. Why Why Record the AJCC stage, and record separately whether the radiological tumour burden falls within Milan, because the published transplant series use Milan as an enrolment limit and the allocation pathway uses a 3 cm solitary limit. They are three different measurements of the same patient and the page keeps them apart deliberately. Additional cautions Additional cautions And know that the radiological measurement is wrong in this tumour in one direction. In 19 transplant recipients whose explants showed cHCC-CCA, 84.2% were within Milan on pre-transplant imaging but only 36.8% remained within Milan on explant pathology (p=0.01 against the matched controls). Imaging-based Milan systematically understages this disease — and imaging-based Milan is exactly the classification the 12-centre transplant analysis used, applied retrospectively at diagnosis for uniformity of analysis rather than as a prospective selection rule, and never validated as a stage in this histology. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not carry an HCC surveillance-and-staging pathway into this disease once the histology is known.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not carry an HCC surveillance-and-staging pathway into this disease once the histology is known. Why Why Switch to the biliary framework: nodal assessment, chest imaging, CA 19-9, and the expectation of early and nodal recurrence. Outcomes sit between HCC and cholangiocarcinoma — in the Taiwan Cancer Registry, among 95,149 primary liver cancers, 5-year overall survival for the combined tumour was 25.7%, intermediate between HCC and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, with 55.5% of the combined group resected and tumour grade unrecorded in 68.7% of the registry entries. Additional cautions Additional cautions Nor should the staging shift become an excuse for pessimism: in 529 SEER patients the median overall survival was 8 months, but that is a whole-registry figure dominated by unresected disease and is not the figure for a resected patient. Neither registry paper should be quoted beyond its descriptive survival. The SEER analysis contains two unreconciled internal contradictions — its abstract states the higher incidence is in women while its text and table report 0.08 per 100,000 in men against 0.03 in women, and the hazard ratio for surgery is 4.94 in the abstract and 4.18 in the table — and in the Taiwan registry the hazard ratio for TACE was 0.56 in the non-surgical stratum and 1.64 in the surgical one, which is the signature of confounding by indication rather than a treatment effect. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Anatomical liver resection to a negative margin, with regional lymphadenectomy, is the only established curative treatment — resection is the standard of care for resectable disease in both NCCN guidelines that address it.
text: Standard Evidence C Anatomical liver resection to a negative margin, with regional lymphadenectomy, is the only established curative treatment — resection is the standard of care for resectable disease in both NCCN guidelines that address it. Indications Preferred when Any patient who meets the criteria above. Both the NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Biliary Tract Cancers guidelines state that liver resection is considered the standard treatment for resectable mixed HCC-CCA, and the contemporary surgical review puts 5-year overall survival after R0 resection at 25–40% with recurrence in more than 60%. On the margin the evidence is not uniform: in an 80-patient Korean hepatectomy series patients with a wide margin did significantly better than those with an R1 resection or a margin of 2 mm or less, while series using a 1 cm cut-off found margin width non-significant. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not offer a non-anatomical wedge where an anatomical resection is achievable, and do not accept a planned close margin. Grade C and not higher because every supporting series is retrospective, single- or few-centre, and none randomises anything — no prospective trial of resection has ever been conducted in this disease. The surgical review that frames the operation is explicit that it manages cHCC-CCA according to oncologic principles developed for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and it does not discuss transplantation at all. Evidence & sources In the first large Western series, 27 patients had a 5-year overall survival of 24% after resection — in a cohort with a 0% rate of cirrhosis, which is why it cannot be set beside the Asian and European transplant series where 60–90% are cirrhotic and hepatitis-B-related. Patients never operated on do not appear in its denominator, and it predates the 2018 consensus and the 2019 WHO classification entirely, so an unknown fraction of those 27 would now be reclassified as small-duct iCCA or excluded as collision tumours. It is still quoted as the baseline poor-prognosis figure in 2026 papers. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Surgical review of retrospective series: 5-y OS after R0 resection 25–40%, recurrence in more than 60% No prospective trial; applies iCCA oncologic principles; does not discuss transplantation

lead: Expect early recurrence, and say the numbers before the operation rather than after it.
text: Standard Evidence C Expect early recurrence, and say the numbers before the operation rather than after it. Indications Preferred when Every consent conversation. In a 95-patient multicentre radical-resection cohort median overall survival was 26.8 months, median recurrence-free survival 7.27 months and 5-year overall survival 23.6%. In 19 tumours resected at a single Japanese centre, 5-year overall survival was 44.7% against 56.6% for HCC and 38.5% for iCCA — differences that did not reach significance, which with 19 patients is uninformative rather than reassuring — while 5-year recurrence-free survival was only 12.2%. In 30 resected tumours from 891 consecutive resections, cHCC-CCA independently predicted worse disease-free survival (HR 3.146, 95% CI 1.854–5.339) and worse overall survival (HR 2.320, 95% CI 1.134–4.747) against HCC, with 5-year disease-free survival 37.3% against 58.3% for HCC and 32.0% for iCCA. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not quote HCC recurrence figures. The one variable that separates a good outcome from a poor one in the largest single-institution series is lymphovascular invasion: 5-year overall survival was 93.3% without it and 35.8% with it in 80 patients, HR 11.35 — with a 95% confidence interval from 3.20 to 40.3, so the direction is secure and the magnitude is not. That same series reported a median overall survival of 85.1 months and 5-year survival of 56.4%, roughly double every other resection cohort here, which points to an unusually early and well-compensated surgical population rather than to better surgery. Do not use it as the resection benchmark in a transplant comparison. Evidence & sources Independent predictors of overall survival in the 95-patient cohort were CA 19-9 of 37 U/mL or more (HR 8.68, p=0.002), Child-Pugh above 5 (HR 5.52, p=0.027), more than one tumour (HR 30.85, p=0.002), tumour size, and post-operative TACE (HR 0.2, p=0.005). Read those as direction at most, and preferably not at all: no confidence intervals are reported, a hazard ratio of 30.85 in a 95-patient Cox model is a sparse-data artefact, and the same model returns an AFP of 200 or more as protective for recurrence-free survival (HR 0.45), which is not biologically credible and most likely marks HCC-dominant tumours that received HCC-directed adjuvant treatment. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: A minimally invasive approach is reasonable in a well-selected patient, provided it does not compromise the margin or the nodal dissection.
text: Reasonable Evidence C A minimally invasive approach is reasonable in a well-selected patient, provided it does not compromise the margin or the nodal dissection. Indications Preferred when Peripheral tumours in a fit patient at a centre with the laparoscopic or robotic volume. NCCN's Principles of Surgery for intrahepatic disease state that minimally invasive approaches by experienced surgeons have been shown to be safe and effective in well-selected cases. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let the approach dictate the lymphadenectomy. The published comparisons of minimally invasive and open resection in intrahepatic biliary malignancy specifically exclude or do not separately report cHCC-CCA, so the oncological comparability claim is borrowed. Evidence & sources [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: In a cirrhotic patient with a small tumour, decide resection against transplantation as one question rather than two — this is clinical decision 5, and operating on the liver first may make transplantation unsuitable.
text: Reasonable Evidence C In a cirrhotic patient with a small tumour, decide resection against transplantation as one question rather than two — this is clinical decision 5, and operating on the liver first may make transplantation unsuitable. Indications Preferred when Any cirrhotic patient with a tumour of 3 cm or less in whom both operations are technically possible. In a three-centre French study of cirrhotic patients with iCCA or cHCC-CCA of 5 cm or less, 49 transplanted patients had lower recurrence than 26 resected patients (18% versus 46%, p=0.01) and higher 5-year recurrence-free survival (75% versus 36%, p=0.004). Note which endpoint moved: 5-year overall survival was 67% against 40% and did not reach significance (p=0.17). The protective hazard ratio for transplantation, 0.23 (95% CI 0.07–0.82, p=0.02), comes from a multivariable model in the 2–5 cm subgroup of 24 transplant against 21 resection patients. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not read that as a treatment effect, and this time the authors say so themselves. A known cholangiocarcinoma diagnosis was an absolute contraindication to transplantation throughout the study period, so all 49 transplant diagnoses were made on the explant — 44 had been listed for HCC and 5 for decompensated cirrhosis. The transplant arm waited a median of 394 days from diagnosis to surgery against 131 days in the resection arm, which the authors state inevitably selected tumours that had not progressed, and 63% of them had pre-operative TACE against 15% of the resected patients. There was no intention-to-treat analysis and no dropout denominator. Read clinical decision 5 before the decision is made. Evidence & sources The local CPG does allow a prior attempted resection onto the transplant pathway, provided there has been a sustained response to neoadjuvant therapy for at least six months after the most recent intervention. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not offer resection for nodal disease beyond the porta hepatis, or for multifocal disease outside a highly selected case.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not offer resection for nodal disease beyond the porta hepatis, or for multifocal disease outside a highly selected case. Why Why Route these patients to clinical decision 7. NCCN's Principles of Surgery for intrahepatic disease are explicit: lymph node metastases beyond the porta hepatis and distant metastatic disease contraindicate resection, gross nodal metastases to the porta hepatis portend a poor prognosis and resection should only be considered in highly selected cases, and multifocal liver disease generally represents intrahepatic spread. This does not establish distant M1 disease: multiple intrahepatic tumors meet T2 criteria unless higher T features apply. Additional cautions Additional cautions Those statements were written for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Applying them to cHCC-CCA is an extrapolation — but it is the extrapolation that matches this tumour's nodal recurrence pattern, which is biliary rather than hepatocellular. lead: Do not promise an HCC outcome to a resected patient because the tumour is HCC-predominant.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not promise an HCC outcome to a resected patient because the tumour is HCC-predominant. Why Why Give the figures for this histology and for the component proportion if it is known. Even the HCC-dominant group in the 306-patient proportion study had a median recurrence-free survival of 1.02 years and a 5-year overall survival of 46.1%. Additional cautions Additional cautions Population-level figures are worse again and should not be quoted to a resection candidate either: 529 SEER patients had a median survival of 8 months and the Taiwan registry gave 5-year overall survival of 25.7%, but both are dominated by patients who were never resected. lead: Perform a regional lymphadenectomy of the porta hepatis when cHCC-CCA is known or suspected, and record the number of nodes retrieved and the number involved.
text: Standard Evidence C Perform a regional lymphadenectomy of the porta hepatis when cHCC-CCA is known or suspected, and record the number of nodes retrieved and the number involved. Indications Preferred when Every resection in which the histology is known or suspected pre-operatively. NCCN's Principles of Surgery for intrahepatic biliary disease state that a regional lymphadenectomy of the porta hepatis is carried out; the contemporary surgical review makes nodal dissection part of the definition of a potentially curative operation and puts nodal metastasis in cHCC-CCA at 25–35%; and where nodal recurrence occurs it concentrates at the hepatic hilum, involved in 62.3% of the 53 patients in the mapping study whose first recurrence was nodal. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not make the dissection contingent on how the tumour looks: the whole problem of this assessment is that the histology is usually not known until afterwards. Nodal status is also an AJCC category — N1 is stage IIIB regardless of T — so an unsampled node leaves the patient unstaged rather than node-negative. Evidence & sources Grade C, and the honest position is that no study has shown that lymphadenectomy improves survival in cHCC-CCA. The case for it is staging information, the nodal recurrence pattern, and concordance with the iCCA guideline that governs the staging system. The mapping study it leans on had only 11 cHCC-CCA patients among 53, counts recurrences rather than patients at risk, and was designed to define radiotherapy volumes. It is not a demonstrated survival benefit. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Nodal mapping study: hepatic hilum involved in 62.3% of 53 patients whose first recurrence was nodal Only 11 cHCC-CCA among 53; counts recurrences, not patients at risk

lead: Where cHCC-CCA was not suspected and no nodes were taken, write that in the operative note as a decision with a reason, not as an omission.
text: Standard Evidence D Where cHCC-CCA was not suspected and no nodes were taken, write that in the operative note as a decision with a reason, not as an omission. Indications Preferred when Every hepatectomy for presumed HCC. This matters because the next surgeon, the pathologist and the board all need to know whether pNx means 'judged unnecessary' or 'not considered'. In a 179-patient single-centre cohort of curative resections for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma including 77 cHCC-CCA, node dissection was performed in only 54 (30%) and reached the 6-node adequacy standard in only 14 of those 54 (26%); the only independent driver of the decision to dissect was a pre-operative diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma (OR 3.33, 95% CI 1.54–7.34, p=0.002), present in 70% of the dissected group against 29% of the undissected. The dissection followed the label, not the tumour. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not leave the nodal status silent. A pNx specimen in a tumour that turns out to be cHCC-CCA is the commonest avoidable information loss in this disease. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Routine regional lymphadenectomy What the guideline wording supports: NCCN carries out a regional lymphadenectomy of the porta hepatis for intrahepatic biliary malignancy, and the narrative reviews of surgical management of cHCC-CCA make R0 resection with regional node dissection the standard.
text: Routine regional lymphadenectomy Evidence C What the guideline wording supports: NCCN carries out a regional lymphadenectomy of the porta hepatis for intrahepatic biliary malignancy, and the narrative reviews of surgical management of cHCC-CCA make R0 resection with regional node dissection the standard. Indications Preferred when Any patient in whom cHCC-CCA is known or suspected pre-operatively, and any patient in whom staging information will change adjuvant or surveillance decisions. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not extend it beyond the porta hepatis as a routine. The nodal mapping study put the para-aortic 16a1, 16a2 and 16b1 regions and the splenic artery and hilum below 10% recurrence, and found no recurrence at all in the para-oesophageal or 16b2 regions. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Nodal mapping study: recurrence <10% at para-aortic 16a1/16a2/16b1 and splenic artery/hilum; none at para-oesophageal or 16b2 stations

lead: Selective lymphadenectomy on intra-operative judgement A single-centre cohort of 179 curative hepatectomies — 102 pure cholangiocarcinoma and 77 cHCC-CCA — reported that selective dissection on clinical judgement did not compromise overall survival: median overall survival was 59.1 months in the undissected group against 30.5 months pN0 and 17.4 months pN1 (p=0.007), with no adjusted difference between pNx and pN0 (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.46–1.30, p=0.34).
text: Selective lymphadenectomy on intra-operative judgement Evidence D A single-centre cohort of 179 curative hepatectomies — 102 pure cholangiocarcinoma and 77 cHCC-CCA — reported that selective dissection on clinical judgement did not compromise overall survival: median overall survival was 59.1 months in the undissected group against 30.5 months pN0 and 17.4 months pN1 (p=0.007), with no adjusted difference between pNx and pN0 (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.46–1.30, p=0.34). Indications Preferred when The HCC-predominant tumour in a cirrhotic patient where hilar dissection carries real morbidity, and the patient in whom the nodal result would not change management. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Read the whole paper, because its other endpoint runs the other way: after adjustment, pNx was an independent adverse factor for progression-free survival (HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.20–3.77, p=0.012). The 59.1-month median in the undissected group is the selection the study is examining — 54% of pNx patients were cHCC-CCA against 19% of the dissected, their tumours were smaller (3.0 against 4.0 cm), earlier staged and less often perineurally invaded, and CA 19-9 was missing in 70% of them. Only 26% of the dissections met the 6-node standard, so the pN0 group is contaminated by understaged patients, which biases the comparison toward no difference. And the cHCC-CCA subgroup analyses, on 77 patients, were all non-significant. Downgraded to D: this is not evidence of equivalence in this histology. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: No nodal dissection Defensible only where the pre-operative diagnosis was HCC, the tumour behaved like HCC, and cHCC-CCA was not on the differential.
text: No nodal dissection Evidence D Defensible only where the pre-operative diagnosis was HCC, the tumour behaved like HCC, and cHCC-CCA was not on the differential. Indications Preferred when Nothing, once the diagnosis is suspected. This option exists on the page because it is what happens to most of these patients in practice, not because it is recommended. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid It leaves the patient unstaged in the system that AJCC says applies to them, it removes the nodal variable from every subsequent adjuvant and surveillance decision, and in the one cohort that examined it, omitting the dissection was independently associated with worse adjusted progression-free survival (HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.20–3.77). Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not extend the dissection to the para-aortic or splenic regions as a routine.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not extend the dissection to the para-aortic or splenic regions as a routine. Why Why Confine the dissection to the porta hepatis and the portal vein–vena cava region, which carried 62.3% and 39.6% of first nodal recurrences in the mapping study. Additional cautions Additional cautions Recurrence in the para-aortic 16a1, 16a2 and 16b1 regions and in the splenic artery and hilum was under 10%, and there was none in the para-oesophageal or 16b2 regions. Downgraded to D: that study maps where recurrence appeared in 53 patients of whom only 11 had cHCC-CCA, its denominator is patients who recurred in nodes rather than patients at risk, the median node count at the original operation was 6 so some apparent recurrences are residual disease in stations nobody dissected, and it was designed to define radiotherapy target volumes rather than the extent of an operation. It is directional evidence about where disease goes, not a trial of dissection extent. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Discuss transplant eligibility at the first multidisciplinary meeting, before an attempted resection or non-protocol treatment that could affect eligibility.
text: Standard Evidence D Discuss transplant eligibility at the first multidisciplinary meeting, before an attempted resection or non-protocol treatment that could affect eligibility. Indications Preferred when Every cirrhotic patient with a small tumour, and every patient in whom the histology is known or suspected and the liver will not tolerate the resection a negative margin requires. The published advantage of transplantation over resection in this disease is confined to small-tumour, cirrhotic populations, which is precisely the group a resection attempt removes from the pathway. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The sequencing recommendation rests on eligibility criteria and on the direction of retrospective comparisons, not on any trial of referral timing — that study does not exist and will not. It also rests on cohorts that cannot speak to a deliberate decision: in the 12-centre analysis only 2 of 99 transplant recipients were knowingly transplanted with the diagnosis, and in the French cirrhosis study a known cholangiocarcinoma diagnosis was an absolute contraindication, so all 49 transplants were explant diagnoses. Evidence & sources The local CPG does permit a prior attempted resection, provided there has been a sustained response to neoadjuvant therapy for at least six months after the most recent intervention. That is more permissive than the perihilar protocol, where surgical violation of the tumour plane is an exclusion. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: 12-centre series: only 2 of 99 transplant recipients were knowingly transplanted with the diagnosis Retrospective; cannot speak to a deliberate transplant decision

lead: NLRB exception review: biopsy-proven mixed HCC–iCCA, solitary ≤3 cm, cirrhosis, unresectable, 6 months stability after local/systemic therapy, no extrahepatic disease; MMaT−3.
text: Standard Evidence D NLRB exception review: biopsy-proven mixed HCC–iCCA, solitary ≤3 cm, cirrhosis, unresectable, 6 months stability after local/systemic therapy, no extrahepatic disease; MMaT−3. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × Use the OPTN National Liver Review Board transplant-oncology criteria as the operative threshold, because those are the criteria the exception request will be judged against — biopsy-proven mixed HCC-iCCA, solitary and 3 cm or less, cirrhosis, unresectable, six months of stability after locoregional or systemic therapy, no extrahepatic disease, score MMaT-3. Indications Preferred when Every listing decision. The guidance also sets the extension rule: imaging every three months confirming the tumour remains 3 cm or less with no extrahepatic disease. Confirm the current OPTN text before any listing decision — this page reflects the guidance as retrieved on 6 October 2026 and the document carries no printed version line. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not plan a pathway against the local CPG's criteria and then discover at submission that they do not match. The local document, approved 11 April 2022, states that candidates are eligible 'regardless of size', does not require cirrhosis, and asks only for biopsy or cytology showing malignancy rather than mixed histology. It also states that the MELD exception application will be made 'once the exception is available from UNOS' — it is now available, and it is narrower than the protocol. Evidence & sources Mind the distinction between referral and allocation. NCCN sets no size limit and says patients whose tumour is limited in size by centre-specific criteria should be evaluated at a transplant centre; the NLRB guidance route (nonstandard review) sets 3 cm; the published series used Milan. A patient can be reasonably referred, reasonably transplanted under a local protocol, and still fail the exception criteria. Know where the 3 cm came from: it is an extrapolation from the 17-centre 'very early' intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma study, which excluded mixed hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma in the same nodule by design, defined its favourable group on explant pathology in 15 patients of whom 46.7% were incidental findings, and supports the 3 cm extension on an intermediate subgroup of 6 patients with 61% 5-year survival. Grade D is generous. [TX-TIMING] [PAYER] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: 17-centre very-early iCCA study: 5-y survival 61% in intermediate subgroup of 6 patients — the basis of the 3 cm extension Excluded mixed HCC-CCA; favourable group 15 patients, 46.7% incidental (explant-defined)

lead: Transplantation for cHCC-CCA within Milan criteria, under a written protocol with prospective registry entry.
text: Reasonable Evidence D PROTOCOL REGISTRY Transplantation for cHCC-CCA within Milan criteria, under a written protocol with prospective registry entry. Indications Preferred when A cirrhotic patient with small-volume, node-negative, well or moderately differentiated disease at a programme that has written its criteria down. In the 12-centre retrospective analysis, 67 patients transplanted for cHCC-CCA within Milan had 5-year overall survival of 70.1% against 73.4% for 1,814 HCC recipients (p=0.806) and disease-free survival of 70.1% against 70.3% (p=0.740), while 5-year recurrence was double: 23.1% against 11.5%, p<0.001. Within Milan, transplantation gave better 5-year disease-free survival than resection (70.3% against 33.6%, p<0.001) but not better overall survival (70.1% against 49.7%, p=0.078). Beyond UCSF criteria 5-year overall survival was 15.8% against 67.3% for HCC. In 32 Korean recipients whose tumours were all found incidentally on the explant, 5-year recurrence was 32.2% and survival 65.8% overall, and 13.3% and 93.3% in the 15 with one or two tumours of 2 cm or less. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not read any of this as a licence to list a diagnosed cHCC-CCA, because almost nobody in it was. Only 11 of 208 patients in the 12-centre analysis had a pre-operative diagnosis of cHCC-CCA and only 2 of those 11 were transplanted; 84 of the 99 transplant recipients had been pre-diagnosed as HCC. The survival 'equivalence' is a non-significant p value in a subgroup of 67, and the significant finding in that same subgroup is that recurrence was double. Milan status was assigned on initial imaging, which in this tumour understages: 84.2% within Milan on imaging fell to 36.8% on explant in a separate matched series. At the Korean centre, patients with a pre-operative diagnosis were principally excluded from transplantation, so that cohort is incidental by construction; its resection comparator was restricted to single 1–4 cm R0 node-negative tumours and still showed no transplant advantage (survival p=0.91, recurrence p=0.22), and post-recurrence survival was significantly worse after transplantation (median 9 against 21 months, p=0.016). The SEER comparison favouring transplantation within Milan rests on 15 matched pairs (p=0.015), 32 pairs overall (p=0.022), and 9 pairs beyond Milan where there was no difference (p=0.340), with Metavir fibrosis stage known in only 120 of 736 patients. Downgraded from C to D for that reason: there is no cohort of any size describing patients deliberately listed with this diagnosis. Evidence & sources The updated meta-analysis of six retrospective comparative studies, now read in full, gives a pooled odds ratio of 0.55 (95% CI 0.38–0.81, p=0.002, I²=0%) for 5-year overall survival favouring transplantation, with the 1-year (0.67, 0.39–1.15) and 3-year (0.70, 0.42–1.17) estimates not significant, and recurrence-free odds ratios of 0.48 at one year and 0.40 at five. Four things qualify it: mean tumour size was 2.19–2.57 cm in the transplant arms against 2.7–6.26 cm in the resection arms, only one of the six studies used propensity matching, leave-one-out analysis flipped the significance of both the 3- and the 5-year overall survival estimates, and the 12-centre analysis contributes 99 of the 215 pooled transplant patients. Nearly all patients in both arms were pathological stage I or II (94.8% against 91.4%), so none of it speaks to beyond-criteria disease. The authors' own conclusion is that transplantation 'could be considered in carefully selected patients' and that the apparent advantage may be selection rather than treatment. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
