lead: Rank the risk with the factors that actually predict transformation, and write them in the note.
text: Standard Evidence C Rank the risk with the factors that actually predict transformation, and write them in the note. Indications Preferred when Every patient in whom transformation is being weighed. From the 533-adenoma series, in order of effect size: TERT promoter mutation odds ratio 67.6 (95% CI 8.3-3072), male sex 18.9 (8.5-44.2), CTNNB1 exon 3 mutation with or without inflammation 9.3 (4.4-20.0), high alcohol intake 4.85, a single nodule on imaging 4.1 (1.7-11.7), fibrosis in the non-tumour liver 3.8 (1.1-11.4), and type 2 diabetes 3.7. TERT promoter mutation was found in 7 of 16 adenomas with malignant transformation (44%) against 179 of 305 carcinomas (59%), 5 of 20 cirrhotic premalignant macronodules (25%) and 0 of 60 typical adenomas; all 7 of the transformed adenomas carrying it also carried a CTNNB1 mutation, which places TERT as a second hit after beta-catenin activation and makes transformation a two-step process. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid These are odds ratios from a cross-sectional surgical series with very wide confidence intervals — the TERT interval runs from 8.3 to 3072, which reflects near-complete separation in a handful of events — and the outcome is a borderline or malignant histological finding at the time of resection, not a prospectively observed event. They rank risk; they do not quantify it, and none has been validated prospectively. TERT promoter mutation is also present by definition only once transformation has occurred, so it confirms rather than pre-empts: it was found in 0 of 60 typical adenomas, a denominator whose upper 95% bound is about 5%, and in 1 of 213 adenomas in a separate series against 3 of 17 borderline lesions. TERT is not always present in adenoma-derived carcinoma either, so a negative result excludes nothing. Evidence & sources Beta-catenin activity is not one thing. Exon 3 deletions and substitutions within the D32-S37 beta-TrCP binding site are highly activating and go with strong homogeneous glutamine synthetase and with malignancy; T41 is moderate; S45, K335 and N387 are weak activators in benign tumours. Ask for the codon, not just the exon. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Where transformation is confirmed, re-stage completely and re-route the case — and do not assume the standardised HCC transplant pathway is available.
text: Standard Evidence D Where transformation is confirmed, re-stage completely and re-route the case — and do not assume the standardised HCC transplant pathway is available. Indications Preferred when The local hepatic adenoma protocol §3 governs this. Complete multiphasic liver imaging, chest CT and alpha-fetoprotein, state the transformation date and the prior adenoma route in the narrative, and route the case. A candidate with an at-risk background — cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B — is assessed against the standardised HCC pathway on its own terms, and this is the HCC pathway from here. A candidate without an at-risk background, which the protocol calls the usual case, cannot be: OPTN Class 5 imaging classification and LI-RADS are defined for patients at risk for carcinoma, most adenoma-derived carcinoma arises in a non-cirrhotic non-at-risk liver, and the lesion therefore cannot be classified on imaging alone. That candidate needs a non-standard review-board request supported by histologic confirmation, complete staging, tumour burden relative to Milan criteria, alpha-fetoprotein, and an explicit statement of why imaging-based classification does not apply. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let a normal alpha-fetoprotein reassure you — the protocol states that alpha-fetoprotein does not exclude carcinoma when normal. Extrahepatic metastasis or macrovascular invasion excludes the candidate from the adenoma protocol either way, in both the at-risk and the non-at-risk case. Evidence & sources The protocol marks this routing VERIFY against the live Policy 9.5 posting before the first such submission, and that verification has not been performed for this page. Treat the routing as the protocol's reasoning, not as confirmed current policy. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Where a borderline lesion is reported, get a second expert liver pathology opinion and sequencing before you call it either thing.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Where a borderline lesion is reported, get a second expert liver pathology opinion and sequencing before you call it either thing. Indications Preferred when Any report of a borderline hepatocellular lesion, a hepatocellular neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential, or atypical adenoma. 7% of the 533 nodules in the molecular series shared intermediate histological features with carcinoma. In the Dutch nationwide male series the diagnosis changed after expert revision plus sequencing in 33 of 66 cases (50%), with final diagnoses of 20 adenoma, 26 uncertain malignant potential and 20 carcinoma, and the revised category tracked tumour-related mortality (5.6%, 35.7% and 44.4%, P=0.031). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not treat borderline as a diagnosis that permits observation. It is a statement that the specimen cannot be classified, which in a male patient or a beta-catenin-activated lesion should be managed as carcinoma until proven otherwise. The two expert pathology series that have examined this both conclude that the adenoma-versus-well-differentiated-carcinoma distinction is prognostically decisive and frequently got wrong. Evidence & sources The dilemmas of atypical and borderline lesions, and the question of which nomenclature to use, are unsettled in the pathology literature itself: the expert reviews concede that the threshold for sufficient versus insufficient atypia remains arbitrary and that the specificity of atypical features in predicting transformation remains to be demonstrated, and the review of the WHO 6th-edition classification adds that in children, patients over 60 and vascular liver disease the morphomolecular features become less well defined, overlap with focal nodular hyperplasia and the line defining malignancy blurs. Name one liver pathologist as the programme's reference reader so that the nomenclature is at least internally consistent. lead: Perform comprehensive specimen or explant mapping in every case and feed the result back to the board.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Perform comprehensive specimen or explant mapping in every case and feed the result back to the board. Indications Preferred when Every resection and every explant. The local hepatic adenoma protocol §8 specifies the dataset: lesion count, largest size, subtype, CTNNB1 findings, haemorrhage, necrosis, atypia, and occult carcinoma; if malignant transformation is found, stage the explant and define post-transplant surveillance at the transplant-oncology conference. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not accept a specimen report that gives a diagnosis without the subtype and the lesion map. Malignant transformation in 4 of 27 male adenomas, and reclassification of half of all presumed male adenomas on expert review, are numbers that only exist because someone looked for them systematically. Evidence & sources This is also the only way the programme will ever know how often its own preoperative assessment was wrong, which is the metric the limited-evidence section says matters most. lead: Do not ablate or embolise a lesion in which transformation is the question.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not ablate or embolise a lesion in which transformation is the question. Why Why Resect it, or biopsy it and then resect it. Both modalities leave viable tissue and neither produces a specimen; EASL already makes residual viable lesion after embolisation an indication for resection. Additional cautions Additional cautions The systematic review of embolisation reported malignant transformation as one of its outcomes of interest precisely because the question cannot be closed by an intervention that leaves the lesion in situ. Treating a possibly malignant lesion with an ablative modality converts a diagnostic problem into an unanswerable one. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not use imaging follow-up alone as the surveillance strategy for a beta-catenin-activated adenoma.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not use imaging follow-up alone as the surveillance strategy for a beta-catenin-activated adenoma. Why Why EASL's position is resection irrespective of size in any instance of proven beta-catenin mutation (evidence level II-3, grade of recommendation 2), and the review of the WHO 6th-edition classification states that beta-catenin exon 3 adenomas are resected or ablated whatever their size. The molecular support in small lesions is thin but points the same way: among women with adenomas under 5 cm, an at-risk molecular profile identified malignant transformation in 2 of 14 (14%) against 1 of 101 (1%) without it (P=0.007), and no HNF1A-inactivated adenoma under 5 cm in a woman transformed. Additional cautions Additional cautions Read the strength of that honestly: 2 transformations among 14 women is a hypothesis-generating subgroup, not a validated rule, and it is the only evidence offered anywhere for abandoning the size threshold in small lesions. The WHO-review statement is expert assertion with no cited cohort quantifying it. What is firm is the negative: no imaging protocol has been shown to detect transformation in an adenoma early, EASL itself says that identification of beta-catenin-activated adenoma and its distinction from carcinoma is not possible by any imaging technique, and alpha-fetoprotein does not exclude it. Surveillance of this subtype is surveillance for growth, not for transformation, and should be described to the patient as such. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Hepatocellular adenoma is not a standardised MELD exception — this is a non-standard review-board request at a recommended MMaT-3, and nothing about it is automatic.
text: Standard Evidence D Hepatocellular adenoma is not a standardised MELD exception — this is a non-standard review-board request at a recommended MMaT-3, and nothing about it is automatic. Indications Preferred when The local UTHealth Houston hepatic adenoma liver transplant protocol V3, policy review 21 September 2026, is the authority for this assessment and the page defers to it entirely. Its classification note is specific: the OPTN Board action of 9 June 2025, with guidance effective 1 July 2025, added recommended exception scores for non-standard transplant-oncology diagnoses but did not move hepatocellular adenoma into the standardised list in Policy 9.5.A to 9.5.I. Standard care remains risk-factor modification, observation, resection, embolisation or ablation, and transplantation requires multidisciplinary confirmation that those are unsafe, infeasible or inadequate. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not describe the score as guaranteed or standardised. The protocol notes that secondary literature stating hepatocellular adenoma has been moved into the standardised list is imprecise on that point, and requires re-verification against the live posting before committee adoption and before each submission. Extensions run on a roughly 90-day cycle under Policy 9.4.C with updated imaging, continued unresectability and continued transplant need; the automatic extension provision that applies to HCC candidates at a policy-assigned score does not extend to non-standard transplant-oncology requests. The protocol marks the cycle length and governing subsection VERIFY, and that verification has not been done here. Evidence & sources For context when a patient asks why thresholds differ between countries: EASL's position is only that transplantation is not recommended in multiple adenoma but might be considered in individuals with underlying liver disease (evidence level III, grade of recommendation 2), and the UK NHSBT Liver Advisory Group Fair Transplant Working Group published national guidance in 2025 assigning patients with benign liver tumours to four eligibility categories (A, B1, B2 and C). That guidance is a consensus document with no underlying cohort, it does not define how adenoma size, number, subtype or prior intervention map onto the categories in any form that can be audited, it makes no reference to beta-catenin or sonic hedgehog status, and its own working group concedes that categorisation still requires individual case review. Its detailed criteria have not been read into this page and should not be quoted from it. [PROTOCOL] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Name the qualifying route in the narrative, and record the CTNNB1 exon and codon where the route is molecular.
text: Standard Evidence D Name the qualifying route in the narrative, and record the CTNNB1 exon and codon where the route is molecular. Indications Preferred when The protocol's molecular route requires a documented CTNNB1 activating alteration with the exon and codon recorded. Exon 3 non-S45 alterations carry the strongest association with malignant transformation and satisfy the route directly. S45 exon 3 and exon 7/8 alterations do not by themselves: the selection committee must document an additional risk feature — size, growth, haemorrhage, a syndromic driver, or diagnostic uncertainty about transformation — and record why the expected benefit justifies deceased-donor organ use and lifelong immunosuppression. Where the molecular result is an immunohistochemical surrogate rather than sequencing, the narrative must state which, and its limitations. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The exon split is an institutional refinement that restricts rather than expands the route, and the protocol requires it to be described as such, because the OPTN guidance itself does not distinguish exon categories. But do not read the split as a statement that S45 is low risk. In 220 adenomas, 373 carcinomas and 17 borderline lesions, S45 was a weak activator in benign tumours yet was identified at similar frequency in mutated adenomas and in mutated carcinomas, and in most carcinomas with a weakly activating mutation a second hit raised activity — duplication of the mutant allele in 60% of those, a second more active CTNNB1 mutation in 33%, or APC inactivation. Chromosome 3p gain or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity was present in 37% of 27 weakly mutated carcinomas against 3% of 75 moderately or highly mutated ones, and in none of 34 adenomas. Those authors concluded that adenomas with S45, and with all high or moderate mutants, should be identified by precise immunohistochemical criteria or by mutation screening — and that S45 gives an intense but heterogeneous glutamine synthetase pattern that is difficult to recognise, so identifying it reliably needs sequencing. Evidence & sources This is the clearest live disagreement on the page. The protocol's restriction is defensible as organ stewardship; it is not defensible as a claim about S45 biology. See the limited-evidence section and approval item 8. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Record the full disease dataset before the request, and keep imaging on the 90-day cycle while listed.
text: Standard Evidence D Record the full disease dataset before the request, and keep imaging on the 90-day cycle while listed. Indications Preferred when The protocol §6 dataset: adenoma number, dominant and aggregate dimensions, bilobar distribution, growth trajectory, haemorrhage and rupture history, symptoms, prior resections, embolisations and ablations, and pathology and molecular results; full blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, INR, liver tests, and alpha-fetoprotein where transformation remains a concern. While listed, multiphasic MRI or CT every 3 months, aligned with the 90-day exception-extension cycle, shortened for active growth, haemorrhage or suspicion of transformation. Immediate re-review for a new rupture, major haemorrhage, rapid growth, suspected carcinoma, or a newly feasible non-transplant option. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid None of these intervals is a risk threshold derived from outcome data; the 3-month interval exists because the extension cycle is 90 days. Do not present it to the patient as a biologically determined surveillance schedule. And the trigger that most often gets missed is the last one: a newly feasible non-transplant option is a reason to come off the pathway. Evidence & sources Post-transplant, for adenoma without malignant transformation the protocol mandates standard transplant clinical and graft surveillance with no routine tumour imaging; where occult or known transformation is found, risk-adapted surveillance with chest and abdominal cross-sectional imaging every 3 to 6 months for the first 2 years and then 6-monthly through year 5, individualised to stage and pathology. Syndrome-specific follow-up continues for glycogen storage disease and for shunt manifestations that transplantation does not fully correct. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Syndromic routePROTOCOL REGISTRY Adenoma in the presence of glycogen storage disease or Abernethy malformation / congenital portosystemic shunt. The protocol requires the narrative to explain separately why transplantation is medically necessary.
text: Syndromic route Evidence D PROTOCOL REGISTRY Adenoma in the presence of glycogen storage disease or Abernethy malformation / congenital portosystemic shunt. The protocol requires the narrative to explain separately why transplantation is medically necessary. Indications Preferred when The patient in whom the underlying disease rather than the adenoma is driving the need, and in whom shunt closure or metabolic optimisation has been assessed and found insufficient. Glycogen storage disease accounted for 53.1% of the 99 published cases in the systematic review and for 16 of the 49 European registry transplants for adenomatosis. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid A syndrome is not an indication. Metabolic genetics for glycogen storage disease and vascular expertise for Abernethy malformation are required at the table, and feasibility of shunt closure must be assessed first. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Molecular routePROTOCOL REGISTRY Unresectable adenoma with a documented CTNNB1 activating alteration, with the exon and codon recorded.
text: Molecular route Evidence D PROTOCOL REGISTRY Unresectable adenoma with a documented CTNNB1 activating alteration, with the exon and codon recorded. Indications Preferred when An unresectable exon 3 non-S45 lesion, which satisfies the route directly on the strength of an odds ratio of 9.3 (95% CI 4.4-20.0) for malignant transformation and the highly activating mutant classification. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Not available on an S45 or exon 7/8 result alone — those need a documented additional risk feature and a recorded justification. And not available on an immunohistochemical surrogate presented as sequencing; state which was done. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Adenomatosis routePROTOCOL REGISTRY Unresectable liver adenomatosis with more than 10 adenomas AND at least one of: recurrent or life-threatening haemorrhage or prior rupture not controllable by embolisation or targeted resection; confirmed or strongly suspected malignant transformation, or a high-risk molecular subtype; a syndromic driver or underlying liver disease independently threatening hepatic function; or documented progression despite an adequate, individualized risk-factor-modification period, with the trajectory and reason for intervention recorded with liver-directed options exhausted or contraindicated.
text: Adenomatosis route Evidence D PROTOCOL REGISTRY Unresectable liver adenomatosis with more than 10 adenomas AND at least one of: recurrent or life-threatening haemorrhage or prior rupture not controllable by embolisation or targeted resection; confirmed or strongly suspected malignant transformation, or a high-risk molecular subtype; a syndromic driver or underlying liver disease independently threatening hepatic function; or documented progression despite an adequate, individualized risk-factor-modification period, with the trajectory and reason for intervention recorded with liver-directed options exhausted or contraindicated. Indications Preferred when The patient with recurrent uncontrollable bleeding, or with transformation, in a liver that resection cannot clear. The route is deliberately conjunctive and the protocol requires dominant lesion size, growth trajectory, complication history and molecular status to be recorded. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Lesion number alone does not qualify. The European registry experience is the cautionary case: of 49 transplants performed for adenomatosis, 17 patients had HCC before or at transplantation; the detailed tables record 12 positive explants, four negative explants after prior HCC and one unavailable result, there were three operative deaths and five retransplantations, and three patients developed carcinoma recurrence, all fatal — so the series documents important mortality and graft harms, but comparison with a separate conservatively managed cohort cannot estimate transplant-attributable mortality or net benefit. The same series found that the report assembled 49 confirmed cases using registry and additional centre ascertainment; the difference between 64 initially mentioned and 49 confirmed does not establish 15 miscoded cases, which is a warning about every registry-based figure in this disease. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Progressive or complicated routePROTOCOL REGISTRY All three of: unresectable after expert hepatobiliary surgical review; unresponsive to appropriate non-operative management, such as observation after stopping oestrogen-containing medications, efforts to maintain an ideal body weight, transarterial embolisation or thermal ablation; and progressive or complicated by haemorrhage, rupture or malignant transformation, with lesion size documented.
text: Progressive or complicated route Evidence D PROTOCOL REGISTRY All three of: unresectable after expert hepatobiliary surgical review; unresponsive to appropriate non-operative management, such as observation after stopping oestrogen-containing medications, efforts to maintain an ideal body weight, transarterial embolisation or thermal ablation; and progressive or complicated by haemorrhage, rupture or malignant transformation, with lesion size documented. Indications Preferred when The patient who has genuinely exhausted the liver-directed options. The protocol allows that an unsafe or clearly futile intervention need not be performed solely to demonstrate failure, provided the reason is documented — which is the clause that keeps this route honest rather than performative. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not invoke it before embolisation and ablation have been assessed by the services that perform them, with the assessment in writing. Elective embolisation avoided surgery in 41 of 49 patients (84%) in one systematic review and reduced median diameter from 76 to 48 mm in a 59-patient multicentre series, so exhausted has to mean assessed and rejected, not untried — but present the other half too, because the patient will ask: 34% of embolised patients still needed surgery, 10% had a grade D complication, one patient died three months after emergency TAE for haemorrhagic shock, following aspiration pneumonia; causal attribution was uncertain, and symptoms decreased from 34/59 (58%) to 22/59 (37%), without a statistically significant difference (P=.134); long-term benefit remains uncertain. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

59-patient multicentre series: median diameter fell from 76 to 48 mm after embolisation

lead: Treat living donation and donor-source ethics review as part of this conversation, not an afterthought.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Treat living donation and donor-source ethics review as part of this conversation, not an afterthought. Indications Preferred when A young patient with benign disease and a willing related donor is exactly the scenario in which living donation is raised. The protocol requires deceased- or living-donor transplantation to comply with current OPTN allocation requirements and institutional donor-source ethics review. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let the availability of a living donor substitute for the selection decision. The question of whether this patient should be transplanted at all is answered before the question of where the graft comes from, and the registry outcomes that make this indication look safe come overwhelmingly from deceased-donor transplantation. Evidence & sources No tumour-specific immunosuppression regimen is established for benign adenoma, and the protocol directs standard institutional operative and immunosuppression protocols. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not list a patient whose disease is safely resectable with an adequate remnant.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not list a patient whose disease is safely resectable with an adequate remnant. Why Why Resect. This is a named exclusion in the local protocol and it is the commonest reason an adenoma case should not reach the review board. Additional cautions Additional cautions EASL does not recommend transplantation in multiple adenoma, and the 122-patient surgical series concluded explicitly that because complications were unrelated to lesion number, patients with multiple adenomas do not need liver transplantation. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not list a stable low-risk adenoma that is responding to hormone withdrawal or weight intervention.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not list a stable low-risk adenoma that is responding to hormone withdrawal or weight intervention. Why Why Keep modifying the risk factors and keep imaging. The protocol names this as an exclusion unless another explicit guidance route is independently met and transplantation is separately justified. Additional cautions Additional cautions 58.5% of adenomas over 5 cm fell below 5 cm at a median 104 weeks with no documented complication, and 69% shrank after oral contraceptives were stopped. A patient on that trajectory is not a transplant candidate, and listing resets nothing about the underlying driver. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not transplant on a suspicion of carcinoma that a biopsy could have settled.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not transplant on a suspicion of carcinoma that a biopsy could have settled. Why Why Where histology is obtainable, obtain it. The protocol's non-standard malignant-transformation route requires histologic confirmation precisely because imaging cannot classify these lesions in a non-at-risk liver. Additional cautions Additional cautions In the European registry series, 17 of 49 patients had HCC before or at transplantation; Tables 3–4 record 12 positive explants, four negative after prior HCC and one unavailable result from patients transplanted for adenomatosis, despite suspected or proven carcinoma being the dominant indication; the authors' own conclusion was that the decision should rely on morphological data and histological evidence of malignant transformation. A substantial fraction of those grafts went to patients whose explant did not confirm the indication. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Answer the at-risk question first, because it decides which diagnostic criteria you are permitted to use for the rest of the workup.
text: Standard Evidence B Answer the at-risk question first, because it decides which diagnostic criteria you are permitted to use for the rest of the workup. Indications Preferred when Every incidental liver lesion, before the next scan is ordered. The LI-RADS at-risk population is cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B, and current or prior HCC including adult transplant candidates. AASLD 2023 and EASL 2025 both build their diagnostic algorithms on that same population and both use the LI-RADS lexicon; EASL 2025 states that LI-RADS should be preferred over its own 2018 algorithm because of the LR-M and LR-TIV categories, while noting the two perform similarly for HCC (LoE 3, strong recommendation). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let the referral's wording settle this. 'Known liver disease' on a request form is not the same as cirrhosis, and MASLD without cirrhosis is not an at-risk liver under either guideline. Evidence & sources Record the aetiology and how cirrhosis was established — histology, imaging, elastography, platelet count, or clinical decompensation. The at-risk answer is the single most consequential line in the report. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: In an at-risk liver, categorise the observation with CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 and put the category in the report — but read the category as a probability derived from retrospective high-prevalence cohorts, not as a measurement.
text: Standard Evidence C In an at-risk liver, categorise the observation with CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 and put the category in the report — but read the category as a probability derived from retrospective high-prevalence cohorts, not as a measurement. Indications Preferred when Every observation in an at-risk liver. In a systematic review of 17 retrospective studies, 2,760 patients and 3,556 observations, the pooled proportions confirmed as HCC and as any malignancy were 94% (95% CI 92-96) and 97% (95-99) for LR-5, 74% (67-80) and 80% (75-85) for LR-4, 38% (31-45) and 40% (31-50) for LR-3, 13% (8-22) and 14% (9-21) for LR-2, and 36% (26-48) and 93% (87-97) for LR-M; no malignancy was found in LR-1. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Three things undercut those figures. All 17 studies were retrospective and observation selection was the commonest high-risk domain, through verification bias and case-control design, so the LR-3 and LR-4 figures are probably inflated relative to an unselected incidental population; the authors themselves call the LR-2 estimate provisional and at high risk of bias while still recommending that LR-2 management be reconsidered, and this page does not inherit that recommendation. The 2022 individual-patient-data meta-analysis of 5,364 observations from 32 studies then shows the major features are not equivalent: nonperipheral washout carried an odds ratio of 13.2 (95% CI 9.0-19.2) and nonrim arterial hyperenhancement 10.3 (6.7-15.6), enhancing capsule only 2.4 (1.7-3.5), and threshold growth was not associated with HCC at all, OR 1.6 (0.8-3.4) — a result the same paper reports a second time as 1.6 (0.7-3.6), p=0.07. Evidence & sources The agreement figures matter as much as the probabilities. Interreader agreement for arterial hyperenhancement and washout is excellent, kappa 0.84-0.87, but agreement on the category that actually drives management is fair for CEUS (kappa 0.30-0.39), fair to substantial for MRI (0.35-0.61) and substantial for CT (0.79), and intermodality agreement is kappa 0.33-0.39 between CT and MRI and 0.22 between MRI and CEUS. A category is not a stable property of the lesion. See the quick reference for the v2018 table. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Systematic review, 17 retrospective studies: pooled HCC/any malignancy LR-5 94/97%, LR-4 74/80%, LR-3 38/40%, LR-2 13/14%, LR-M 36/93%; none in LR-1 All 17 studies retrospective; verification bias likely inflates LR-3/LR-4

IPD meta-analysis, HCC OR: nonperipheral washout 13.2 (95% CI 9.0–19.2), nonrim APHE 10.3 (6.7–15.6), capsule 2.4 (1.7–3.5); threshold growth 1.6 (0.8–3.4), NS Growth OR also reported as 1.6 (0.7–3.6), p=0.07, in the same paper

lead: Outside the HCC at-risk population, imaging criteria cannot establish HCC. An unresolved solid lesion requires tissue.
text: Standard Evidence B Outside the HCC at-risk population, imaging criteria cannot establish HCC. An unresolved solid lesion requires tissue. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × In a liver that is not at risk, accept that no imaging criterion set exists that can call a lesion hepatocellular carcinoma — EASL 2025 says so explicitly, and the consequence is that an unresolved solid lesion here needs tissue, not another category. Indications Preferred when The young patient, the patient with no liver disease, and the patient with MASLD and no cirrhosis. EASL 2025: the non-invasive criteria should only be applied to patients with cirrhosis, chronic HBV infection or a history of HCC, and in other patients the diagnosis of HCC should be confirmed by biopsy (LoE 1, strong recommendation). The guideline gives its own reason — the pre-test probability in these populations has not been precisely established. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not apply a LI-RADS category outside the at-risk population and then act on it. The number means nothing there, and it will be read as though it did. Evidence & sources This does not mean every solid lesion in a normal liver needs a needle. Most are haemangioma, focal fat or focal nodular hyperplasia and are resolved on this page at decision points 4 and 5. It means that an unresolved solid lesion in a normal liver cannot be declared malignant or benign by imaging category alone. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Where cirrhosis is suspected but not established, say so in those words and treat the pathway as undetermined rather than guessing in either direction.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Where cirrhosis is suspected but not established, say so in those words and treat the pathway as undetermined rather than guessing in either direction. Indications Preferred when Advanced fibrosis on elastography without decompensation, a nodular liver contour without portal hypertension, long-standing alcohol use with normal synthetic function. Name the uncertainty, get the hepatology opinion, and decide the pathway once. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not default to the at-risk pathway because it feels safer. It is not neutral: it licenses a treat-without-tissue decision for LR-5, and in a non-cirrhotic liver that decision has no evidence behind it.

lead: Vascular liver disorder: use a separate benign-liver-tumor multidisciplinary assessment, outside this pathway’s two arms.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Vascular liver disorder: use a separate benign-liver-tumor multidisciplinary assessment, outside this pathway’s two arms. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × In a liver with a vascular disorder — Budd-Chiari, chronic portal vein occlusion, obliterative portal venopathy, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia, cardiac congestion — treat the case as its own category and get it to a benign-liver-tumour multidisciplinary review rather than through either arm of this assessment. Indications Preferred when These livers generate multiple arterially hyperenhancing benign nodules — in Budd-Chiari syndrome, imaging displays hepatic nodules in 60-80% of patients, usually under 4 cm, frequently more than ten, hypervascular and disseminated, with no pathognomonic CT or MRI pattern — and LI-RADS specifically excludes cirrhosis caused by vascular disorders and by congenital hepatic fibrosis from its population. EASL's vascular-liver-disease guideline is the document that governs them, and it states plainly that characterisation of these nodules cannot rely on the HCC criteria validated in cirrhosis. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not categorise a hyperenhancing nodule in a Budd-Chiari liver as LR-4 or LR-5 and act on it, and do not treat benignity as settled either: cumulative HCC incidence in Budd-Chiari syndrome is about 4% at a median 5 years. Note what the guideline does not give you — it reports how often these nodules occur in patients known to have vascular disease, and never the inverse probability a radiologist actually faces, which is the chance of underlying vascular disease given multiple hypervascular nodules in a non-cirrhotic liver. The five biopsy triggers it suggests (three or fewer nodules, a nodule 3 cm or larger, heterogeneity or venous-phase washout, change across two studies, rising alpha-fetoprotein) come from one cited source with no sensitivity or specificity, in the same paragraph that says the only formal recommendation is multidisciplinary surveillance. Evidence & sources Two provenance warnings. First, the EASL vascular-liver guidance this page quotes is the 2015 document, built on the agenda of a single 2012 conference with a PubMed-only search and committee opinion where evidence was absent; it has been superseded by a 2026 EASL edition that this page has not obtained, so every statement sourced to it here is provisional and must be re-checked against the new edition before clinical use. Second, the entity the 2015 guideline calls idiopathic non-cirrhotic portal hypertension has been redefined by the 2026 multisociety consensus as porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder or non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis, and nodular regenerative hyperplasia is now a major histological criterion for that disorder rather than a benign nodular tumour to reassure a patient about. Grade D on purpose: this is a scope rule drawn from documents that grade their own evidence as committee opinion. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not use a LI-RADS category outside the at-risk population, and do not write one into a report for a patient who has no risk factor.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not use a LI-RADS category outside the at-risk population, and do not write one into a report for a patient who has no risk factor. Why Why Describe the findings in the lexicon — arterial hyperenhancement, washout, capsule — without assigning a category, and route by what the lesion looks like. Additional cautions Additional cautions A category assigned outside its population is the commonest way a benign adenoma or a metastasis gets treated as HCC. lead: Do not start a workup before the chart has been read.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not start a workup before the chart has been read. Why Why Risk factors for chronic liver disease, prior cancer, oestrogen and androgen exposure, metabolic syndrome, foreign travel and dysentery, constitutional symptoms, and baseline liver tests all change the differential before any scan is added. EASL's benign-tumour guideline puts the history and the baseline bloods ahead of the contrast study for exactly this reason. Additional cautions Additional cautions Ordering the next scan without the history is how a patient ends up with three studies and no diagnosis. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Characterize an indeterminate liver lesion in a patient with known extrahepatic cancer using a test chosen for the lesion size, initial modality and clinical question; contrast MRI is often appropriate.
text: Standard Evidence C Characterize an indeterminate liver lesion in a patient with known extrahepatic cancer using a test chosen for the lesion size, initial modality and clinical question; contrast MRI is often appropriate. Indications Preferred when Use the scenario-specific ACR guidance. For a lesion <1 cm first seen on ultrasound in a patient with known cancer, contrast MRI is the only test rated usually appropriate in that variant. For a lesion first seen on limited CT or MRI, contrast MRI and multiphase CT may both be appropriate; the initial test and clinical context matter. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The 2010 meta-analysis concerns untreated colorectal-cancer staging. Its subcentimetre advantage for MRI does not restrict MRI to small lesions, and a nonsignificant comparison at ≥10 mm does not prove equivalence. Gadoxetate and gadobenate were not represented sufficiently to support a claim that modern liver-specific contrast agents provide no benefit. Evidence & sources Two cautions on transporting those numbers. They come from treatment-naive patients being staged for a known colorectal primary, where prevalence is high; the paper reports no predictive values at all, and after chemotherapy steatosis and sinusoidal injury degrade detection on every modality. And the figure that matters for a sub-centimetre lesion cuts against reassurance: the test being ordered to characterise it misses two metastases in five at that size. The same paper publishes two incompatible sets of per-patient sensitivities — 83.6, 88.2 and 94.1% in the abstract and Table 4, and 81.2, 93.4 and 94.2% in its own summary box — and does not reconcile them. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Treat a sub-centimetre lesion in a cancer patient as probably benign but explicitly unresolved, and say which of the two it is in the report.
text: Standard Evidence C Treat a sub-centimetre lesion in a cancer patient as probably benign but explicitly unresolved, and say which of the two it is in the report. Indications Preferred when Every small lesion reported in a patient under oncological surveillance. In 2,978 cancer patients who had both an initial and a follow-up abdominal CT at one cancer centre, a small hepatic lesion was mentioned in the radiology report of 378 (12.7%); 44 of the 378 (11.6%) grew and were counted metastatic, 303 (80.2%) were stable over a mean 25.6 months, and 31 (8.2%) were stable for under 6 months and left indeterminate. The rate varied by primary: metastatic in 3 of 76 (4%) with lymphoma, 8 of 57 (14%) with colorectal cancer and 14 of 63 (22%) with breast cancer. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not quote 11.6% as the malignant rate without saying it is the most favourable of three analyses the authors ran. Counting all 31 indeterminates as malignant gives 19.8%, and splitting them evenly gives 15.7% — nearly one in five at the top end. Benignity was defined as not growing on the same test, with no histology in any case, and requiring a second CT at the same institution conditions the cohort on surviving and staying in follow-up, which preferentially removes the patients whose lesions would have grown. The ACR algorithm's rule for this patient is a new sub-centimetre lesion in a high-risk liver gets MRI at 3 to 6 months — a deliberate interval, not a discharge. Evidence & sources Number and size pull in different directions in the two series and neither is decisive. In the cancer-centre cohort, solitary and multiple lesions did not differ significantly (metastatic in 9.8% against 14.0%, p>0.05), and nor did the presence of extrahepatic metastases (36% against 25.7%, p>0.05); the study was underpowered for both and reports no power calculation. In the older 1,454-examination CT series, the gradient by number was steep — 5% of patients with one small lesion progressed against 76% of those with five or more — but lesion number there is confounded with tumour burden and stage. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Route by the primary's name, not by the word metastasis: a known colorectal primary is the CRLM pathway from here, and a known neuroendocrine primary is the NELM pathway from here.
text: Standard Evidence D Route by the primary's name, not by the word metastasis: a known colorectal primary is the CRLM pathway from here, and a known neuroendocrine primary is the NELM pathway from here. Indications Preferred when As soon as the primary is established. Those pathways carry their own resectability, sequencing and biopsy rules, and the most common way to damage a patient at this assessment is to start a generic workup instead of entering the right pathway. For colorectal disease in particular the consequence is concrete — biopsy of a resectable colorectal liver metastasis is contraindicated on that pathway, and this page's job is to get the patient there before anyone books one. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not route on an assumption. A liver lesion in a patient with a treated colorectal cancer is not automatically a colorectal metastasis, and the local master workup CPG requires colorectal origin to be confirmed and the primary's status verified before the CRLM pathway is entered. Evidence & sources The local Master Workup and Staging CPG sets the minimum staging bundle for each destination: CT or MRI of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus FDG PET-CT, CEA, colonoscopy and molecular profile for CRLM; somatostatin-receptor imaging, cross-sectional staging and central review of grade and Ki-67 for neuroendocrine liver metastases. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: FDG PET-CT The ACR Appropriateness Criteria rate FDG PET-CT usually appropriate in exactly one of eight variants — an indeterminate liver lesion larger than 1 cm found on non-contrast or single-phase CT or non-contrast MRI in a patient with a known extrahepatic malignancy. For the same lesion found on ultrasound it drops to may be appropriate, and it is rated usually not appropriate in a normal liver on the explicit basis that there is no relevant literature supporting its use there.
text: FDG PET-CT Evidence C The ACR Appropriateness Criteria rate FDG PET-CT usually appropriate in exactly one of eight variants — an indeterminate liver lesion larger than 1 cm found on non-contrast or single-phase CT or non-contrast MRI in a patient with a known extrahepatic malignancy. For the same lesion found on ultrasound it drops to may be appropriate, and it is rated usually not appropriate in a normal liver on the explicit basis that there is no relevant literature supporting its use there. Indications Preferred when The larger indeterminate lesion where the question is whether disease is confined to the liver, since the test answers a staging question the liver MRI cannot. Per-patient sensitivity for colorectal liver metastases was 94.1% (95% CI 91.6-95.9), higher than CT at 83.6% (66.9-92.8), p=0.025. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not use it to clear a small lesion. Per-lesion sensitivity was 81.4% (66.5-90.6), statistically indistinguishable from MRI at 80.3%, and the FDG PET/CT data specifically amounted to one per-lesion data set, far too few for comparison with other modalities. A negative PET does not characterise a sub-centimetre lesion. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Somatostatin-receptor PET The functional study for a suspected or known neuroendocrine primary, and the one the local master workup CPG names in the minimum staging bundle for neuroendocrine liver metastases. The ACR Appropriateness Criteria rate DOTATATE PET-CT may be appropriate for an indeterminate lesion larger than 1 cm in a patient with a known extrahepatic malignancy, and usually not appropriate in a normal liver.
text: Somatostatin-receptor PET Evidence C The functional study for a suspected or known neuroendocrine primary, and the one the local master workup CPG names in the minimum staging bundle for neuroendocrine liver metastases. The ACR Appropriateness Criteria rate DOTATATE PET-CT may be appropriate for an indeterminate lesion larger than 1 cm in a patient with a known extrahepatic malignancy, and usually not appropriate in a normal liver. Indications Preferred when A hypervascular, often multiple lesion set in a patient with flushing, diarrhoea, a known small-bowel or pancreatic primary, or a previously resected neuroendocrine tumour — which is the NELM pathway from here. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not substitute it for cross-sectional liver imaging; it answers receptor status and whole-body distribution, not resectability. And do not read the appropriateness rating as evidence — the criteria dismiss it in the normal-liver variants on the stated ground that no relevant literature exists, which is absence of evidence converted into a numerical rating. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Where the lesion is the only evidence of metastatic disease and would change the treatment plan from curative to palliative, treat that as a multidisciplinary question rather than a radiological one.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Where the lesion is the only evidence of metastatic disease and would change the treatment plan from curative to palliative, treat that as a multidisciplinary question rather than a radiological one. Indications Preferred when The patient about to have a curative resection of a colorectal, breast or lung primary, in whom one sub-centimetre liver lesion appeared on the staging CT. The 80.2% stability rate in the 2,978-patient series is a reason to re-image rather than to abandon the operation — bearing in mind that the same series puts the malignant rate anywhere from 11.6% to 19.8% depending on how its 31 indeterminate lesions are counted. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let an 8 mm indeterminate lesion cancel a curative operation without the board seeing it, and do not let it be ignored either. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not biopsy a liver lesion in a patient whose colorectal liver metastases are resectable.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not biopsy a liver lesion in a patient whose colorectal liver metastases are resectable. Why Why Confirm colorectal origin from the primary's pathology and operate. This is the position of the CRLM pathway and the reason routing by name matters at this assessment. Additional cautions Additional cautions In 598 patients resected with curative intent for colorectal metastases, 90 had been biopsied before referral and 17 of those 90 (19%) had needle-track deposits; 4-year overall survival after resection was 32.5% (standard error 5.5) against 46.7% (2.8) in the 508 not biopsied, p=0.008, an absolute difference of 14.2% (95% CI 2.0-26.4). Read the limits honestly, because they are larger than the paper admits. Every biopsy happened at a referring hospital, so the exposure is really a referral route and a marker of diagnostic uncertainty; the biopsied group had synchronous colorectal and hepatic disease in 61% against 26%, p<0.001, the single largest prognostic imbalance in the paper, dismissed without any multivariable model; the claimed independent effect of biopsy is reported as 'p=0.001, Student's t test' with no hazard ratio, confidence interval or covariate list; and conditioning the denominator on having reached a curative resection removes the patients whom dissemination had already made inoperable. The 19% track-deposit rate is the harder number, though open biopsy at laparotomy produced as many deposits as a percutaneous needle (22% against 15%, p=0.398), which suggests some of what was counted is laparotomy implantation rather than needle tracking. Evidence & sources The counterweight is real and also thin: in the same series, inadvertent resection for benign disease without preoperative histology occurred in 6 of 514 (1.2%) — two haemangiomas and four cysts — in a specialist unit with intraoperative ultrasound. Six events in expert hands is not a rate that transports to a general surgical setting. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Resected cohort (n=598): needle-track deposits in 17 of 90 biopsied (19%); 4-y OS 32.5% vs 46.7%, biopsied vs not biopsied, p=0.008 Synchronous disease 61% vs 26%, biopsied vs not; no multivariable model; resected-only

lead: Do not characterise a liver lesion on a scan that was not acquired to characterise it.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not characterise a liver lesion on a scan that was not acquired to characterise it. Why Why If the study was a single-phase staging CT, say the lesion is unresolved and name the test that would resolve it. Additional cautions Additional cautions The ACR algorithm's benign and suspicious feature lists assume adequate phases and adequate dose; it warns that assessing small liver lesions is challenging when aggressive dose-reduction has been used, particularly in high-risk patients. lead: A homogeneous, sharply marginated, non-enhancing lesion of water attenuation is a simple cyst: say so, give no follow-up interval, and discharge it.
text: Standard Evidence C A homogeneous, sharply marginated, non-enhancing lesion of water attenuation is a simple cyst: say so, give no follow-up interval, and discharge it. Indications Preferred when The commonest cystic finding by a wide margin. The ACR criteria are -10 to +20 Hounsfield units, homogeneous and sharply marginated, with no enhancement, wall thickening, nodularity or septa; enhancement should be 20 HU or less after contrast. In 45,319 ultrasound examinations at one German university hospital, hepatic cysts were the second commonest of five pre-specified benign findings at 2,631 (5.81%), mean size 22.3 mm, solitary in 62.8%, rising monotonically with age from 0.8% in those under 30. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Three cautions, two of them the white paper's own. Pseudoenhancement can make a genuinely benign cyst measure above 20 HU, so a single high reading is not proof of a solid component — and the same document concedes that in a lesion under 1 cm an accurate density measurement may not be attainable at all, which is precisely where most of the caseload sits. Cystic metastases exist, with ovarian cancer and gastrointestinal stromal tumours the named examples, so low density alone is not definitive in a patient with cancer. And the 5.81% figure is a prevalence of one benign finding in a hospital ultrasound population, not a probability that this cyst is benign: metastases, HCC, abscess and biliary hamartoma were never counted in that study's numerator. Evidence & sources Discharge rule: a simple cyst in a patient with no known malignancy needs no imaging follow-up, no size threshold and no interval. Symptoms from a large cyst are a surgical question, not a diagnostic one. The 20 HU threshold itself is a consensus number — the 2010 white paper gave it as 'up to about 20 HU' and invoked radiologists' discretion to resolve the pseudoenhancement problem — so it is a reporting convention, not a derived cut-point. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Multiple small non-enhancing cystic foci that do not communicate with the biliary tree on MRCP are biliary hamartomas — von Meyenburg complexes — and the diagnosis is made on MRI, not by counting them on CT.
text: Standard Evidence D Multiple small non-enhancing cystic foci that do not communicate with the biliary tree on MRCP are biliary hamartomas — von Meyenburg complexes — and the diagnosis is made on MRI, not by counting them on CT. Indications Preferred when The patient whose CT was read as multiple sub-centimetre hypodensities, which is the point at which a cancer patient gets labelled metastatic by mistake. These are ductal plate malformations, usually 1 to 15 mm and mostly under 5 mm, subcapsular and periportal, and they are common: a single autopsy series of 2,843 cases gives a prevalence of about 5.6%, and in 95 forensic autopsies of men aged 35 to 69 with targeted sectioning, bile duct tumours were the most frequent finding at 26 cases (27%), mean diameter 1.3 mm, multiple in 46% of the men. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The published difficulty is exactly the one that matters here. The review states that on CT these lesions cannot be distinguished from small metastases in a patient with a known primary, and that ultrasound is non-specific. It then recommends heavily T2-weighted MRI with MR cholangiography as the discriminator without reporting a single sensitivity, specificity or predictive value for any of those features, and concedes that fibrous-predominant complexes may not be visible on MRI at all. If the clinical setting is a known primary and the foci are not uniform, resolve it on MRI and accept that the resolution is a judgement, not a measurement. Evidence & sources Grade D, downgraded from C after the full-text read: the entire imaging recommendation rests on a narrative single-centre review with no search strategy, no accuracy data and no interobserver agreement, and the autopsy prevalence is one secondhand figure from one 1996 series. Discharge rule with a caveat: no surveillance interval is established, and the pathway discharges them. About 35 cases of cholangiocarcinoma arising in von Meyenburg complexes have been reported in roughly fifty years, against a carrier prevalence of about 5.6% — so the absolute risk is vanishingly small and has never been computed. See the limited-evidence section. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: A rim-enhancing collection in a febrile patient is an abscess until proved otherwise: take cultures, start antibiotics, and drain it with a catheter rather than a needle.
text: Standard Evidence B A rim-enhancing collection in a febrile patient is an abscess until proved otherwise: take cultures, start antibiotics, and drain it with a catheter rather than a needle. Indications Preferred when Fever, rigors, right upper quadrant pain and a raised white count with a cystic-looking lesion. In a meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials and 1,425 adults, percutaneous catheter drainage gave a higher clinical success rate than percutaneous needle aspiration, odds ratio 4.12 (95% CI 2.01-8.45), p<0.001. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Carry four limits with that odds ratio. The abscess size subgroup that matters most is the one that fails: in the 5-10 cm stratum, which is 8 of the 12 trials and the commonest clinical scenario, the confidence interval crossed the line of no effect, and only the >5 cm and >10 cm strata — three trials between them — excluded it; the paper's abstract nonetheless reports that the subgroups 'confirmed the consistency of this benefit', which is true of the direction of point estimates and not of significance. Nine of the 12 trials were Indian and 8 enrolled mixed amoebic-predominant abscesses, so pyogenic abscess is represented by 3 trials and 212 patients with no pyogenic-only pooled estimate reported. 'Clinical treatment success' is never defined, and the authors name varying definitions as a likely source of the 56% heterogeneity, so the pooled effect is an odds ratio on an undefined composite. And the safety claim is not equivalence: the complication odds ratio of 1.02 comes from 7 of the 12 trials with a 95% interval of 0.30-3.50, which permits a 70% reduction or a 3.5-fold increase. Evidence & sources Treat the odds ratio as a direction, not a threshold, and note that the pooled comparison does not identify a size below which a single aspiration is sufficient. A necrotic metastasis and a necrotic cholangiocarcinoma can both look like an abscess, and an abscess can be the first sign of an occult cancer — see the alternative column. The ACR incidental-findings algorithm explicitly does not cover hepatic infection, so nothing on this assessment comes from it. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Meta-analysis, 12 RCTs (n=1,425): clinical success catheter drainage vs needle aspiration OR 4.12 (95% CI 2.01–8.45), p<0.001 5–10 cm stratum (8 of 12 trials) CI crossed no effect; success undefined; mostly amoebic

lead: After a pyogenic liver abscess with no obvious source, investigate for an occult cancer rather than treating the abscess as the whole diagnosis.
text: Reasonable Evidence C After a pyogenic liver abscess with no obvious source, investigate for an occult cancer rather than treating the abscess as the whole diagnosis. Indications Preferred when Every cryptogenic pyogenic abscess, and particularly a diabetic patient. In a Taiwanese claims cohort of 1,257 patients with ICD-coded pyogenic liver abscess and no prior cancer, followed a median 3.33 years, the standardised incidence ratio against national rates was 3.83 (95% CI 3.30-4.42) for all cancers, 7.87 (5.94-10.21) for liver cancer, 34.58 (21.67-52.36) for biliary tract cancer and 5.27 (3.76-7.18) for colorectal cancer. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Read the time course and the denominator before acting on those ratios. The highest ratios all fell in the first 90 days to one year — all cancers 360.82 (278.46-459.91), biliary tract 1,153 (694-1,801) — which cannot be a biological effect of an abscess; it is the result of imaging and endoscoping a patient intensively, and in some cases the cancer caused the abscess or was the abscess. Several of those ratios are built on expected counts of 0.01 to 0.02 cases and are numerically meaningless however many decimal places they carry. The comparison is to the general Taiwanese population adjusted for age and sex only, in a cohort that was 47.6% diabetic and 7.8% cirrhotic; cirrhosis alone moves the liver-cancer ratio from 4.21 to 59.77, so the unstratified 7.87 is a confounded average, and no matched internal comparator was constructed although the same database could have supplied one. Exposure is two or more appearances of one ICD-9 code with no imaging, culture or clinical validation. The only estimate consistent with a genuine late effect is the all-cancer ratio beyond 5 years, 1.52 (1.09-2.05). Evidence & sources The practical inference is to complete the search now, not to enrol the patient in long-term surveillance — and the inference runs the opposite way from how this cohort is usually cited: it is evidence that a lesion called an abscess may be a cancer, not that an abscess will become one. What 'the search' consists of is a local decision: cross-sectional imaging is already done, and the cohort gives no yield estimate, no modality and no stratification, so whether every cryptogenic abscess gets a colonoscopy is not settled by it. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Claims cohort, 1,257 patients, median 3.33 y: SIR vs national rates, all cancers 3.83 (95% CI 3.30–4.42), biliary tract 34.58 (21.67–52.36), colorectal 5.27 (3.76–7.18) Highest ratios in first 90 days to one year (detection); age/sex-adjusted only; ICD-coded

lead: A cystic lesion with septations, mural nodularity or an enhancing component is a surgical lesion — get it to MRI and to a hepatobiliary surgeon, and plan for resection rather than drainage.
text: Reasonable Evidence D A cystic lesion with septations, mural nodularity or an enhancing component is a surgical lesion — get it to MRI and to a hepatobiliary surgeon, and plan for resection rather than drainage. Indications Preferred when The multilocular cyst, the cyst with an internal nodule, the cyst that has grown. Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver is the entity being excluded, it carries malignant potential, and the operation is complete resection with negative margins. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not aspirate or fenestrate it. The published series are small, selected and worse than they first appear — in one report of six resected intrahepatic biliary cystadenomas from a single Karachi pathology file over seven years, every case had been operated on under a preoperative impression of simple or hydatid cyst, sizes ranged 5.5 to 14.0 cm, and recurrence occurred in three of the five patients in whom any follow-up was available, two patients having been lost, one of them after a recurrence was already documented. Margins could not be assessed in at least three of the six because the specimens arrived opened or in pieces, so the claim that recurrence follows incomplete excision is inferred rather than shown; no dysplasia or malignancy was found in any of the six, and the 20% malignant-transformation figure the series invokes to justify radical resection is a single citation with no denominator. The authors attribute their own recurrence rate partly to limited local hepatobiliary surgical expertise. Six cases is not an evidence base; it is a warning about what the misdiagnosis costs. Evidence & sources Grade D on purpose. There is no comparative evidence for resection over observation in a radiologically suspected mucinous cystic neoplasm, no study establishes how often a septated cystic liver lesion is one, and the septation sign itself is contradicted by the series' own figure legend, which records one case as having no internal septations and reads that as favouring cystadenoma. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Single-centre series of six resected cystadenomas: all misread pre-op as simple or hydatid cyst; size 5.5–14.0 cm; recurrence in three of five followed Margins unassessable in at least three; no dysplasia or malignancy in any of the six

lead: Where the history includes relevant exposure, consider cystic echinococcosis and stage it on imaging before touching it.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Where the history includes relevant exposure, consider cystic echinococcosis and stage it on imaging before touching it. Indications Preferred when Foreign travel or residence in an endemic area, sheep or dog contact, a cyst with daughter cysts, detached membranes or a calcified wall. The WHO Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis consensus is an image-based, stage-specific approach grouping cysts as active (CE1, CE2), transitional (CE3) and inactive (CE4, CE5), and it recommends strongly that an imaging-based classification system be used; the four options it sets out are percutaneous treatment, surgery, anti-infective drug treatment, or watch and wait. Puncture, aspiration, injection and re-aspiration with mandatory albendazole cover is first-line for CE1 and CE3a cysts larger than 5 cm, and is contraindicated for CE2, CE3b, CE4 and CE5. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not aspirate a suspected hydatid cyst as though it were a simple cyst or an abscess, and do not treat an unclassified cyst at all until its parasitic nature is proven. The stage decides the option, and the stage is a subjective ultrasound judgement for which the consensus reports no interobserver agreement, while noting that calcification — the most objective feature — is unreliable for viability and occurs at every stage. The consensus states that percutaneous treatment should only be undertaken by experienced operators with resuscitation drugs and a surgical back-up team, but never states an anaphylaxis rate, and gives no sensitivity or specificity for any test in the document, including the two sequential serological assays it requires. Evidence & sources Grade D, downgraded from C after the full-text read. Ten of the eleven graded recommendations in this consensus are Strength B, Quality of Evidence III — the category for expert opinion and descriptive studies — the search was English-language Medline only and closed in 2008, consensus was reached by email with no voting or agreement threshold, and the watch-and-wait strategy for inactive cysts is described by the authors themselves as deserving formal evaluation. Serology supports but does not establish the diagnosis, and a negative test does not exclude it. Note also that the AASLD liver biopsy paper states that careful aspiration of these lesions with a 19-gauge needle can be undertaken, with none of the precautions this consensus requires; where the two conflict, follow the echinococcosis consensus. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not put a needle into a cystic liver lesion that has a septum, a mural nodule or an enhancing wall.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not put a needle into a cystic liver lesion that has a septum, a mural nodule or an enhancing wall. Why Why Image it properly, discuss it, and resect it if it is a mucinous cystic neoplasm. Additional cautions Additional cautions Aspiration neither excludes the diagnosis nor treats it, and incomplete removal is the recognised cause of recurrence and malignant transformation in the reported series. lead: Do not give a simple cyst a surveillance interval.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not give a simple cyst a surveillance interval. Why Why Call it benign, state the criteria it meets, and stop. Additional cautions Additional cautions An interval attached to a definitively benign finding generates scans indefinitely and is the precise failure the ACR incidental-findings programme exists to prevent — the white paper's first two core recommendations are to forgo workup of lesions under 1 cm in low-risk patients and to forgo workup of lesions with distinctly benign features regardless of risk.
