lead: Restage with pancreas-protocol CT or MRI of the abdomen plus chest and pelvis CT after neoadjuvant therapy, and judge response on two of three metrics.
text: Standard Evidence D Restage with pancreas-protocol CT or MRI of the abdomen plus chest and pelvis CT after neoadjuvant therapy, and judge response on two of three metrics. Indications Preferred when Every patient at the end of neoadjuvant therapy. The three metrics are radiologic (RECIST change on high-quality triple-phase CT or contrast-enhanced MRI), biochemical (CA 19-9 or CEA, interpretable only if the baseline was elevated and liver function has normalised) and metabolic (FDG-PET SUV or metabolic tumour volume against a baseline treatment-naive avid scan). Where the metrics conflict — tumour smaller on CT but CA 19-9 rising — NCCN asks for a third metric and a board discussion, deciding on two of three. The biochemical metric is the one with the most supporting data: ESMO cites a pooled analysis of 17 studies and 2,242 patients in which a CA 19-9 fall of more than 50% or normalisation after neoadjuvant treatment was associated with better overall survival (P<0.0001). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not read mild increases in perivascular soft tissue as progression; NCCN states this alone does not represent progression, ESMO states that persistent perivascular soft tissue is not synonymous with residual tumour, and after neoadjuvant therapy solid contact is often replaced by hazy density or stranding. Evidence & sources Examples of an optimal response given by NCCN are CA 19-9 normalisation, or near-normalisation, or at least a 50% decrease, and a complete or near-complete metabolic response on PET. The degree of significance is explicitly left to the local treatment team, which makes it a local approval item. ESMO adds the relevant caveat about the radiologic metric: imaging performance for restaging after chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy is lower than in treatment-naive settings. The trials bear that out — pathologic and nodal response in PREOPANC-2 and NORPACT-1 moved substantially without survival moving at all. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Guideline-cited pooled analysis (ESMO; 17 studies, 2,242 pts): CA 19-9 fall >50% or normalisation after neoadjuvant therapy associated with better OS (P<0.0001) Secondary citation; interpretable only if baseline elevated and liver function normalised

lead: Operate 4 to 8 weeks after completing neoadjuvant therapy, and only where there is a high likelihood of achieving R0 while avoiding R2.
text: Standard Evidence C Operate 4 to 8 weeks after completing neoadjuvant therapy, and only where there is a high likelihood of achieving R0 while avoiding R2. Indications Preferred when The surgical principles NCCN sets for an anatomically advanced tumour that has responded are en bloc resection of the tumour and at-risk tissue to a negative margin, re-establishment of end-organ arterial inflow and venous outflow, restoration of gastrointestinal continuity, and biliary drainage. Much of this is assessed intraoperatively, because cross-sectional imaging distinguishes viable tumour from scar poorly. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not attempt a resection whose likely outcome is R2. And do not abandon one because the vessel contact looks unchanged — if there is no apparent shrinkage and no extrapancreatic progression, NCCN's instruction is that surgery should still be attempted.

lead: Venous (portal vein / SMV) resection and reconstructionEXPERTISE NCCN states venous resection of the portal/SMV axis is supported by evidence if complete tumour excision to R0 is technically feasible with reasonably limited risks.
text: Venous (portal vein / SMV) resection and reconstruction Evidence C EXPERTISE NCCN states venous resection of the portal/SMV axis is supported by evidence if complete tumour excision to R0 is technically feasible with reasonably limited risks. Indications Preferred when A responder whose only barrier to R0 is a reconstructable venous segment, at a centre that does these routinely, with suitable vessel proximal and distal to the involved site. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid It is associated with higher complexity, greater potential blood loss, increased postoperative morbidity and mortality, and a higher likelihood of a positive margin. A vein resection done to convert an R2 into an R1 is not a gain.

lead: Consolidative chemoradiation before surgeryEXPERTISE NCCN says consolidative chemoradiation may be considered after chemotherapy and before surgical resection where the response is significant, and may be considered where the response is minimal as an alternative to switching regimens.
text: Consolidative chemoradiation before surgery Evidence C EXPERTISE NCCN says consolidative chemoradiation may be considered after chemotherapy and before surgical resection where the response is significant, and may be considered where the response is minimal as an alternative to switching regimens. Indications Preferred when Where the board wants to improve the chance of a clear margin in a tumour whose anatomy makes R0 marginal. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Its role and necessity remain poorly defined. A021501 closed its radiotherapy arm early for futility on R0 rate in the first 30 evaluable patients (10 of 30 versus 17 of 30) and its arms are by design not comparable, so the descriptive difference in median overall survival (17.1 versus 29.8 months) cannot be read as harm from radiotherapy — but nothing in the trial supports adding it, and 15 of 55 patients allocated to it never received it. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Radiotherapy arm vs arm without: closed early for futility on R0, 10/30 vs 17/30; median OS 17.1 vs 29.8 mo, descriptive only Arms not comparable by design; 15 of 55 allocated never received it

lead: Arterial resection (hepatic artery, celiac axis, SMA)EXPERTISE NCCN restricts it to centres with proven experience in pancreatectomy with vascular resection and reconstruction, and to highly selected patients after extensive neoadjuvant therapy with objective responses.
text: Arterial resection (hepatic artery, celiac axis, SMA) Evidence D EXPERTISE NCCN restricts it to centres with proven experience in pancreatectomy with vascular resection and reconstruction, and to highly selected patients after extensive neoadjuvant therapy with objective responses. Indications Preferred when Almost nobody. Where it is contemplated, NCCN requires that the patient be counselled about the operative morbidity and mortality risk, the potential effect on quality of life, and that the long-term benefit — the chance of cure — is currently unknown. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid It is often part of a multivisceral resection with significantly greater morbidity and mortality. Do not offer it for a minimal response: NCCN's governing rule is that the more complex and risky the resection, the greater the objective response needed to justify it.

lead: Switch to a different regimen and reassess, rather than operating, where the response is minimal or there has been local progression without metastases.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Switch to a different regimen and reassess, rather than operating, where the response is minimal or there has been local progression without metastases. Indications Preferred when NCCN's response table: with a minimal response, resection is considered in selected tumours without or with limited vascular involvement and no significant increase in surgical risk, and otherwise a different neoadjuvant therapy is considered with reassessment after second-line chemotherapy. With local progression and no metastatic progression, switching regimen is recommended, and resection may then be considered if there is no further progression and R0 is technically feasible — for a tumour with vascular involvement, only after a significant response to the second regimen. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not interpret switch and reassess as indefinite therapy. Set the reassessment date when the switch is made.

lead: Where the response warrants resection but the operation is not technically feasible locally, get a second opinion at a centre with expertise in vascular resection.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Where the response warrants resection but the operation is not technically feasible locally, get a second opinion at a centre with expertise in vascular resection. Indications Preferred when NCCN recommends this explicitly at every response category in its table. It is the step most often skipped. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not record not resectable here as not resectable. [EXPERTISE]

lead: Do not abandon the operation because the degree of vessel contact has not changed.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not abandon the operation because the degree of vessel contact has not changed. Why Why Judge the response on the three metrics and the clinical picture — performance status, pain, satiety, weight and nutrition, diabetes control are all listed by NCCN as possible metrics of response. Additional cautions Additional cautions NCCN's significant-response row states that resection is recommended in the majority of cases independent of the degree of vascular involvement if R0 is technically feasible. Radiographic vascular contact after chemotherapy frequently represents fibrosis, imaging cannot tell the two apart, and ESMO states that imaging performance after chemotherapy is lower than in treatment-naive settings. Note also that less vascular work was needed after neoadjuvant therapy in the trials that counted it — concomitant venous resection in 14% versus 29% in NORPACT-1 (p=0.0034) and vascular resection in 16.5% versus 21.4% in the pooled analysis — so unchanged contact on the scan is a poor guide to what the operation will require. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: With vs without neoadjuvant therapy: concomitant venous resection 14% vs 29% (p=0.0034)
Pooled analysis, with vs without neoadjuvant therapy: vascular resection 16.5% vs 21.4%

lead: Do not operate for a minimal response when the operation required is an arterial resection.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not operate for a minimal response when the operation required is an arterial resection. Why Why Switch regimen, reassess, and only reconsider an arterial resection after a significant response. Additional cautions Additional cautions This inverts NCCN's rule that the risk of the operation sets the threshold for the response needed to justify it, and it is the combination with the worst morbidity and mortality on the page.

lead: Do not use the word unresectable for a patient who has not yet had systemic therapy.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not use the word unresectable for a patient who has not yet had systemic therapy. Why Why Borderline resectable is a treatment category, not a verdict. Say what the barrier to R0 is and what would have to change. Additional cautions Additional cautions A patient told at diagnosis that they are inoperable rarely gets re-asked the question, which is how a responder is lost.

lead: Standard lymphadenectomy, to the stations the International Study Group on Pancreatic Surgery names — extended lymphadenectomy gives no survival benefit.
text: Standard Evidence C Standard lymphadenectomy, to the stations the International Study Group on Pancreatic Surgery names — extended lymphadenectomy gives no survival benefit. Indications Preferred when For pancreatoduodenectomy the ISGPS consensus is to resect stations 5, 6, 8a, 12b1, 12b2, 12c, 13a, 13b, 14a, 14b, 17a and 17b, using Japanese Pancreas Society nomenclature. For cancers of the body and tail, removal of stations 10, 11 and 18 is standard. Lymphadenectomy also matters for adequate nodal staging, which drives the adjuvant discussion. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Extended lymphadenectomy — nodes along the left side of the SMA and around the celiac trunk, splenic artery or left gastric artery — showed no survival benefit over standard lymphadenectomy in the trials the consensus summarises and cannot be recommended. There was no level I evidence on the prognostic impact of positive para-aortic nodes. Evidence & sources Downgraded from B to C, and flagged for provenance: this consensus statement is cited from its abstract only. No new papers were obtained for this depot and the full text was not retrieved, so the station list and the no-benefit claim have not been checked against the published trials the consensus relies on, and neither has the strength of agreement behind either. ISGPS reached consensus on selectively removing suspected nodes outside the resection area for frozen section, but no consensus on whether to continue or terminate the resection when those nodes are positive — so that is a local decision made in advance, not in the room. Both pancreatic resection in a relatively fit patient and non-resectional palliative treatment were accepted as reasonable in that situation. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: R0 in this disease means more than 1 mm of clearance — report the distance in millimetres for every margin within 1.0 cm of tumour.
text: Standard Evidence D R0 in this disease means more than 1 mm of clearance — report the distance in millimetres for every margin within 1.0 cm of tumour. Indications Preferred when Every specimen. Per the current College of American Pathologists protocol, tumour at or within 1 mm of a resection margin constitutes a positive margin, and ESMO's 2023 guideline uses the same definition. NCCN asks for clearance reported with millimetre accuracy for all margins where tumour is within 1.0 cm, and with centimetre accuracy beyond that, so that the data accumulate for future analysis. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not present the 1 mm rule as established in pancreatic cancer. NCCN states that the recommendation is based primarily on extrapolation from data on rectal adenocarcinoma and that there is currently a lack of definitive evidence for what constitutes an adequate margin in pancreatic resection specimens. A standardised definition does not yet exist. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D on the full-text read: this is a threshold nobody derived. The single study that supplied the clinical argument for it, 163 consecutive pancreatoduodenectomies at one centre, answered its own question in the null — median survival 15.4 months (95% CI 11.3–18.2) for equivocal R1, tumour within 1 mm but not reaching the margin, against 12.6 months (9.2–14.3) for unequivocal R1, log-rank P=0.102 — and concluded the two should be treated as one category on the strength of a non-significant test. Equivocal R1 versus R0 was also non-significant (P=0.114), so the study cannot separate the intermediate group from either neighbour. R0 (n=35) gave median survival 25.4 months with a 95% CI of 10.5 to 40.8 months, and margin status did not survive multivariable adjustment (univariate HR 1.747, 1.117–2.734, P=0.015; adjusted HR 1.443, 0.896–2.324, P=0.132), where lymph node ratio, tumour size and adjuvant chemotherapy did. Only 27% of that cohort received adjuvant chemotherapy, in 1997–2007. The practical consequence matters more than the prognostic one: applying the rule moved the R1 rate at that centre from 44% to 79%, which means R0 rates are substantially a function of local pathology protocol and the R0 figures quoted across the trials on this page — PREOPANC 71% of resected, ESPAC5 14% to 23%, NORPACT-1 56% versus 39%, APACT 76% with no central pathology review — are not comparable with one another. The 16-versus-14-month and 35-month margin-clearance figures carried in the NCCN discussion text supplied to this page come from a different review, appear in a sentence that inverts them, and were not retrieved for this depot; confirm the direction against the published discussion before quoting them. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Dissect the specimen to a stated protocol — axial or bivalve — and accept that there is no single correct method.
text: Standard Evidence D Dissect the specimen to a stated protocol — axial or bivalve — and accept that there is no single correct method. Indications Preferred when Axial slicing, perpendicular to the long axis at regular intervals, preserves spatial relationships and is useful for radiologic-pathologic correlation. The bivalve method, bisecting along probes in the bile and pancreatic ducts, is better for localising small lesions near the ampulla or ducts and for assessing ductal involvement and margins. Knowing the clinically suspected lesion is what should pick the method. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid What is not optional is clear and accurate assessment of the margins, tumour size, and the relationship to pancreatic surfaces, margins, bile duct, main pancreatic duct and duodenum. Organs resected en bloc need serial sectioning to assess both direct extension and separate metastatic deposits, with at least one section demonstrating each. Evidence & sources In distal pancreatectomy, assess the peripancreatic soft-tissue surfaces and the pancreatic neck, document splenic vessel involvement and splenic invasion, and consider shaving and submitting the splenic artery and vein margins. Frozen section of the pancreatic neck is a recommended option. Direct tumour invasion of the spleen is pT3. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Send peritoneal washings whenever the abdomen is open, and act on a positive result.
text: Standard Evidence C Send peritoneal washings whenever the abdomen is open, and act on a positive result. Indications Preferred when At staging laparoscopy and at resection. Intraoperative ultrasound can be used as an adjunct to further evaluate the liver, the tumour and vascular involvement. The yield is real: in PREOPANC, 13 of the 28 patients allocated to neoadjuvant therapy who never started it were found metastatic at the mandatory staging laparoscopy. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Positive cytology is equivalent to M1 disease. If a resection has already been performed in such a patient, they are treated for M1 disease — so the result has to reach the oncologist, not sit in the chart. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: PREOPANC: 13 of 28 patients allocated to neoadjuvant therapy who never started it were metastatic at mandatory staging laparoscopy

lead: A written minimum annual volume for pancreatoduodenectomy at this centre, with a textbook-outcome audit behind it.
text: Reasonable Evidence D A written minimum annual volume for pancreatoduodenectomy at this centre, with a textbook-outcome audit behind it. Indications Preferred when NCCN's opening line in this guideline is that decisions about diagnosis, resectability and management should involve multidisciplinary consultation at a high-volume centre, and it repeats high-volume centre at the drainage, vascular resection, recurrence and gastric outlet decision points. A threshold that is written down makes the referral decision auditable. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The guideline never states a number, and no number here is evidence based. Volume-outcome relationships in pancreatic surgery are observational and consistent; the threshold itself is a governance choice. [EXPERTISE] Evidence & sources NCCN never states a number, and no number here is evidence based. Volume-outcome relationships in pancreatic surgery are observational and consistent; the threshold itself is a governance choice. The one randomised dataset in this depot that looked at it found centre volume associated with survival in a post hoc multivariable model (10 or more patients enrolled, HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61–0.98, P=.03, in PRODIGE-24's 77 hospitals) — a finding confounded with case mix, surgical quality, access to relapse therapy and country, and selected by a stepwise procedure with no multiplicity correction. Do not cite it as a derived threshold. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Post hoc multivariable, RCT dataset (77 hospitals): centre enrolling ≥10 patients associated with survival, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.61–0.98), P=.03 Confounded by case mix and country; stepwise selection, no multiplicity correction

lead: Resection of a local recurrence, in a carefully restaged patient, as part of a multimodal plan rather than as an isolated operation.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Resection of a local recurrence, in a carefully restaged patient, as part of a multimodal plan rather than as an isolated operation. Indications Preferred when In a pooled analysis of 55 patients from 19 studies who underwent pancreatectomy for recurrent pancreatic cancer, 1-, 3- and 5-year survival were 82.2%, 49.2% and 40.6%. NCCN asks for careful evaluation in a multidisciplinary clinic with detailed restaging, and a plan that may include neoadjuvant chemotherapy with or without radiotherapy and then resection. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Fifty-five patients across nineteen studies is a selected series of selected series. Chemoradiation can be considered for local recurrence if radiation was not given before, but NCCN notes limited data to support specific radiotherapy recommendations in this setting. Where there is metastatic disease with or without local recurrence, this is a systemic problem — see the metastatic assessment.

lead: Resection of limited pulmonary-only metastases after resection, in a selected patient.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Resection of limited pulmonary-only metastases after resection, in a selected patient. Indications Preferred when The lung is a common site of recurrence after pancreatic resection, and NCCN states resection may be considered for those with limited pulmonary-only metastases. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid NCCN also states that more data are needed before recommendations can be made about managing pulmonary metastases, so this is a case-by-case board decision and not a pathway.

lead: Extended lymphadenectomy.
text: Avoid Evidence C Extended lymphadenectomy. Why Why Standard lymphadenectomy to the ISGPS stations. Additional cautions Additional cautions Extending the dissection to the left side of the SMA and around the celiac trunk, splenic artery or left gastric artery showed no survival benefit in the trials the ISGPS consensus summarises, and the consensus is that extended lymphadenectomy cannot be recommended. The consensus statement is cited from its abstract only; the full text was not retrieved for this depot. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: A pathology report that says margins negative without millimetres.
text: Avoid Evidence D A pathology report that says margins negative without millimetres. Why Why Agree the reporting format with pathology once, in writing, including which margins are inked, which are shaved and which are taken perpendicular. Additional cautions Additional cautions Without millimetre clearance the adjuvant radiation discussion cannot be had, and the data NCCN asks the field to accumulate are not accumulated. The guideline's own argument is that if under 1 mm clearance proves to carry an unacceptably high local recurrence rate, then postoperative radiotherapy would deserve strong consideration in exactly those patients — which is unanswerable without the number.

lead: Attempting a resection whose likely outcome is R2.
text: Avoid Evidence C Attempting a resection whose likely outcome is R2. Why Why NCCN's instruction is that resection should only be attempted if there is a high likelihood of achieving R0 while avoiding an R2 resection. Additional cautions Additional cautions An R2 resection in this disease delivers the morbidity of a major pancreatectomy with none of the oncologic benefit, and it delays systemic therapy.

lead: mFOLFIRINOX for 24 weeks PRODIGE 24 / CCTG PA.6 (n=493) is the strongest adjuvant result in this disease and NCCN lists mFOLFIRINOX as a preferred adjuvant option for patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy. ESMO's 2023 guideline takes the same position for fit patients at [I, A], and recommends completing 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy at [I, A].
text: mFOLFIRINOX for 24 weeks Evidence A PRODIGE 24 / CCTG PA.6 (n=493) is the strongest adjuvant result in this disease and NCCN lists mFOLFIRINOX as a preferred adjuvant option for patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy. ESMO's 2023 guideline takes the same position for fit patients at [I, A], and recommends completing 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy at [I, A]. Indications Preferred when A recovered patient with good performance status. On the mature 5-year analysis, median disease-free survival 21.4 months (95% CI 17.5–26.7) versus 12.8 months (11.6–15.2) against gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.66 (0.54–0.82), P<.001; median overall survival 53.5 months (43.5–58.4) versus 35.5 months (30.1–40.3), hazard ratio 0.68 (0.54–0.85), P=.001; 5-year overall survival 43.2% (36.5–49.7) versus 31.4% (25.5–37.5); metastasis-free survival 29.4 versus 17.7 months. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The toxicity is the whole of the trade-off and must be said out loud: grade 3 or 4 adverse events in 180 of 237 (75.9%) versus 128 of 242 (52.9%), with the one treatment-related death in the gemcitabine arm. Delivery was poor — 67.2% completed all 12 cycles, only 33.6% achieved a relative dose intensity of 0.80 or more, and 55% discontinued oxaliplatin at least once — so adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX in practice means a dose-attenuated, incompletely delivered regimen. Eligibility was restricted to age 18 to 79, no symptomatic heart failure or coronary artery disease, WHO performance status 0 or 1, full recovery from surgery, a clear postoperative scan and a postoperative CA 19-9 of 180 U/mL or less, so these figures do not transfer to a patient who has not recovered from a pancreatoduodenectomy, and they are not the expectation for resected PDAC in general. Evidence & sources Three things the 3-year report did not show. The effect attenuated with mature data, as early stopping for benefit at 91.8% of expected events predicts: the disease-free survival hazard ratio moved from 0.58 to 0.66, overall survival from 0.64 to 0.68, and the much-quoted 54.4-month median to 53.5 months. Most patients in both arms still relapse — 5-year disease-free survival differs by only 7.1 points (26.1% versus 19.0%) against 11.8 points at 5-year overall survival, so part of the survival gain accrues after relapse. And post-relapse survival was numerically worse in the mFOLFIRINOX arm (13.1 versus 15.0 months), with first-relapse chemotherapy given to 107/160 (66.9%) versus 151/182 (83.0%) relapsers. Among the 151 control-arm patients receiving chemotherapy, 112 (74.2%) received FOLFIRINOX; that is 61.5% of all 182 control-arm relapsers — so the trial partly measures the benefit of giving the regimen early rather than at relapse. In the 101 patients aged 70 or older (20.5% of the trial) the disease-free survival estimate was imprecise (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.53–1.39). The mature overall-survival HR was 0.90 (0.56–1.46), with interaction P=.32; this does not demonstrate loss of benefit with age. Assess fitness and tolerance individually. Quality of life was never collected. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

mFOLFIRINOX vs gemcitabine, 5-y analysis: median DFS 21.4 vs 12.8 mo, HR 0.66 (0.54–0.82); median OS 53.5 vs 35.5 mo, HR 0.68 (0.54–0.85); 5-y OS 43.2 vs 31.4% Selected trial population; age ≥70 DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.53–1.39), not significant

lead: Gemcitabine with capecitabine NCCN's other preferred adjuvant option for patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy, and ESMO's alternative for patients over 75, ECOG performance status 2 or a contraindication to mFOLFIRINOX at [I, B]. ESPAC-4 (n=730 analysed) gave median overall survival 28.0 months (95% CI 23.5–31.5) versus 25.5 months (22.7–27.9) against gemcitabine monotherapy, hazard ratio 0.82 (0.68–0.98), stratified log-rank p=0.032.
text: Gemcitabine with capecitabine Evidence A NCCN's other preferred adjuvant option for patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy, and ESMO's alternative for patients over 75, ECOG performance status 2 or a contraindication to mFOLFIRINOX at [I, B]. ESPAC-4 (n=730 analysed) gave median overall survival 28.0 months (95% CI 23.5–31.5) versus 25.5 months (22.7–27.9) against gemcitabine monotherapy, hazard ratio 0.82 (0.68–0.98), stratified log-rank p=0.032. Indications Preferred when A patient who wants adjuvant treatment but cannot take a triplet — poorer performance status, neuropathy, a slow recovery, or a preference against irinotecan and oxaliplatin. Its population is the least selected in the adjuvant literature: WHO performance status up to 2, R1 margins allowed and no ceiling on postoperative CA 19-9, These selection differences prevent ranking regimens by cross-trial survival medians. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not offer it as equivalent to mFOLFIRINOX, and state both halves. The comparator was gemcitabine alone, the two combinations have never been compared directly, and the difference in medians against gemcitabine was 2.5 months. The relapse-free survival endpoint was negative (13.9 versus 13.1 months, hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.73–1.02, p=0.082), the trial was stopped and published early at 458 of 480 target deaths on a signal of efficacy, and the widely quoted 5-year figures (28.8% versus 16.3%) are estimates extrapolated well past the bulk of the data at 43.2 months median follow-up. Grade 3–4 events occurred in 226 of 359 (63%) versus 196 of 366 (54%), with neutropenia 38% versus 24% and hand-foot syndrome 7% versus 0%, and 169 of 364 combination patients (46%) did not complete all six cycles. Evidence & sources The benefit sits almost entirely in the R0 subgroup — median overall survival 39.5 months (32.0–58.0) versus 27.9 months (23.8–34.6) in R0, against 23.7 months (20.7–27.1) versus 23.0 months (21.6–26.2) in R1 — reported as a trend test across four groups with no treatment-by-margin interaction test, and 60% of the trial was R1. Reading ESPAC-4 as support for adjuvant gemcitabine with capecitabine specifically in a margin-positive patient is reading something the data do not show. The trial is also the source of the prognostic weight of postoperative CA 19-9: 113 of 662 patients (17%) had a value above 92.5 kU/L with median survival 13.1 months (10.8–16.2) against 29.6 months (26.6–32.1) below it, which is the selection step CONKO-001 and PRODIGE-24 applied and ESPAC-4 did not. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Gemcitabine–capecitabine vs gemcitabine, n=730: median OS 28.0 vs 25.5 mo, HR 0.82 (0.68–0.98), p=0.032; RFS negative, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.73–1.02) Stopped early at 458 of 480 deaths; benefit mainly R0 (60% R1); never compared with mFOLFIRINOX

lead: Gemcitabine alone An other recommended option in NCCN. CONKO-001 (n=354 analysed) established that adjuvant therapy beats observation: median disease-free survival 13.4 months (95% CI 11.6–15.3) versus 6.7 months (6.0–7.5), HR 0.55 (0.44–0.69), P<.001, and final median overall survival 22.8 versus 20.2 months, hazard ratio 0.76 (0.61–0.95), P=.01, with 5-year survival 20.7% (14.7–26.6) versus 10.4% (5.9–15.0) and 10-year 12.2% versus 7.7% at a median follow-up of 136 months.
text: Gemcitabine alone Evidence B An other recommended option in NCCN. CONKO-001 (n=354 analysed) established that adjuvant therapy beats observation: median disease-free survival 13.4 months (95% CI 11.6–15.3) versus 6.7 months (6.0–7.5), HR 0.55 (0.44–0.69), P<.001, and final median overall survival 22.8 versus 20.2 months, hazard ratio 0.76 (0.61–0.95), P=.01, with 5-year survival 20.7% (14.7–26.6) versus 10.4% (5.9–15.0) and 10-year 12.2% versus 7.7% at a median follow-up of 136 months. Indications Preferred when A frail patient in whom the choice is between single-agent treatment and none. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The median overall survival gain over observation was 2.6 months; the durable difference is in the 5- and 10-year rates. Eligibility required postoperative CEA and CA 19-9 both below 2.5 times the upper limit of normal — about 92.5 kU/L for CA 19-9 — which ESPAC-4 later showed silently removes the 17% of resected patients whose median survival is 13.1 months, so the curves describe a favourably selected population. Evidence & sources Downgraded from A to B on the full-text read. Overall survival was a secondary endpoint that became significant only on the final of several analyses, nine years after the primary report, with no multiplicity adjustment reported for the repeated testing. The authors themselves note that because relapse was common in the first year and gemcitabine was standard therapy at relapse, the design is better read as immediate versus delayed gemcitabine than as chemotherapy versus none. The primary disease-free survival endpoint was assessed in part by abdominal ultrasound every 8 weeks with no central radiology review and recurrence dated from the first subjective symptom, in an open-label trial — which is why a 2.0-fold difference in median disease-free survival sits beside a 2.6-month median survival difference. Eighteen of 186 patients (10%) never started gemcitabine, mainly for postoperative complications, and only 62% completed all six cycles. Enrolment ran 1998 to 2004 across 88 centres with no central pathology review and no uniform margin definition, so neither its R1 rate nor its 20.2-month observation arm is a usable benchmark today. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Gemcitabine vs observation: primary DFS 13.4 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.55 (0.44–0.69), P<.001; final OS 22.8 vs 20.2 mo, HR 0.76 (0.61–0.95), P=.01 OS secondary, significant only at final analysis; excluded CA 19-9 ≥2.5× ULN

lead: A fluoropyrimidine alone NCCN lists fluorouracil with leucovorin and continuous-infusion fluorouracil as other recommended adjuvant options, and capecitabine monotherapy as a treatment option.
text: A fluoropyrimidine alone Evidence D NCCN lists fluorouracil with leucovorin and continuous-infusion fluorouracil as other recommended adjuvant options, and capecitabine monotherapy as a treatment option. Indications Preferred when Where gemcitabine is contraindicated or the patient will not tolerate it. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid No trial establishes a fluoropyrimidine alone as equivalent to the combinations above. The arms that support it sit inside ESPAC-1 and ESPAC-3, neither of which was retrieved or read in full for this depot; their medians (20.1 and 23.0 months) are in the same range as every other single-agent arm from that era, and NCCN notes scepticism about the efficacy of the fluorouracil and folinic acid regimens used in those trials.

lead: Restage before the first cycle — a proportion of patients have already relapsed.
text: Standard Evidence D Restage before the first cycle — a proportion of patients have already relapsed. Indications Preferred when Every patient. NCCN states it is important to evaluate for disease recurrence before initiating adjuvant therapy because of the risk of early relapse. A patient who has relapsed is on the metastatic assessment, not this one. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not start a 24-week adjuvant course on the assumption that the postoperative scan will be clean.

lead: Prioritise completing the course over starting it quickly.
text: Standard Evidence D Prioritise completing the course over starting it quickly. Indications Preferred when A retrospective analysis of ESPAC-3 found that completion of the six-course chemotherapy, but not the time to initiate it, was an independent prognostic factor for survival. NCCN's inference is that delaying until the patient has fully recovered from surgery may allow completion of the full course and improve outcomes. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid This is a retrospective analysis of a randomised trial, not a randomised comparison of timing, and it is vulnerable to the obvious confounder — patients who complete treatment are patients who were well enough to complete it. Do not use it to justify an open-ended delay. The same confounding appears in PRODIGE-24's own mature report, where completing all cycles predicted survival (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.49–0.84, P=.002; 5-year overall survival 41.9% versus 27.4%) in a landmark analysis while achieving a relative dose intensity of 0.80 or more did not (HR 1.01, 0.80–1.28, P=.93) — which is the clue that completion marks patient fitness rather than drug effect, and that pushing a patient through all 12 cycles is not what the finding supports. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D. The primary report for the ESPAC-3 analysis is carried only in the NCCN discussion text supplied to this page; it was not retrieved or read in full for this depot, so none of its figures has been checked. The PRODIGE-24 landmark analysis quoted above is post hoc, with variables selected by stepwise procedures and no multiplicity correction. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Post hoc landmark: completing all cycles vs not, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.49–0.84), 5-y OS 41.9% vs 27.4%; dose intensity ≥0.80 not predictive, HR 1.01 (0.80–1.28) Stepwise selection, no multiplicity correction; completion likely marks fitness

lead: Adjuvant nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine — only if both halves of APACT are stated.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Adjuvant nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine — only if both halves of APACT are stated. Indications Preferred when A patient who cannot take mFOLFIRINOX and in whom a taxane doublet is preferred to gemcitabine with capecitabine. At the 5-year cutoff, with 88% data maturity, median overall survival was 41.8 versus 37.7 months against gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.678–0.947), P=.0091, with 5-year overall survival 38% versus 31%. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid APACT (n=866) missed its primary endpoint: independently assessed disease-free survival 19.4 months (95% CI 16.62–21.91) versus 18.8 months (13.83–20.30), hazard ratio 0.88 (0.729–1.063), P=.18. The trial's own statement is that because the primary endpoint was not met, all other comparisons are descriptive, and the journal's relevance note calls it a negative phase 3 study that fails to change the standard of care. The overall survival figure comes from the third of three successive cutoffs, with the P value improving from .045 to .0232 to .0091 across December 2018, April 2020 and April 2021 with no prespecified plan for repeated testing and no multiplicity adjustment anywhere. Grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent events occurred in 371 of 429 (86%) versus 286 of 423 (68%), serious events in 41% versus 23%, and two treatment-emergent deaths occurred in each arm. Evidence & sources Downgraded from B to C. The unpriced cost is neurological: grade 3 or worse peripheral neuropathy in 15% of the combination arm and 0% of the gemcitabine arm, with 84% of those affected not improved to grade 1 or less at the primary cutoff and a median 195 days to improve by one grade — in a trial that collected no quality-of-life data at all. Only 287 of 432 patients completed six cycles against 310 of 434 on gemcitabine, 64% needed a dose reduction, and the population is the most selected in the adjuvant literature: CA 19-9 below 100 U/mL with a median of 13.6 U/mL, a clear screening scan, ECOG 0–1, and 1,226 patients screened to randomise 866, which is why the gemcitabine arm reached 37.7 months. The trial's most durable contribution has nothing to do with the regimen: in the same gemcitabine arm, blinded independent review gave a median disease-free survival of 18.8 months and the unblinded investigators gave 13.7 months, with 77% concordance and 48% to 51% of patients censored. Every other adjuvant trial on this page used unblinded investigator-assessed disease-free survival and reported 12.8 to 13.4 months, so disease-free survival differences in open-label adjuvant trials are partly a detection artefact. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Nab-paclitaxel–gemcitabine vs gemcitabine: primary endpoint missed, DFS 19.4 vs 18.8 mo, HR 0.88 (0.729–1.063), P=.18; OS 41.8 vs 37.7 mo, HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.678–0.947) OS descriptive only, from the third of three cutoffs with no multiplicity adjustment

lead: Consider adjuvant chemoradiation after chemotherapy in selected node-negative patients through multidisciplinary discussion; the overall RTOG 0848 result was negative.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Consider adjuvant chemoradiation after chemotherapy in selected node-negative patients through multidisciplinary discussion; the overall RTOG 0848 result was negative. Indications Preferred when RTOG 0848 randomized 354 patients without recurrence after five chemotherapy cycles. From this randomization, overall survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.96, 90% CI 0.79–1.18), nor was final-report disease-free survival (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.65–1.03; two-sided P=.089). Significant nodal-status interactions and favorable node-negative results support an individualized discussion, not routine treatment of every resected patient. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid None of the patients received FOLFIRINOX: 67% received gemcitabine alone, 28% gemcitabine/erlotinib and 5% other gemcitabine combinations. Benefit after modern chemotherapy is unestablished. Only ten patients were both node-negative and margin-positive, so margin-specific inference is inadequate. SBRT substitution is unestablished. Evidence & sources The final primary report is now available. Grade-3 toxicity was greater with chemoradiation (38% versus 19%); grade-4/5 toxicity did not significantly differ. The main clinical text, tables and figure captions were reviewed in the continuation; figure pixels, the separate supplement and protocol were not. The earlier abstract’s one-sided DFS formulation should not replace the final nonsignificant two-sided result. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Surveillance after resection — history and examination, CA 19-9 and contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis — offered with an explicit statement of what it is for.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Surveillance after resection — history and examination, CA 19-9 and contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis — offered with an explicit statement of what it is for. Indications Preferred when NCCN's stated rationale is consensus-based: earlier identification of recurrence may allow enrolment in investigational studies or other treatment. CA 19-9 is listed as category 2B. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Say what is known. A SEER-Medicare analysis showed no significant survival benefit for patients who received regular surveillance CT scans. There are no data that a rising tumour marker leads to earlier intervention and better outcomes, and no evidence that serial ctDNA monitoring improves outcomes. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D: the rationale is consensus and the only outcome data quoted are negative. The surveillance interval is a local decision on this page. The guideline footnote that defines it did not survive the machine extraction supplied to the programme, so no interval is quoted here; confirm it against the current published guideline before publication and record which version was used. [PAYER] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not start adjuvant therapy without restaging.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not start adjuvant therapy without restaging. Why Why Scan, then start. Additional cautions Additional cautions This is a sequence error rather than a judgement call: a patient with radiologic recurrence is on a different pathway and a different conversation.

lead: Do not present RTOG 0848 as establishing routine adjuvant chemoradiation benefit in node-positive disease.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not present RTOG 0848 as establishing routine adjuvant chemoradiation benefit in node-positive disease. Why Why Individualize radiation decisions with oncology and radiation oncology review, considering the systemic regimen, margins, nodal status, recovery, toxicity and patient preferences. Additional cautions Additional cautions The overall primary result was negative and the node-positive subgroup did not show benefit. A subgroup result does not establish a universal prohibition for every clinical context. The node-negative signal also requires caution after modern chemotherapy.

lead: Do not present adjuvant nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine as established.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not present adjuvant nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine as established. Why Why Where a doublet is needed, gemcitabine with capecitabine has a positive primary endpoint and NCCN's preferred label; nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine does not. Additional cautions Additional cautions APACT's blinded independently assessed primary endpoint was negative, hazard ratio 0.88 (0.729–1.063), P=.18, and the trial states that all other comparisons are therefore descriptive. The overall survival signal that followed came from the third of three successive data cutoffs with no prespecified repeated-testing plan, at the cost of 86% grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent events and 15% grade 3 or worse peripheral neuropathy against 0%, 84% of it unresolved at the primary cutoff, with no quality-of-life data. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: Nab-paclitaxel–gemcitabine: blinded independent primary endpoint negative (P=.18), other comparisons descriptive; grade ≥3 events 86%, grade ≥3 neuropathy 15% OS signal only at third of three cutoffs, no repeated-testing plan; no QoL data

lead: Multiagent induction chemotherapy if performance, biliary drainage and nutrition permit; schedule reassessment at treatment start.
text: Standard Evidence D Multiagent induction chemotherapy if performance, biliary drainage and nutrition permit; schedule reassessment at treatment start. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × Multiagent induction chemotherapy for a patient with adequate performance status, good biliary drainage and adequate nutritional intake — with the reassessment date set when it starts. Indications Preferred when ECOG 0–1, or ECOG 2 with intermediate performance status, treated per the metastatic first-line options. In the patient-level meta-analysis of FOLFIRINOX in locally advanced disease (13 studies, 689 patients; 11 studies and 315 locally advanced patients with survival data), pooled median overall survival from the start of FOLFIRINOX was 24.2 months (95% CI 21.7–26.8) and median progression-free survival 15.0 months (13.8–16.3), with 1-year survival 79.5% and 2-year survival 50.1%. Resection followed in a pooled 25.9% (20.2–31.9), and 60 of the 81 resected patients with margin data were R0, pooled 78.4% (60.2–92.2). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Every one of those figures comes from single-arm cohorts with no randomised comparator, eleven of thirteen retrospective, and the pooled population is selected — median overall survival across the individual studies ranged from 10.0 to 32.7 months. Survival was measured from the start of FOLFIRINOX, so every patient had to survive diagnosis, staging, biliary drainage and the decision to treat before entering the analysis; LAP07's 7.7-month median for patients who progressed during induction shows how large the invisible group is. A pooled 63.5% of patients also received radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy (I² 90%, per-study range 31% to 100%), so the resection rate cannot be attributed to chemotherapy alone. The 78.4% R0 figure has a resected-only denominator — 81 of 325 patients, so it describes 19% of the cohort. Grade 3 or 4 events ran at 60.4 per 100 patients, and the report of no deaths attributed to FOLFIRINOX toxicity across 490 patients is a retrospective-records artefact rather than a safety finding. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D on the full-text read. Because patient-level data were pooled into a single Kaplan-Meier curve rather than meta-analysed, no I² or prediction interval is reported for overall survival at all, so the narrow 95% CI of 21.7 to 26.8 months reflects the number of patients and not the three-fold disagreement between studies. The pooled population is not one population: only three of thirteen studies enrolled exclusively locally advanced patients, seven had no formal resectability criteria, and none used staging laparoscopy. Across studies there was no correlation between overall survival and radiotherapy use (p=0.12), resection rate (p=0.39) or number of FOLFIRINOX cycles (p=0.95), so none of the obvious explanations for the 24.2-month figure can be shown to drive it. The comparator the authors offer, 6 to 13 months with gemcitabine, is a narrative historical range and not a synthesis. Their own conclusion is that these results need testing in a randomised controlled trial and that it remains unestablished which patients benefit from radiotherapy or resection afterwards. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Patient-level meta-analysis of single-arm cohorts: pooled median OS 24.2 mo (95% CI 21.7–26.8) from FOLFIRINOX start, PFS 15.0 mo (13.8–16.3); resection 25.9% (20.2–31.9) Eleven of thirteen retrospective; study medians 10.0 to 32.7 mo; 63.5% also had radiotherapy

lead: Re-ask the resectability question on biological response, not on the label the patient arrived with.
text: Standard Evidence D Re-ask the resectability question on biological response, not on the label the patient arrived with. Indications Preferred when NCCN states the term locally advanced should only be used at initial diagnosis, that locally advanced does not imply unresectable tumour, and that once neoadjuvant therapy has been delivered the criteria for resection should be based on the biological response. Where there is a response, a second opinion at a centre with expertise in vascular resection and reconstruction is recommended even if the patient is considered technically unresectable locally. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not let the second opinion be the step that is skipped because the first assessment was done by the person who would have to do the operation. Evidence & sources The response assessment and the resection criteria are those in the borderline resectable assessment — two of three metrics, and the rule that a riskier operation needs a bigger response to justify it. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Offer conversion surgery only where R0 is achievable, and only after an objective response.
text: Standard Evidence C Offer conversion surgery only where R0 is achievable, and only after an objective response. Indications Preferred when A responder in whom en bloc resection to a negative margin, re-established arterial inflow and venous outflow, gastrointestinal continuity and biliary drainage are all achievable — assessed partly intraoperatively, because imaging distinguishes viable tumour from scar poorly. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Arterial resection in this group is the highest-risk operation on the page and NCCN restricts it to specialist centres, highly selected patients, extensive neoadjuvant therapy and objective response, with explicit counselling that the chance of cure is unknown. Evidence & sources CONKO-007 gives the one randomised figure on how often conversion actually happens from this starting point, and the one randomised figure on what it costs. Of 336 patients randomised after 3 months of induction chemotherapy without progression, 62 of 169 in the chemoradiotherapy arm and 60 of 167 in the chemotherapy arm underwent surgery — 36% to 37%, with no difference between arms (P=.91) — and R0 was achieved in 43 of 169 (25%) and 30 of 167 (18%). Thirty-day postoperative mortality was 5 of 60 and 5 of 62, 8% in both arms. One operative death in twelve is the number to put in the consent conversation, and the trial's conclusion that conversion surgery did not increase postsurgical mortality means only that it did not differ between the randomised arms. Those 336 patients are also the 64% of enrolled patients who survived and did not progress through 3 months of chemotherapy: the 159 of 495 (32.1%) who progressed during induction had a median survival of 9 months with no 5-year survivors. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Chemoradiotherapy vs chemotherapy after induction: surgery 62/169 vs 60/167 (P=.91); R0 25% vs 18%; 30-day postoperative mortality 8% in both arms Randomised only the 64% not progressing through 3 months of induction

lead: Continue chemotherapy alone after induction LAP07 (449 enrolled, 442 eligible, 269 randomised after 4 months of gemcitabine-based induction without progression) found no overall survival difference between continuing chemotherapy and adding chemoradiotherapy: median overall survival from first randomisation 16.5 months (95% CI 14.5–18.5) with chemotherapy versus 15.2 months (13.9–17.3) with chemoradiotherapy, hazard ratio 1.03 (0.79–1.34), P=.83. The independent data monitoring committee stopped accrual when the interim analysis crossed the futility boundary at 221 deaths.
text: Continue chemotherapy alone after induction Evidence B LAP07 (449 enrolled, 442 eligible, 269 randomised after 4 months of gemcitabine-based induction without progression) found no overall survival difference between continuing chemotherapy and adding chemoradiotherapy: median overall survival from first randomisation 16.5 months (95% CI 14.5–18.5) with chemotherapy versus 15.2 months (13.9–17.3) with chemoradiotherapy, hazard ratio 1.03 (0.79–1.34), P=.83. The independent data monitoring committee stopped accrual when the interim analysis crossed the futility boundary at 221 deaths. Indications Preferred when The default after induction for a patient in whom the objective is survival rather than local control or conversion to resection. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid LAP07's chemotherapy backbone was gemcitabine with or without erlotinib, not FOLFIRINOX, so it does not test chemoradiotherapy after a modern triplet; CONKO-007 later did and was also null. Read the null carefully: the trial was stopped at its interim analysis for futility and that analysis was declared final, so it never reached its planned 392 deaths, and a confidence interval of 0.79 to 1.34 cannot exclude a clinically meaningful 20% benefit or harm — this is underpowered, not equivalent. Survival was measured from the first randomisation while the intervention was allocated at the second, so four months are common to both arms by construction and any true effect is diluted toward the null. Evidence & sources Two further qualifications. Despite a formal radiotherapy quality assurance programme, only 37 of 117 assessable plans (32%) were per protocol, 59 (50%) had minor and 21 (18%) major deviations, with survival 17.0 versus 13.4 months for per-protocol or minor versus major deviations (HR 1.43, 0.86–2.36, P=.17) — underpowered, but pointing in the harmful direction, so the trial cannot cleanly separate radiotherapy does not work from this radiotherapy was not delivered well enough. And curative-intent resection was achieved in only 18 of 442 patients (4%), 11 of them R0, with median overall survival 30.9 months in those 18 — gemcitabine-based induction almost never converts locally advanced disease. Erlotinib added to gemcitabine was useless and possibly harmful (11.9 versus 13.6 months, HR 1.19, 0.97–1.45, P=.09). Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Chemo vs chemoradiotherapy after induction: median OS 16.5 vs 15.2 mo, HR 1.03 (CI 0.79–1.34), P=.83; stopped for futility at interim Gemcitabine-based backbone; never reached planned 392 deaths; underpowered, not equivalence

lead: Chemoradiotherapy after induction, for local control or to raise the chance of R0 CONKO-007 (525 enrolled, 495 received induction — 402 FOLFIRINOX, 93 gemcitabine — and 336 randomised without progression at 3 months to continuing chemotherapy or to 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent gemcitabine) missed its primary endpoint: overall R0 resection rate 43 of 169 (25%) with chemoradiotherapy versus 30 of 167 (18%) with chemotherapy, P=.113. Among the patients who actually underwent surgery, R0 was 43 of 62 (69.4%) versus 30 of 60 (50.0%), P=.04, and the overall distribution of R0, R1, R2 and no resection also favoured it, P=.02. Median follow-up was 76 months.
text: Chemoradiotherapy after induction, for local control or to raise the chance of R0 Evidence C CONKO-007 (525 enrolled, 495 received induction — 402 FOLFIRINOX, 93 gemcitabine — and 336 randomised without progression at 3 months to continuing chemotherapy or to 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent gemcitabine) missed its primary endpoint: overall R0 resection rate 43 of 169 (25%) with chemoradiotherapy versus 30 of 167 (18%) with chemotherapy, P=.113. Among the patients who actually underwent surgery, R0 was 43 of 62 (69.4%) versus 30 of 60 (50.0%), P=.04, and the overall distribution of R0, R1, R2 and no resection also favoured it, P=.02. Median follow-up was 76 months. Indications Preferred when Where the board's objective is specifically local control, or a clear margin in a patient who has responded and in whom surgery is planned. The local-control effect is the most solid finding in either trial: in CONKO-007, locoregional recurrence as a first event at 5 years was 29.9% versus 40.9%, hazard ratio 0.41 (95% CI 0.227–0.746), P=.004, and all locoregional recurrence 46.9% versus 63.2%, hazard ratio 0.33 (0.206–0.530), P<.001, with distant metastasis identical (82.7% versus 84.7%, P=.52). LAP07 found the same direction (locoregional progression 32% versus 46%, P=.03) and a longer delay to reintroduction of any treatment (6.1 versus 3.7 months, P=.02). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Neither trial shows a survival benefit. CONKO-007 found no overall survival difference, hazard ratio 0.937 (95% CI 0.747–1.174), P=.57, with 151 deaths in each arm, and surgery was performed equally often in the two arms (P=.91). Its 5-year survival claim (10.1% versus 3.8%) is a tail comparison inside a null trial, reported without a p value and with standard errors of 2.5% and 1.8% on 8 and 4 patients at risk. The R0 advantage that did reach significance is conditional on reaching theatre, which was not randomised, and the authors state that physicians' knowledge of the R0 endpoint changed their behaviour — which is exactly the mechanism that produces an R0 difference in the operated subgroup and none in the randomised population. Surgery itself was strongly associated with longer survival (hazard ratio 0.525, 0.408–0.676, P<.001, median 19 versus 13 months), which in a non-randomised comparison of operated against non-operated patients is selection, not treatment effect. Evidence & sources Downgraded from B to C. The primary endpoint was changed mid-trial from overall survival to R0 resection rate, and the effect size for the new endpoint was calculated from unblinded interim data on 180 already-enrolled patients in which one arm's R0 rate was already nearly twice the other's — the sample size and the hypothesis were set using the result, and the trial still failed even that favourably chosen endpoint. Radiotherapy was never centrally reviewed, for stated financial reasons, in a trial whose whole question is whether radiotherapy helps; LAP07, which did review it, found 18% major deviations. Gemcitabine was the radiosensitiser, which the authors concede SCALOP suggests is inferior to capecitabine. Pathologic response did favour chemoradiotherapy (complete response 11 of 169 versus 1 of 167, P=.01; circumferential-margin-negative 28 of 33 versus 15 of 26, P=.04; ypN0 35 of 47 versus 23 of 45, P=.03). Thirty-day postoperative mortality was 8% in both arms. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

CRT vs chemo: locoregional progression 32% vs 46%, P=.03; time to reintroduction of any treatment 6.1 vs 3.7 mo, P=.02; no survival benefit 18% major radiotherapy deviations on central review

lead: Upfront chemoradiation or SBRT, without induction chemotherapyEXPERTISE NCCN permits upfront chemoradiation or SBRT in select patients with locally advanced disease. If disease progresses, the options are a clinical trial (preferred), systemic therapy, or chemoradiation or SBRT if radiation was not previously given and the primary site is the sole site of progression.
text: Upfront chemoradiation or SBRT, without induction chemotherapy Evidence D EXPERTISE NCCN permits upfront chemoradiation or SBRT in select patients with locally advanced disease. If disease progresses, the options are a clinical trial (preferred), systemic therapy, or chemoradiation or SBRT if radiation was not previously given and the primary site is the sole site of progression. Indications Preferred when A narrow group — a patient who cannot have multiagent chemotherapy, or in whom a local problem dominates. SBRT should be delivered at an experienced high-volume centre with image-guided radiotherapy, or in a trial. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not use it as the default first treatment for a fit locally advanced patient. Systemic therapy addresses the occult metastatic disease that is the usual cause of death in this group, and NCCN states further studies are needed before SBRT is recommended even in borderline resectable disease.

lead: Palliative and best supportive care, single-agent chemotherapy, or palliative radiotherapy, for a patient with poor performance status.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Palliative and best supportive care, single-agent chemotherapy, or palliative radiotherapy, for a patient with poor performance status. Indications Preferred when NCCN's options for ECOG 3 in locally advanced disease. Select patients with poor performance status may still benefit from single-agent chemotherapy or from targeted therapy based on molecular profiling. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not put a patient with ECOG 3 through a triplet to avoid the conversation. Survival benefit from systemic therapy in this disease is largely confined to patients with adequate performance status, good biliary drainage and adequate nutritional intake.

lead: Do not promise an operation at the start of induction therapy.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not promise an operation at the start of induction therapy. Why Why Say what the numbers are: about a quarter of locally advanced patients treated with FOLFIRINOX in the pooled single-arm data went on to resection, and in the one randomised trial starting from unresectable disease, 122 of 336 patients randomised after 3 months without progression reached theatre (36% to 37%) and 73 of 336 (22%) achieved R0 — with 30-day postoperative mortality of 8% in both arms. Of the 495 patients who started induction, 159 (32.1%) progressed before randomisation and had a median survival of 9 months. Additional cautions Additional cautions A patient who was told the chemotherapy was to shrink it so we can operate and who then does not reach an operation has been given the wrong frame for most of their remaining time. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not treat an unresectable label applied at diagnosis as final.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not treat an unresectable label applied at diagnosis as final. Why Why Re-ask on biological response, and send responders for a second opinion at a vascular-resection centre as NCCN recommends. Additional cautions Additional cautions This is the commonest way a potentially convertible patient is lost, and NCCN addresses it twice — in the instruction that the term should only be used at diagnosis, and in the explicit second-opinion recommendation.

lead: Do not offer radiotherapy as a survival-prolonging treatment in locally advanced disease.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not offer radiotherapy as a survival-prolonging treatment in locally advanced disease. Why Why Offer it, where it is offered, for local control or for margin quality in a patient heading to theatre, and say which. The local-control effect is real and randomised: locoregional recurrence hazard ratio 0.33 (95% CI 0.206–0.530), P<.001, in CONKO-007 and 32% versus 46% locoregional progression in LAP07. Additional cautions Additional cautions LAP07: hazard ratio 1.03 (0.79–1.34), P=.83, stopped early for futility at its interim analysis, which then became the final one. CONKO-007: hazard ratio 0.937 (0.747–1.174), P=.57, primary endpoint not met. Two randomised trials, both null for overall survival, and neither powered to exclude a clinically meaningful difference. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

CONKO-007, radiotherapy vs no radiotherapy: OS HR 0.937 (0.747–1.174), P=.57, primary endpoint not met; locoregional recurrence HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.206–0.530) Not powered to exclude a clinically meaningful OS difference

lead: FOLFIRINOX or mFOLFIRINOX PRODIGE 4 / ACCORD 11 (n=342, ECOG 0–1) established the triplet: median overall survival 11.1 months (95% CI 9.0–13.1) versus 6.8 months (5.5–7.6) against gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.57 (0.45–0.73), P<0.001, with median progression-free survival 6.4 months (5.5–7.2) versus 3.3 months (2.2–3.6), hazard ratio 0.47 (0.37–0.59), and an objective response rate of 31.6% versus 9.4%.
text: FOLFIRINOX or mFOLFIRINOX Evidence A PRODIGE 4 / ACCORD 11 (n=342, ECOG 0–1) established the triplet: median overall survival 11.1 months (95% CI 9.0–13.1) versus 6.8 months (5.5–7.6) against gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.57 (0.45–0.73), P<0.001, with median progression-free survival 6.4 months (5.5–7.2) versus 3.3 months (2.2–3.6), hazard ratio 0.47 (0.37–0.59), and an objective response rate of 31.6% versus 9.4%. Indications Preferred when A patient with ECOG 0–1, good biliary drainage and adequate nutritional intake. It is the regimen with the largest relative survival effect in this disease and the one whose population is best defined, and it is the only first-line triplet with quality-of-life data: definitive deterioration of global health status at 6 months in 31% versus 66%, hazard ratio 0.47 (0.30–0.70), P<0.001 — a time-to-event measure that a regimen delaying progression by 3.1 months will improve almost mechanically, so read it as consistent with the survival result rather than as independent evidence. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The toxicity excluded ECOG 2 patients for a reason: grade 3–4 neutropenia 45.7% versus 21.0% with filgrastim given to 42.5% versus 5.3%, febrile neutropenia 5.4%, diarrhoea 12.7% versus 1.8%, sensory neuropathy 9.0% versus 0%, with one treatment-related death in each arm. Do not give it to a jaundiced, undrained or malnourished patient — eligibility required bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the upper limit, age under 76, no cardiac disease and measurable disease, and NCCN's definition of good performance status for this disease includes biliary drainage and nutritional intake, not just the ECOG number. Evidence & sources Two things the trial does not establish. The regimen as delivered was already dose-attenuated (relative dose intensity 78% to 82%), which is part of why modified FOLFIRINOX performs similarly, so the trial does not show full-dose FOLFIRINOX is necessary. And 82.5% of FOLFIRINOX patients received gemcitabine afterwards while about half the gemcitabine patients received an oxaliplatin-based regimen, with post-second-line survival identical at 4.4 months in both arms — so the 4.3-month difference reflects first-line sequencing rather than anything unique to the four-drug combination. The phase 2 and phase 3 patients were pooled, with the trial continued only because the phase 2 response assessment was met. Nothing in the trial addresses adjuvant or neoadjuvant use, and PREOPANC-2 and NORPACT-1 show that extrapolation does not hold. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: NALIRIFOX NAPOLI 3 (n=770, 187 sites, 18 countries) gave median overall survival 11.1 months (95% CI 10.0–12.1) versus 9.2 months (8.3–10.6) with nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.83 (0.70–0.99), p=0.036, with median progression-free survival 7.4 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.69 (0.58–0.83), p<0.0001. NCCN recognises high-level evidence supporting NALIRIFOX over nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine.
text: NALIRIFOX Evidence A NAPOLI 3 (n=770, 187 sites, 18 countries) gave median overall survival 11.1 months (95% CI 10.0–12.1) versus 9.2 months (8.3–10.6) with nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.83 (0.70–0.99), p=0.036, with median progression-free survival 7.4 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.69 (0.58–0.83), p<0.0001. NCCN recognises high-level evidence supporting NALIRIFOX over nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine. Indications Preferred when The same population as FOLFIRINOX, where the liposomal-irinotecan schedule is preferred on toxicity or logistics. Eligibility was deliberately broad, with no upper age limit and no exclusion for clinical ascites, which is the one axis on which it is less selected than PRODIGE 4. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid NCCN states plainly that this regimen does not appear to have clear advantages compared with FOLFIRINOX or mFOLFIRINOX, and there is no randomised comparison between them — NALIRIFOX is FOLFIRINOX with liposomal irinotecan substituted and lower oxaliplatin, and PRODIGE 4's median was also 11.1 months. Grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent events occurred in 322 of 370 (87%) versus 326 of 379 (86%), with treatment-related deaths in 2% of each arm — this is not a gentler triplet, though grade 3–4 peripheral neuropathy was lower (3.2% versus 5.8%). The margin is narrow: the design required a hazard ratio below 0.844 at a final-analysis alpha of 0.048, and the point estimate sits just inside it. Evidence & sources The hierarchical testing sequence broke at step three — objective response rate 41.8% versus 36.2%, odds ratio 1.26 (0.95–1.69), p=0.11 — so the formal evidence chain stops after progression-free survival and every later p value, including the sensitivity analyses, is nominal. Follow-up was 16.1 months with asymmetric censoring in the winning arm (12% versus 2% still on treatment at cutoff), which is the configuration in which an early positive signal attenuates. Progression was assessed by investigators with no blinded central review, in an open-label trial. The sensitivity analysis censoring at subsequent therapy gives 15.1 versus 9.2 months, three times the primary result, and is informative censoring that should not be read as the true effect. Quality of life and cost were not reported, in a trial whose practical question is whether a proprietary liposomal formulation justifies its price; the sponsor participated in design, data collection, analysis, interpretation and manuscript approval. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

PRODIGE 4 FOLFIRINOX median OS 11.1 mo (separate trial); no randomised comparison of NALIRIFOX with FOLFIRINOX exists Separate trial, not head-to-head; NCCN sees no clear advantage over FOLFIRINOX

lead: Nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine MPACT (n=861) gave median overall survival 8.5 months (95% CI 7.89–9.53) versus 6.7 months (6.01–7.23) against gemcitabine alone, hazard ratio 0.72 (0.62–0.83), P<0.001, with 1-year survival 35% versus 22% and 2-year 9% versus 4%.
text: Nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine Evidence A MPACT (n=861) gave median overall survival 8.5 months (95% CI 7.89–9.53) versus 6.7 months (6.01–7.23) against gemcitabine alone, hazard ratio 0.72 (0.62–0.83), P<0.001, with 1-year survival 35% versus 22% and 2-year 9% versus 4%. Indications Preferred when A patient who cannot take a triplet — ECOG 2 equivalent, significant neuropathy, or a preference against a 46-hour infusion — but who is fit for a doublet. Its floor was a Karnofsky score of 70, so it admits frailer patients than PRODIGE 4, and the largest reductions in risk of death were in patients with worse disease. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid It was the comparator NALIRIFOX beat in NAPOLI 3, so do not choose it for a triplet-eligible patient on the grounds of equivalence. State both halves of its own result: a 1.8-month median gain, grade 3 or worse peripheral neuropathy in 17% versus 1% and fatigue in 17% versus 7%, and no quality-of-life data collected at all — PRODIGE 4, run in the same era, did collect it. The combination arm also received a higher median cumulative gemcitabine dose than the monotherapy arm (11,400 versus 9,000 mg/m²) because patients stayed on treatment longer, so part of the benefit is more gemcitabine and the trial cannot separate the two. Evidence & sources Its bilirubin ceiling was the upper limit of normal, stricter than PRODIGE 4's 1.5 times, which excludes many jaundiced patients with pancreatic head cancer — so the two landmark first-line trials selected differently in opposite directions on two different axes and their medians (8.5 and 11.1 months) are not comparable. The neuropathy recovery data are reported among patients who improved, with no cumulative incidence of unresolved neuropathy at a fixed time; APACT, the adjuvant trial of the same regimen, later found 84% of grade 3 or worse neuropathy had not improved to grade 1 or less at its primary cutoff. The preceding four-centre phase 1–2 result of 12.2 months did not replicate, falling by more than 3 months in the phase 3 trial — a caution that applies to every single-arm or few-centre figure quoted on this page. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
