Adjuvant trial of the same regimen: 84% of grade ≥3 neuropathy not improved to grade ≤1 at primary cutoff Adjuvant population, not the metastatic MPACT population

lead: Gemcitabine alone, or palliative and best supportive care NCCN recommends systemic therapy for patients with good or intermediate performance status, and makes palliative and best supportive care including palliative radiotherapy the preferred option for poor performance status; patients with ECOG 4 should be supported exclusively by palliative and best supportive care.
text: Gemcitabine alone, or palliative and best supportive care Evidence B NCCN recommends systemic therapy for patients with good or intermediate performance status, and makes palliative and best supportive care including palliative radiotherapy the preferred option for poor performance status; patients with ECOG 4 should be supported exclusively by palliative and best supportive care. Indications Preferred when A frail patient in whom single-agent treatment is the ceiling, or one for whom the honest offer is symptom control. Select patients with poor performance status may still benefit from single-agent chemotherapy or from a targeted agent identified on molecular profiling. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not treat a declining patient with a doublet to avoid the conversation. NCCN notes that patients with advanced disease can deteriorate abruptly — bleeding, thromboembolism, escalating pain, stent occlusion, cholangitis — and that new symptoms are often wrongly attributed to chemotherapy when the cause is gastric outlet obstruction or carcinomatosis.

lead: Order comprehensive genomic profiling and germline testing at the first visit, and bank enough tissue for it.
text: Standard Evidence B Order comprehensive genomic profiling and germline testing at the first visit, and bank enough tissue for it. Indications Preferred when Every patient with metastatic disease. NCCN asks for testing for fusions (ALK, NRG1, NTRK, ROS1, FGFR2, RET), mutations (BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS, PALB2), amplifications (HER2), microsatellite instability, mismatch repair deficiency and tumour mutational burden, using an FDA-approved or validated NGS assay, plus HER2 by immunohistochemistry with or without FISH. In metastatic disease, enough tissue for sequencing should be obtained at biopsy, with two extra needle passes banked. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not wait for the result before starting treatment. NCCN is explicit that if BRCA1/2 status is unknown, the patient is treated with systemic therapy as clinically indicated. The sequencing changes the maintenance and later-line decisions, not usually the first-line one. And do not quote the 5.5% germline figure as the proportion with an actionable result: it is driven mostly by ATM and BRCA2, and of the six genes it covers only BRCA1/2 has a randomised treatment consequence in this disease. Evidence & sources Downgraded from A to B. The recommendation is NCCN's; the evidence under it is mixed. The germline prevalence estimate comes from a clinic-based case series compared with public sequencing databases rather than a recruited control group, and carriage was not associated with survival (HR 0.86, P=.09). What is randomised is narrower: a phase 3 progression-free survival result in germline BRCA1/2 after platinum, and a phase 3 survival result in RAS G12 disease after prior therapy. Everything else on the molecular list is single-arm, in alterations reaching 1% to 2% of the disease or less, with pancreatic subsets of 10 to 40 patients and no screening denominators reported — so the testing is justified by the small number of large effects, not by the length of the panel. Screen for clinical-trial eligibility at the same visit; NCCN strongly encourages enrolment at every stage. [PAYER] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Treat biliary and gastric outlet patency, pain, nutrition and thrombosis as part of the treatment plan, with named owners.
text: Standard Evidence C Treat biliary and gastric outlet patency, pain, nutrition and thrombosis as part of the treatment plan, with named owners. Indications Preferred when For biliary obstruction NCCN prefers an endoscopic biliary metal stent, with percutaneous biliary drainage and subsequent internalisation as the alternative. For gastric outlet obstruction, EUS-guided gastrojejunostomy at a high-volume centre is an option. Exocrine insufficiency, pain and nutrition need active management because NCCN's own definition of a treatable performance status depends on them. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not attribute intractable nausea and vomiting to chemotherapy without excluding gastric outlet obstruction, or abdominal bloating and reduced intake without considering peritoneal carcinomatosis — NCCN names both as recognised misattributions. Evidence & sources A short course of radiotherapy may be given to painful metastatic sites such as bone. Plastic biliary stents may be considered for palliation where predicted survival is under 3 months. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Daraxonrasib for eligible metastatic PDAC; the US indication is not restricted to a RAS mutation RASolute 302 (phase 3, n=500 randomised, 248 daraxonrasib and 252 investigator's-choice chemotherapy, more than 90% with RAS G12 mutations) had dual primary endpoints in the RAS G12 population and met both: median overall survival 13.2 versus 6.6 months, hazard ratio 0.40, P<0.001, and median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review 7.3 versus 3.5 months, hazard ratio 0.45.
text: Daraxonrasib for eligible metastatic PDAC; the US indication is not restricted to a RAS mutation Evidence A RASolute 302 (phase 3, n=500 randomised, 248 daraxonrasib and 252 investigator's-choice chemotherapy, more than 90% with RAS G12 mutations) had dual primary endpoints in the RAS G12 population and met both: median overall survival 13.2 versus 6.6 months, hazard ratio 0.40, P<0.001, and median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review 7.3 versus 3.5 months, hazard ratio 0.45. Indications Preferred when The FDA approval of 26 August 2026 covers adults with metastatic PDAC after at least one systemic therapy, or those not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. The randomized trial studied patients progressing after one prior line; it does not directly establish the same benefit in untreated patients unfit for combinations. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Benefit was shown in the RAS G12 and overall randomized populations. In the small non-G12 subgroup (n=41), PFS HR was 1.38 (95% CI 0.60–3.17) while OS HR was 0.37 (0.15–0.93); these exploratory, imprecise estimates do not establish lack of benefit. Interpretation also requires the open-label design, short follow-up and differential treatment non-initiation (38/252 chemotherapy versus 7/248 daraxonrasib). Check the current prescribing information and patient-specific toxicity risks. Evidence & sources The comparator was unconstrained investigator's choice from gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, modified FOLFIRINOX, FOLFOX or liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil, given per local prescribing practice, and its 6.6-month median sits at the low end of published second-line outcomes, so its quality is not auditable from the report. The trial was open label with no crossover; overall survival in an open-label trial remains exposed to differential post-progression therapy, which is not detailed by arm. The sponsor supported the trial and performed and validated the statistical analyses, with five author employees. An overall survival hazard ratio of 0.40 in second-line PDAC is extraordinarily large and should be read with the comparator's 15.1% non-receipt and 11.2% toxicity discontinuation in view. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
