lead: Neoadjuvant systemic therapy, with or without subsequent chemoradiation, in a patient with high-risk features — presented as a selection exercise, not as a survival benefit.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Neoadjuvant systemic therapy, with or without subsequent chemoradiation, in a patient with high-risk features — presented as a selection exercise, not as a survival benefit. Indications Preferred when NCCN's high-risk features are equivocal or indeterminate imaging findings, markedly elevated CA 19-9 or CEA, large primary tumours, large regional nodes, excessive weight loss and extreme pain. Regimens differ by presumed subtype: CapeOx, FOLFIRINOX or FOLFOX for intestinal type; albumin-bound paclitaxel–gemcitabine, capecitabine–gemcitabine, cisplatin–gemcitabine or FOLFIRINOX for pancreatobiliary and mixed type. Repeat pancreatic-protocol CT or MRI afterwards, then operate if still resectable. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not offer it as a treatment effect. In the largest series NCCN cites — 8,688 ampullary cancers with 175 receiving neoadjuvant therapy — median overall survival was 43 against 33 months with surgery first and the difference was not significant (P=0.416), and the neoadjuvant patients were younger and more often node-positive. Neoadjuvant use runs at only 1%–4% of resections, downstaging occurred in 15%–67% of tumours, and NCCN states there is limited evidence to recommend specific neoadjuvant regimens off-study and that there are no prospective randomised phase III data behind these recommendations. Name the borrowing when you offer a regimen: modified FOLFIRINOX comes from PRODIGE-24, a trial of resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that excluded nonductal pancreatic tumours by design, restricted entry to WHO performance status 0–1, age under 80 and CA 19-9 under 180 U/mL, and produced grade 3 or 4 toxicity in 75.9% of patients — with an imprecise disease-free survival estimate in the 101 patients aged 70 or over (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.53–1.39), which does not establish absence of benefit, who are closer to the median age of ampullary cancer than the trial population as a whole. Evidence & sources Surgery first is NCCN's preferred route for resectable disease. Where chemoradiation is considered because of positive or close margins, chemotherapy should be given before it. Nothing in the adjuvant pancreatic trials transfers to the neoadjuvant ampullary setting: PRODIGE-24 enrolled only after complete macroscopic resection, excluded nonductal tumours, and reported in a disease whose resected median survival is roughly half that of ampullary cancer. [PROTOCOL] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Borrowed resected-PDAC trial: mFOLFIRINOX grade 3 or 4 toxicity 75.9%; age ≥70 subgroup (n=101) no DFS benefit, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.53–1.39) Ductal PDAC only, nonductal excluded; PS 0–1, age <80, CA 19-9 <180 U/mL

lead: Minimally invasive pancreatoduodenectomy where the programme does them.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Minimally invasive pancreatoduodenectomy where the programme does them. Indications Preferred when NCCN records that meta-analysis and a multicentre international cohort found better operative time, blood loss and length of stay with laparoscopic than open pancreatoduodenectomy. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid NCCN also states that how laparoscopic and robotic pancreatoduodenectomy compare with the open operation remains to be investigated, and the ampullary-specific data are thin. Approach is a programme decision about volume and expertise, not an oncological one. [EXPERTISE]

lead: Do not add an extended lymphadenectomy.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not add an extended lymphadenectomy. Why Why Standard regional lymphadenectomy, with the nodes counted. Mark and submit separately any station taken beyond the standard dissection, as PERIPAN asks. Additional cautions Additional cautions In the pancreatic literature, which NCCN carries across to this operation, a randomised single-institution trial, an Italian multicentre randomised series of 81 patients, a Japanese randomised multicentre trial and multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomised trials all found no survival impact from extended lymphadenectomy, with more postoperative diarrhoea. Sampling of aortocaval and common hepatic artery nodes can be considered because involvement there carries an inferior prognosis — that is staging, not therapy. Evidence & sources Downgraded from A to B. The randomised evidence against extended lymphadenectomy is strong, consistent and large, but all of it is in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; no randomised trial of lymphadenectomy extent has been done in ampullary cancer, and the extrapolation is NCCN's. Grade A on an ampullary page would claim randomised ampullary evidence that does not exist. The recommendation itself is not in doubt, and the direction of any residual uncertainty favours the standard operation. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not route a locally advanced tumour to a resection attempt without a second opinion.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not route a locally advanced tumour to a resection attempt without a second opinion. Why Why NCCN treats locally advanced ampullary disease the same way as metastatic disease in the current version, and asks for referral to a tertiary cancer centre for a second opinion about unresectability — that is clinical decision 7 from here. Additional cautions Additional cautions An exploratory attempt that violates the tumour plane converts a systemic-therapy patient into a systemic-therapy patient with a laparotomy.

lead: Report the subtype as intestinal, pancreatobiliary, mixed or tubular-NOS, based on the invasive component and on morphology, with immunohistochemistry as support rather than as the determinant.
text: Standard Evidence C Report the subtype as intestinal, pancreatobiliary, mixed or tubular-NOS, based on the invasive component and on morphology, with immunohistochemistry as support rather than as the determinant. Indications Preferred when Every resected invasive ampullary carcinoma. PERIPAN asks for subtyping of tubular-type adenocarcinomas based on the invasive component, reserving mixed for tumours with unequivocal intestinal and pancreatobiliary areas where the lesser component is at least 30%, and replacing the old term hybrid with tubular-NOS, with the favoured lineage and component percentages given in a comment. NCCN asks for intestinal, pancreatobiliary or mixed, with ambiguous cases classified as tubular adenocarcinoma with mixed features and the predominant pattern noted. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not rely on an immunohistochemical panel to settle it. NCCN states that immunohistochemistry is not required and that overlap between intestinal and pancreatobiliary profiles may make current panels unreliable for definitive determination. PERIPAN adds that pancreatobiliary tumours are more likely to express MUC1 and CK7 and less likely CDX2, MUC2 and CK20 — and the reverse for intestinal — but that none of these markers is entirely specific or sensitive individually or in combination, that studies have used positivity thresholds of 1%, 5%, 10%, 20% and 50%, and that even the best-performing published formula leaves more than a quarter of cases ambiguous. Evidence & sources Typical morphology: intestinal tumours have large tubules lined by tall columnar cells with elongated, pseudostratified, hyperchromatic nuclei, with dirty intraluminal necrosis as a further clue; pancreatobiliary tumours have more widely separated, smaller, simpler glands lined by cuboidal or low columnar cells without stratification, often with desmoplastic stroma. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: State the reproducibility of the subtype call alongside the call itself — interobserver agreement is fair, not good.
text: Standard Evidence B State the reproducibility of the subtype call alongside the call itself — interobserver agreement is fair, not good. Indications Preferred when Any report or board discussion where the subtype is about to drive a treatment choice. In 232 resected ampullary carcinomas with an invasive component over 3.0 mm, read independently and blind by five pathologists from five institutions, overall agreement on a purist four-category scheme was fair (κ 0.39, P<0.001) and all five observers agreed in 53 of 232 cases (23%). By consensus of three of five the commonest category was mixed pancreatobiliary-intestinal at 94 cases (40%), then pure pancreatobiliary 74 (32%), other 51 (22%) and pure intestinal only 13 (6%). Asked to force each tumour into a predominant pattern, agreement improved only to moderate (κ 0.44, P<0.0001) with all five agreeing in 81 cases (35%). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not present the prognostic claim without this, because the claim exists only under the forced classification. Under the purist scheme there was no survival difference at all: pure intestinal 80 against pure pancreatobiliary 40 months (P=0.33), and across pure pancreatobiliary, mixed and pure intestinal 40, 56 and 80 months (P=0.65), with T stage, node status and 3- and 5-year survival all non-significant. Only after the 94 indeterminate mixed tumours — 40% of the cohort — were force-assigned to a side did a difference appear: pancreatobiliary-predominant against intestinal-predominant median survival 41 against 80 months (P=0.026), 3-year 55% against 75%, 5-year 38% against 57%, hazard ratio for death 1.78 (95% CI 1.06–2.98, P=0.028). And that difference was not independent: on multivariable analysis high tumour budding, high T stage and node positivity all remained significant while predominant histologic type failed, P=0.39. NCCN's own position is that current data on the independent prognostic and predictive value of subtyping are conflicting. PERIPAN says the role of immunohistochemistry and tumour markers in prognosis or treatment response is still unclear, and attributes that to the inconsistent definitions of ampullary carcinoma used in the historical literature. Evidence & sources The mixed phenotype is a feature of the organ, not a failure of the pathologist: the ampulla sits at the junction of three epithelia, and intratumoral heterogeneity is expected. That is also why the subtype in a biopsy may not be the subtype in the tumour. Two details make the 23% full-agreement figure an optimistic ceiling rather than a floor. The cohort was restricted to tumours with an invasive component over 3.0 mm, which removes exactly the small, mostly intra-ampullary tumours where subtyping is hardest and where the classification would most change management. And in a side experiment within the same paper, two fields from a single tumour shown blind to eight observers were called pancreatobiliary by 6 of 8 and hybrid by 2 of 8 for one field, and intestinal by 4 of 8 and mixed by 4 of 8 for the other. Pure intestinal carcinoma — the phenotype that intestinal-type regimens are chosen for — comprised 13 of 232 cases under the purist scheme, so every statement about the pure intestinal phenotype in that paper rests on 13 patients. The counterweight, which is solid, is that even pancreatobiliary-predominant ampullary carcinoma behaved far better than pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: median 41 against 15.6 months (P<0.001), and hazard ratio 1.97 (95% CI 1.42–2.72, P<0.001) when matched for size and node status — although that 476-patient comparator cohort is described as previously unpublished, with no inclusion criteria, dates, stage distribution or treatment given. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Test every ampullary carcinoma for mismatch-repair deficiency as a reflex, regardless of subtype.
text: Standard Evidence C Test every ampullary carcinoma for mismatch-repair deficiency as a reflex, regardless of subtype. Indications Preferred when Every case at diagnosis. PERIPAN recommends reflex mismatch-repair testing by immunohistochemistry or PCR, on the grounds that recent studies show deficiency rates comparable to colorectal cancer and independent of subtype, and that deficiency identifies a subset with different behaviour and candidacy for immunotherapy. It asks for the result to follow the diagnosis immediately or accompany the final pathology report. The test is cheap, it is a germline trigger as well as a treatment test, and nothing about it depends on the subtype call being reliable — which is the strongest argument for making it a reflex. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not make it conditional on age, subtype or stage — but do not quote a prevalence figure with more confidence than the data carry. The one-in-six estimate PERIPAN relies on is graded low evidence and is the upper end of a wide range: deficiency was found in 18 of 119 tested non-medullary ampullary carcinomas (15%) in one institutional series, where the 119 were a convenience subset of 348 cases that happened to have been tested, and in only 1 of 23 early-onset ampullary carcinomas (4.3%) in a nationwide Dutch series where the same analysis found 11 of 23 duodenal carcinomas (47.8%) deficient. The claim that every mismatch-repair-deficient ampullary and pancreatic carcinoma in that Dutch series was attributable to Lynch syndrome rests on 1 ampullary and 2 pancreatic patients, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in that paper. Medullary-type ampullary carcinoma, 11 of 359 cases (3%) in one series, was mismatch-repair deficient in 7 of 11 (64%) and should prompt the test on sight. Evidence & sources NCCN reaches a narrower position, recommending somatic molecular profiling for patients with metastatic disease who are candidates for anticancer therapy, with microsatellite instability and mismatch-repair deficiency among the alterations sought; the 2021 ESGE ampullary guideline went further in the other direction and recommended against routine immunohistochemistry, PCR and microsatellite instability testing of ampullary biopsies, a position PERIPAN has since reversed. The reflex-for-all position is PERIPAN's and is the live local choice. Whichever is adopted, the local deficiency rate should be measured rather than assumed, because the published range runs from 4% to 15% and no series has established the figure in an unselected, consecutively tested ampullary population. [PAYER] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Single series: medullary type in 11 of 359 ampullary carcinomas (3%); mismatch-repair deficient in 7 of 11 (64%)

lead: Next-generation sequencing of the tumour, preferably RNA-based for fusions, in a patient who is a candidate for anticancer therapy.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Next-generation sequencing of the tumour, preferably RNA-based for fusions, in a patient who is a candidate for anticancer therapy. Indications Preferred when NCCN recommends tumour or somatic profiling by NGS for patients with metastatic disease who are candidates for therapy, to identify actionable alterations including fusions in ALK, NRG1, NTRK, ROS1, FGFR2 and RET, mutations in BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS and PALB2, HER2 amplification, microsatellite instability, mismatch-repair deficiency and tumour mutational burden, with HER2 overexpression by immunohistochemistry with or without FISH. Tissue is preferred; cell-free DNA may be considered if tissue testing is not feasible. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not expect the subtype to predict the genomics in an individual patient. A genomic classification of 3,411 periampullary cancers, as summarised by NCCN, found high concordance between histologic subtype and genomic category overall — pancreatobiliary resembling pancreatic adenocarcinoma with frequent KRAS mutation, intestinal resembling colorectal adenocarcinoma with APC and PIK3CA mutations, higher tumour mutational burden and mismatch-repair deficiency — but also significant genomic heterogeneity within each histologic subtype. NCCN adds that the prognostic value of KRAS over histologic subtype is questionable and that the distribution of KRAS across subtypes is unclear because the studies are small. Evidence & sources Other reported somatic alterations include APC, TP53, CDKN2A, DPC4, ELF3, PIK3CA, SMAD4 and HER2 amplification, with pathogenic germline BRCA1/2, ATM, RAD50 and MUTYH variants described. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Report the rare non-tubular subtypes separately, because they behave differently.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Report the rare non-tubular subtypes separately, because they behave differently. Indications Preferred when PERIPAN recognises medullary, micropapillary, gastric-type, rhabdoid and osteoclastic carcinomas, and poorly cohesive carcinoma with or without signet-ring cell formation, as entities to be reported separately from tubular adenocarcinomas. Medullary carcinoma was 11 of 359 ampullary carcinomas (3%), a frequency similar to the colon and unlike the pancreas; patients were younger (mean 57 against 65 years, P=0.02) and the invasive component was larger (mean 3.2 against 1.9 cm, P=0.01), while overall size did not differ significantly (3.5 against 2.6 cm, P=0.09). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not fold these into the intestinal/pancreatobiliary dichotomy, and do not carry the prognostic claim. In the medullary series 7 of 11 were mismatch-repair deficient against 18 of 119 tested non-medullary cases (15%, P<0.001), 6 of the 7 with MLH1/PMS2 loss, none carrying BRAF V600E, and 7 of 8 tested expressed PD-L1 by combined positive score and 6 of 8 by tumour proportion score, against 6 of 18 (33%) and 0 of 18 among non-medullary deficient carcinomas — a different therapeutic conversation entirely. But 5-year survival was 53% against 47% (P=0.47), and 53% against 48% against glandular ampullary carcinomas alone (P=0.84), so the suggestion that medullary carcinoma behaves less aggressively is a non-significant 6-point difference. Despite the pushing border, lymphovascular invasion was present in 7 of 11 (64%, identical to non-medullary) and node positivity was 40% against 46%. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D. Eleven cases with 3 deaths cannot support a survival comparison; no adjuvant treatment data are reported for either group; PD-L1 was assessed in 8 of 11 cases, EBV in 3, INI1 in 8 and MLH1 promoter methylation in 1, with no statement of why the others lacked tissue, which is a real risk of bias in exactly the markers that generate the therapeutic claim; the PD-L1-independent-of-MMR-status finding comes from 4 mismatch-repair-proficient tumours of which 3 stained positive; PD-L1 thresholds had to be extrapolated from lung and gastric cancer because none is established for the ampulla; and medullary morphology was assigned with no blinded review and no interobserver data, against a 50%-non-gland-forming criterion applied retrospectively to slides accrued over 1989 to 2013. The direction is real, the point estimates are fragile, and the authors state that a clinical trial is needed before immunotherapy can be recommended on these findings. Treat the subtype as a reason to test, not as a treatment decision. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Medullary 11 of 359 ampullary carcinomas (3%); medullary vs non-medullary: dMMR 7/11 vs 18/119 (15%), P<0.001; 5-y survival 53 vs 47% (P=0.47), NS Eleven cases, 3 deaths; markers tested in subsets only; no adjuvant data

lead: Do not let the subtype alone decide whether to give adjuvant therapy.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not let the subtype alone decide whether to give adjuvant therapy. Why Why Decide on stage, nodal burden, margin and fitness, and treat the subtype as one input among those — see clinical decision 7, where the two halves of the subtype-directed argument are set out. Additional cautions Additional cautions The two subtype-stratified analyses do not carry equal weight, and the full-text read explains their divergence by cohort and method rather than by chance. The positive result comes from 214 resections at 5 European centres, where adjuvant therapy was associated with longer median overall survival in the pancreatobiliary and mixed group (85 against 65 months, P=0.005; multivariable hazard ratio 0.351, 95% CI 0.151–0.851, P=0.015) with no significant benefit in intestinal tumours (115 against 147 months, hazard ratio 0.443, 0.099–1.984, P=0.287) — but in that same cohort the whole-cohort result was negative and numerically inverted, with median overall survival 168 months without adjuvant therapy against 113 months with it, hazard ratio 1.124 (0.756–1.987), P=0.608, and adjuvant therapy was allocated at tumour board on T3/4 stage, node positivity and raised CA 19-9, with no propensity matching, weighting or landmark analysis performed anywhere in the study. The negative result comes from 357 resections at 12 institutions, where adjuvant therapy was propensity-matched on the factors that actually drove its selection — node positivity (odds ratio 5.17, 95% CI 3.01–8.87) and perineural invasion (2.74, 1.59–4.70) — deaths within 90 days were excluded to limit immortal time bias, and the signal disappeared in both subtypes (intestinal hazard ratio 1.21, 0.67–2.16, P=0.53; pancreatobiliary 1.35, 0.66–2.76, P=0.41), at every stage stratum, and whether the analysis was restricted to fluorouracil-based or gemcitabine-based regimens, with no interaction between agent and subtype. NCCN cites a third retrospective study, of 475 patients, that found benefit confined to the intestinal subtype (5-year overall survival 83.7% against 33.2%, P=0.015) — a third direction from a third cohort. Evidence & sources Reid's reproducibility study is the ceiling on all of this: a classification with κ 0.39, full agreement in 23% of cases and 40% of tumours mixed cannot support a treatment interaction, and in that cohort the subtype itself failed multivariable analysis at P=0.39. Neither of the two adjuvant cohorts had central pathology review or immunohistochemistry, and one excluded 369 of 756 screened patients (49%) for unknown subtype — a larger group than the one analysed. Misclassification of that magnitude biases any subtype-by-agent interaction towards the null, which is an argument for reading the negative result cautiously as well; the propensity-matched intervals do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction, so what that study establishes is the absence of a large benefit rather than the absence of any. Decide on stage, nodal burden, margin and fitness, and treat the subtype as one input among those — see clinical decision 7. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not use the term papillary adenocarcinoma for the invasive component, and do not call pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia an ampullary precursor.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not use the term papillary adenocarcinoma for the invasive component, and do not call pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia an ampullary precursor. Why Why PERIPAN's nomenclature: intra-ampullary papillary tubular neoplasm for a precursor growing along the ampullary lumen, adenoma for one on the duodenal surface of the papilla, and the predominant component deciding when both are involved. Additional cautions Additional cautions Both habits move patients between disease categories on a word. PanIN is not an ampullary precursor, and incidental dysplasia in the pancreas or bile duct does not disqualify an ampullary origin. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Offer adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II and III disease as a reasonable choice, not as an established benefit — and give both halves of ESPAC-3 when you do.
text: Standard Evidence C Offer adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II and III disease as a reasonable choice, not as an established benefit — and give both halves of ESPAC-3 when you do. Indications Preferred when A fit patient within 12 weeks of resection, with a total systemic-therapy duration of about 6 months. ESPAC-3 periampullary is the only phase III randomised trial to enrol a substantial ampullary population: 434 randomised and 428 analysed from 100 centres in 18 countries, of whom 297 had ampullary, 96 intrapancreatic bile duct and 35 other cancers (10 duodenal, 25 nondescript), allocated to observation (144), bolus fluorouracil with folinic acid (143) or gemcitabine (141). NCCN carries a category 1 designation for fluorouracil–leucovorin and for gemcitabine on the strength of it. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid The primary analysis was negative. Median overall survival was 35.2 months (95% CI 27.2–43.0) with observation against 43.1 months (34.0–56.0) with chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.11), χ²=1.33, P=0.25, and the trial did not meet its primary endpoint. Significance appeared only in the prespecified multivariable analysis adjusting for age, bile duct cancer, poor tumour differentiation and positive lymph nodes: hazard ratio 0.75 (95% CI 0.57–0.98), Wald χ²=4.53, P=0.03, in a model of 415 patients and 236 deaths. By arm, unadjusted, fluorouracil against observation gave 0.95 (0.71–1.28), P=0.74 and gemcitabine 0.77 (0.57–1.05), P=0.10, with a three-group log-rank χ² of 2.96, P=0.23. The trial was open-label, a fifth of the fluorouracil arm (28 of 143) never received a dose, and only about half of each chemotherapy arm completed six cycles. Serious treatment-related adverse events were more frequent with fluorouracil–folinic acid than gemcitabine (70 of 143 patients, 49%, reporting 162 events against 43 of 141, 30%, reporting 81; P=0.002), with grade 3–4 diarrhoea 14% against 4% and stomatitis 11% against 0%. The authors themselves describe the positive multivariable result and the gemcitabine-specific result as hypothesis generating. Evidence & sources Downgraded from B to C on the full-text read, and the reason is specific: this page cannot cite ESPAC-3 as establishing adjuvant benefit in ampullary cancer. The trial was powered on 243 deaths and 430 patients to detect a 12 percentage-point absolute gain in 5-year survival (hazard ratio 0.68) across the pooled periampullary population, and the authors state that a separate survival analysis for each tumour type could not be built into the design because the incidence of each would have required an unattainable sample. It was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival is reported anywhere in the paper: within the 297 ampullary patients the medians are observation 40.6 months (95% CI 30.6–61.4, 59 deaths), fluorouracil 57.8 months (32.8–84.0, 50 deaths) and gemcitabine 70.8 months (45.3–not estimable, 42 deaths), and they appear without a P value. Two further features of the full text matter. First, the adjustment that turns the result positive was for four variables on two of which the observation arm was prognostically the worst at baseline — poorly differentiated 33% against 22% and 19%, node positive 62% against 60% and 54% — so the shift from 0.86 to 0.75 is partly correcting a randomisation imbalance rather than independently confirming the primary analysis, and its interval only just excludes 1. Second, pooling created a group in which chemotherapy looked harmful: in the 96 intrapancreatic bile duct patients, median survival was 27.2 months (15.4–31.9) with observation against 18.3 (12.9–28.7) with fluorouracil and 19.5 (16.2–36.1) with gemcitabine. Any pooled benefit is therefore carried by the ampullary and other patients, in whom it was never formally tested. Survival differed sharply by tumour type — ampullary 53.1 months (42.3–72.5), other 32.6, bile duct 20.9 (17.0–27.5), χ²=27.75, P<0.001, bile duct hazard ratio 2.13 (1.61–2.83) against ampullary — and the trial's own discussion concedes that intrapancreatic bile duct cancer may need to be treated as a separate entity. Observation-arm survival of 35 months is also far better than the ampullary literature of the era, which implies a fit, early-stage, selected population; screening data on who was excluded and why were not collected. See nonpm for a discrepancy in the extracted guideline text at this point. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Median OS 35.2 vs 43.1 mo, observation vs chemotherapy; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.11), P=0.25, primary endpoint not met; adjusted HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.57–0.98), P=0.03 Not powered for ampullary subgroup (297 of 428); adjusted result hypothesis generating

lead: Choose the regimen by subtype, understanding that every option except fluorouracil and gemcitabine is an extrapolation from another disease.
text: Standard Evidence C Choose the regimen by subtype, understanding that every option except fluorouracil and gemcitabine is an extrapolation from another disease. Indications Preferred when NCCN's lists. For pancreatobiliary and mixed type: fluorouracil–leucovorin, gemcitabine, capecitabine, capecitabine–gemcitabine, cisplatin–gemcitabine, FOLFOX or CapeOx, and modified FOLFIRINOX. For intestinal type: fluorouracil–leucovorin, gemcitabine, capecitabine, and FOLFOX or CapeOx. Chemotherapy precedes chemoradiation where chemoradiation is being considered for a positive or close margin. Only fluorouracil with folinic acid and single-agent gemcitabine have ever been given to ampullary patients in a randomised adjuvant trial, and that trial was negative on its primary endpoint. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Name the source of each extrapolation when consenting, and say that the two trials doing most of the work excluded this disease by design. Capecitabine–gemcitabine rests on ESPAC-4, a trial of resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in which nonductal pancreatic tumours were an explicit exclusion criterion: 730 patients analysed, median overall survival 28.0 months (95% CI 23.5–31.5) against 25.5 (22.7–27.9), hazard ratio 0.82 (0.68–0.98), P=0.032 — a 2.5-month median gain whose upper confidence limit almost touches 1, reported early on a monitoring committee's recommendation at 458 of a planned 480 deaths with no alpha adjustment presented, with the benefit concentrated in R0 patients (39.5 against 27.9 months) and essentially no separation in R1 disease (23.7 against 23.0 months), and grade 3–4 adverse events in 226 of 359 patients (63%) against 196 of 366 (54%). Modified FOLFIRINOX rests on PRODIGE-24, also resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with nonductal tumours excluded, and with entry restricted to WHO performance status 0–1, age under 80 and CA 19-9 under 180 U/mL: 493 patients, median disease-free survival 21.6 months (17.7–27.6) against 12.8 (11.7–15.2), hazard ratio 0.58 (0.46–0.73), P<0.001, median overall survival 54.4 against 35.0 months, hazard ratio 0.64 (0.48–0.86), P=0.003, at the cost of grade 3–4 toxicity in 180 of 237 patients (75.9%) against 128 of 242 (52.9%), and with an imprecise disease-free survival estimate in the 101 patients aged 70 or over (HR 0.86, 0.53–1.39), which does not establish absence of benefit. Capecitabine rests on BILCAP in biliary tract cancer, which excluded ampullary carcinoma and whose primary analysis was not significant (median overall survival 51.1 against 36.4 months, P=0.097), and on X-ACT in colon cancer for the intestinal subtype; cisplatin–gemcitabine on ABC-02 in advanced biliary tract cancer, which included 20 ampullary patients (subgroup OS HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.21–1.82) and was not an adjuvant trial (11.7 against 8.1 months, hazard ratio 0.64, 0.52–0.80, P<0.001); and CapeOx on a 31-patient phase II trial in advanced small bowel and ampullary cancers of which 12 were ampullary, again not adjuvant. The full-text review confirms that BILCAP excluded ampullary carcinoma and that ABC-02 included the small, imprecise ampullary subgroup described above. Evidence & sources NCCN states that the panel added capecitabine–gemcitabine for pancreatobiliary and mixed type on the basis of clinical expertise and that there are no prospective randomised phase III data supporting these recommendations. The two pancreatic trials are therefore borrowed evidence in the strict sense: both were designed to answer a question in a different tumour with roughly half the resected median survival of ampullary cancer, both excluded nonductal tumours as a matter of protocol, and neither reports a single ampullary patient. Transplanting a regimen with 75.9% grade 3–4 toxicity into a disease with no randomised evidence that any adjuvant chemotherapy helps is a decision about risk tolerance, not an application of trial evidence, and the consent conversation should say so. For stage I disease NCCN offers systemic therapy or observation; observation is a real option, not a concession. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

Capecitabine in biliary tract cancer: primary overall-survival analysis not significant (P=0.097) Extrapolated from biliary tract cancer; cited from abstract and guideline text only

lead: Adjuvant therapy directed by subtype NCCN lists different regimens for pancreatobiliary/mixed and intestinal type, so the guideline already uses subtype to choose the drug — but not to choose whether to treat.
text: Adjuvant therapy directed by subtype Evidence C NCCN lists different regimens for pancreatobiliary/mixed and intestinal type, so the guideline already uses subtype to choose the drug — but not to choose whether to treat. Indications Preferred when The argument for treating pancreatobiliary and mixed tumours preferentially rests on 214 resections at 5 European centres over 1996 to 2017, where adjuvant therapy gave median overall survival of 85 against 65 months in that group (P=0.005) and remained independent on multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 0.351, 95% CI 0.151–0.851, P=0.015), with no significant benefit in intestinal tumours (115 against 147 months, hazard ratio 0.443, 0.099–1.984, P=0.287). Regimens were pancreatic-type, gemcitabine monotherapy in 35 of 75 treated patients (46.6%). Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Read that cohort's whole-cohort result before relying on its subgroup. Across all 214 patients, median overall survival was 168 months without adjuvant therapy against 113 months with it, hazard ratio 1.124 (95% CI 0.756–1.987), P=0.608 — crude survival was 55 months longer in the untreated patients, because the decision to treat was made at multidisciplinary meeting on T3/4 stage, node positivity and raised CA 19-9, and no propensity matching, inverse-probability weighting or landmark analysis was performed anywhere in the study. A protective hazard ratio of 0.351 appearing only after the cohort is cut by subtype, in a dataset whose unstratified signal runs the other way, with no interaction test reported and only 53 treated pancreatobiliary or mixed patients supporting a model that also contains ASA, CEA, T, N, grade and margin, is the pattern of a subgroup artefact. The intestinal point estimate is in the same protective direction and merely imprecise. Subtype itself was not independent in the whole cohort (hazard ratio 1.559, 0.756–3.216, P=0.229); the 16 mixed tumours were pooled with pancreatobiliary after the data were seen; subtype was assigned locally at 5 centres over 21 years with no central review or immunohistochemistry; 20% of treated patients had an unknown regimen and treatment completion and dose intensity were not captured; year of surgery is not adjusted for in any model despite the cohort straddling the introduction of adjuvant gemcitabine; and several reported hazard ratios lie outside their own confidence limits. The whole-cohort median overall survival of 136.5 months is also far outside every other series in this literature, against a median follow-up of 80 months. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Adjuvant therapy directed by stage, nodes and margin, ignoring subtype NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III.
text: Adjuvant therapy directed by stage, nodes and margin, ignoring subtype Evidence C NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III. Indications Preferred when NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III. The best-adjusted individual-patient analysis sits here too: in 357 resections at 12 institutions, with 81 propensity-matched pairs, adjuvant therapy showed no survival benefit overall (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.51–1.56, P=0.69) and none within any stage stratum, while stage drove both treatment and outcome — adjuvant use rose from 17.4% in stage I to 64.0% in stage II and 74.0% in stage III, and median survival fell from 137 to 57 to 45 months. Adding radiotherapy conferred nothing against surgery alone (hazard ratio 0.77, 0.41–1.44, P=0.41) or against chemotherapy alone (1.58, 0.69–2.60, P=0.28), and recurrence was predominantly distant (38 of 58, 65.5%) rather than locoregional (11 of 58, 19.0%). The registry weight points the other way: NCCN's discussion reports that in 4,190 National Cancer Database cases adjuvant chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 47.2 against 35.5 months (hazard ratio 0.82, P<0.01) and adjuvant chemoradiation 38.1 against 31.0 months (0.84, P=0.02), with higher T and N stages appearing to benefit most, and two large meta-analyses of 71 studies with 8,280 patients and of 10 studies with 3,361 report clinical benefit. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid All of the supportive evidence is registry and retrospective, and the confounding runs one way: NCCN records that in the studies finding no effect, adjuvant therapy was more frequently used in patients with more advanced disease. That biases towards finding no benefit in unadjusted analyses and towards finding benefit once stage is adjusted — which is exactly the pattern the literature shows, including inside ESPAC-3 itself. The propensity-matched null is not a clean negative either: matching discarded 195 of 357 patients, the matched intervals do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction, half the screened population (369 of 756) was excluded for unknown subtype, matching omitted grade, lymphovascular invasion, margin, CA 19-9 and year of surgery despite grade, lymphovascular invasion and margin all differing between treated and untreated patients, median follow-up of 34 months is shorter than the 57-month median survival, and the 17-year accrual is dominated by gemcitabine monotherapy so it cannot speak to modern multiagent therapy. Black race appeared as one of the strongest predictors of both death (hazard ratio 3.93, 95% CI 1.95–7.93) and treatment omission (odds ratio 0.26, 0.09–0.76), which signals access and socioeconomic confounding that no propensity model built on tumour variables can absorb. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Adjuvant chemoradiation after chemotherapy for a positive or close margin, or for node-positive disease, as a shared decision.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Adjuvant chemoradiation after chemotherapy for a positive or close margin, or for node-positive disease, as a shared decision. Indications Preferred when NCCN lists chemoradiation as an option after chemotherapy for stage II and III disease, with capecitabine or fluorouracil concurrent for all subtypes and gemcitabine concurrent for pancreatobiliary type only. NCCN cites a systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 retrospective studies including 3,361 ampullary cancers in which adjuvant chemoradiation reduced the risk of death (hazard ratio 0.75, P=0.01), with the benefit reported as concentrated in node-positive disease — median overall survival 32.1 against 15.7 months (hazard ratio 0.47, P=0.004) in 186 patients with nodal involvement, and improved disease-specific and overall survival in N2 disease in 1,106 patients. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not present it as established. NCCN records contradictory studies on the usefulness of adjuvant chemoradiation in ampullary cancer, all the supporting evidence is retrospective, adjuvant therapy in these series was preferentially given for higher T stage, nodal involvement and close or positive margins, and the one randomised EORTC trial of adjuvant chemoradiation in pancreatic head and periampullary cancers did not report how many patients had ampullary cancer. The one individual-patient analysis in this depot that matched on the drivers of treatment selection found that adding radiotherapy conferred nothing — against surgery alone hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.41–1.44), P=0.41, and against chemotherapy alone 1.58 (0.69–2.60), P=0.28 — in a disease whose recurrences are distant in roughly two-thirds of cases and locoregional in a fifth. Adjuvant chemoradiation use fell from 20% to 12% between 2004–2005 and 2012–2013 while chemotherapy use rose from 9% to 32%. Evidence & sources Chemotherapy first, then chemoradiation, is NCCN's sequence. Downgraded from C to D: every supporting figure is registry or meta-analysed retrospective data with treatment allocated by the prognostic factors being adjusted for, no randomised trial reports an ampullary result, and the best-adjusted cohort analysis is negative. The recommendation stays on the page because NCCN lists it and because a close or positive margin is a real clinical problem with few other answers, but it should be offered as a shared decision in the absence of evidence rather than as a standard of care. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not tell a patient that adjuvant chemotherapy has been shown to improve survival in resected ampullary cancer.
text: Avoid Evidence B Do not tell a patient that adjuvant chemotherapy has been shown to improve survival in resected ampullary cancer. Why Why Say what is true: the one randomised trial missed its primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.66–1.11, P=0.25), became significant only after adjustment for four prognostic variables on two of which the observation arm was worse at baseline (0.75, 0.57–0.98, P=0.03), was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and reports no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival anywhere. Then offer it, because the adjusted estimate and the registry data point the same way and because there is nothing better to offer — but offer it as a reasonable choice rather than as a demonstrated benefit, and record which it was presented as. Additional cautions Additional cautions The overstatement is not hypothetical — the extracted NCCN systemic-therapy page itself states that ESPAC-3 demonstrated significant improvements in disease-free and overall survival with adjuvant gemcitabine or fluorouracil versus observation in resectable ampullary adenocarcinoma, which the published trial does not support, and quotes median survivals of 23.0 and 23.6 months that match the ESPAC-3 pancreatic cohort rather than the periampullary trial. Confirm the wording against the published guideline before quoting it. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×
tied_results: RCT, adjuvant chemotherapy vs observation: primary endpoint missed, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.11), P=0.25; significant only after adjustment, HR 0.75 (0.57–0.98), P=0.03 Observation arm worse at baseline on two adjusted variables; not powered for ampullary subgroup

lead: Do not start adjuvant therapy without the subtype and mismatch-repair result in hand.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not start adjuvant therapy without the subtype and mismatch-repair result in hand. Why Why NCCN asks for adjuvant therapy to start within 12 weeks of surgery if the patient is fit, which leaves time for both results; PERIPAN asks for mismatch-repair testing to accompany the final pathology report. Additional cautions Additional cautions Starting a pancreatobiliary regimen in a tumour that turns out to be intestinal, or missing a mismatch-repair-deficient tumour, is an avoidable error of sequence rather than of judgement. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Biopsy a metastatic site to confirm the diagnosis, using a core biopsy wherever possible so there is tissue for profiling.
text: Standard Evidence D Biopsy a metastatic site to confirm the diagnosis, using a core biopsy wherever possible so there is tissue for profiling. Indications Preferred when NCCN's own sequence for metastatic disease: biopsy confirmation preferably from a metastatic site, with core biopsy recommended if possible to obtain adequate tissue for molecular profiling or other ancillary studies, and histologic subtyping attempted on whichever specimen is obtained. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not accept a cytological aspirate as the end of the diagnostic process when systemic therapy and molecular profiling both depend on the tissue. PERIPAN prefers core material over cytology for the same reason, and asks that the pathologist be told when a patient will not go to surgery so that immunohistochemical and molecular tests are done without delay. Evidence & sources In this setting subtyping on the biopsy is appropriate rather than discouraged, because it may influence treatment and no resection specimen is coming. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Choose first-line systemic therapy by performance status and presumed subtype, and define performance status the way NCCN does.
text: Standard Evidence D Choose first-line systemic therapy by performance status and presumed subtype, and define performance status the way NCCN does. Indications Preferred when NCCN defines good performance status as ECOG 0–1 with good biliary drainage and adequate nutritional intake, intermediate as ECOG 2 and poor as ECOG 3 — so drainage and nutrition are part of the eligibility assessment, not a separate matter. For pancreatobiliary and mixed type with good or intermediate status: albumin-bound paclitaxel–gemcitabine, capecitabine–gemcitabine, cisplatin–gemcitabine, cisplatin–durvalumab–gemcitabine, or FOLFOX; with ECOG 0–1 only, also FOLFIRINOX or modified FOLFIRINOX and NALIRIFOX. For poor performance status, palliative and best supportive care are preferred. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not treat any of these backbones as validated in this disease. ABC-02 randomised 410 patients with locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer or ampullary cancer to cisplatin–gemcitabine or gemcitabine, giving median overall survival 11.7 against 8.1 months (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.52–0.80, P<0.001) and progression-free survival 8.0 against 5.0 months (P<0.001) — the ampullary subgroup contained 20 patients (9 cisplatin–gemcitabine, 11 gemcitabine), with OS HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.21–1.82), too imprecise to establish a separate ampullary benefit. The FOLFIRINOX and modified FOLFIRINOX options arrive from PRODIGE-24 and the gemcitabine-based ones partly from ESPAC-4, both of which were trials of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that excluded nonductal tumours by protocol, and PRODIGE-24 produced grade 3 or 4 toxicity in 75.9% of a population restricted to performance status 0–1 and age under 80. NCCN states that data for systemic therapy in ampullary cancer are very limited and that the recommendations are extrapolated from pancreatic, colorectal and biliary tract cancer. Evidence & sources Subtype-directed selection partly extrapolates from colorectal, pancreatic and biliary cancers. ABC-02 did include 20 ampullary patients, with an imprecise subgroup OS HR of 0.62 (95% CI 0.21–1.82). ABC-06 separately included 11 ampullary patients after GemCis progression; it informs the subsequent-treatment discussion below, not first-line or adjuvant therapy. Screen for clinical trials and explain these population limits. [PROTOCOL] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Cisplatin–gemcitabine vs gemcitabine (n=410, advanced biliary tract incl. ampullary): median OS 11.7 vs 8.1 mo, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.52–0.80), P<0.001 Ampullary patients not counted, effect size unknown; cited from abstract and guideline text only
Source trial of the FOLFIRINOX options: grade 3–4 toxicity in 75.9% of a population restricted to PS 0–1 and age <80 Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma trial; nonductal tumours excluded by protocol

lead: Order somatic profiling and germline testing, and act on mismatch-repair deficiency.
text: Standard Evidence C Order somatic profiling and germline testing, and act on mismatch-repair deficiency. Indications Preferred when Every metastatic patient who is a candidate for anticancer therapy. NCCN's actionable list includes ALK, NRG1, NTRK, ROS1, FGFR2 and RET fusions, BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS and PALB2 mutations, HER2 amplification and overexpression, microsatellite instability, mismatch-repair deficiency and tumour mutational burden, with RNA-based assays preferred for fusions. Mismatch-repair deficiency is the highest-yield single result, reported in 15% of tested non-medullary ampullary carcinomas in one institutional series and in 64% of the rare medullary variant. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not equate the gene with the target, and do not let a negative tissue result end the question — NCCN accepts cell-free DNA testing where tissue testing is not feasible. Do not quote a firm deficiency prevalence either: the 15% figure comes from 18 of 119 cases that happened to have been tested out of 348, and a nationwide series of early-onset disease found deficiency in only 1 of 23 ampullary carcinomas (4.3%), so the published range is wide and the local rate should be measured. Evidence & sources A deficient result is also a germline trigger, though the ampullary evidence for that is a single case: in the nationwide early-onset series the one deficient ampullary carcinoma and both deficient pancreatic carcinomas proved to be Lynch syndrome, while the strong signal in that study was in duodenal cancer (11 of 23 deficient, 8 Lynch and 2 constitutional mismatch repair deficiency). Refer on the result, not on the prevalence estimate. [PAYER] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: OPEN proposal AMP-R1: local therapy or surgery after systemic response in selected oligometastatic disease; not an activated institutional pathway.
text: Proposed — not activated Evidence D OPEN proposal AMP-R1: local therapy or surgery after systemic response in selected oligometastatic disease; not an activated institutional pathway. Indications Preferred when NCCN lists systemic therapy followed by surgery or other locally directed therapies to liver or lung metastases for select patients with oligometastatic disease and response or stable disease on systemic therapy, after multidisciplinary review. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid There is no comparative evidence in ampullary cancer, and the selection that produces the good outcomes is doing the work. Treat it as a protocol and registry activity rather than a standard offer. [REGISTRY] [PROTOCOL] Evidence & sources The liver is the dominant distant site: 38%–65% of distant recurrences in series reporting site, with peritoneum, lung and bone following. Nodal involvement was the sole predictor of liver metastasis in one analysis. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Palliative radiotherapy or chemoradiation for symptoms, and palliative care alongside treatment rather than after it.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Palliative radiotherapy or chemoradiation for symptoms, and palliative care alongside treatment rather than after it. Indications Preferred when NCCN offers systemic therapy followed by radiotherapy for palliative indications, and palliative radiotherapy for severe pain refractory to analgesic therapy in the subsequent-therapy setting. Palliative and best supportive care run concurrently in every performance-status band, and are the preferred option in ECOG 3. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not present palliative radiotherapy as disease control. It is symptom-directed here, and the ampullary-specific evidence is confined to small retrospective series.

lead: After progression, reassess fitness, biliary drainage, prior treatment and toxicity, molecular targets and trial options; consider a subsequent regimen when appropriate.
text: Reasonable Evidence D After progression, reassess fitness, biliary drainage, prior treatment and toxicity, molecular targets and trial options; consider a subsequent regimen when appropriate. Indications Preferred when For a fit patient after gemcitabine–cisplatin, FOLFOX with active symptom control is a qualified option. ABC-06 enrolled 162 biliary-tract patients with ECOG 0–1 after GemCis progression: median OS 6.2 versus 5.3 months, adjusted HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.50–0.97), against active symptom control alone. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Only 11 patients had ampullary cancer (4 FOLFOX, 7 control); their exploratory OS HR was 0.71 (0.18–2.77). This does not establish an independent ampullary benefit, first-line or adjuvant efficacy, or benefit after prior oxaliplatin. Address drainage, organ function, infection and residual neuropathy before treatment. Evidence & sources Continue active symptom control throughout. When further anticancer treatment is unsuitable or declined, prioritize supportive care, symptom treatment and goals-of-care planning. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not treat an ampullary tumour as pancreatic cancer because it sits next to the pancreas.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not treat an ampullary tumour as pancreatic cancer because it sits next to the pancreas. Why Why Record the epicentre, use the subtype to pick a backbone, and quote survival figures from ampullary rather than pancreatic series. Additional cautions Additional cautions Even the worst tubular ampullary group outperforms pancreatic adenocarcinoma substantially — median 41 against 15.6 months matched for size and node status, hazard ratio 1.97 (95% CI 1.42–2.72), and 3-year survival 41% against 11% in the ampullary-ductal subset — so a pancreatic prognosis given to an ampullary patient is wrong in a direction that changes their decisions. Hold the figures loosely: the matched comparison uses a 476-patient pancreatic cohort described as previously unpublished with no inclusion criteria or treatment data, and part of the ampullary advantage in the modern literature comes from the strict epicentre definition having reclassified 21% of previously labelled ampullary cases, mostly pancreatic, out of the group. Evidence & sources Evidence & sources i Evidence & sources Evidence & sources ×

lead: Do not start systemic therapy in an undrained, cholestatic patient and call the resulting toxicity a performance-status problem.
text: Avoid Evidence D Do not start systemic therapy in an undrained, cholestatic patient and call the resulting toxicity a performance-status problem. Why Why Drain first where drainage is indicated, by ERCP in preference to the percutaneous route, with a stent as short as feasible; NCCN builds drainage and nutrition into its definition of good performance status for exactly this reason. Additional cautions Additional cautions The sequence error is common and it is attributed afterwards to the patient rather than to the plan.

lead: After papillectomy/ampullectomy: duodenoscopy with scar/abnormal-area biopsies within 3 months, at 6 and 12 months, then yearly for ≥5 years.
text: Standard Evidence C After papillectomy/ampullectomy: duodenoscopy with scar/abnormal-area biopsies within 3 months, at 6 and 12 months, then yearly for ≥5 years. Full explanation i Full explanation Recommendation: full explanation and evidence × After endoscopic papillectomy or surgical ampullectomy, perform duodenoscopy with biopsies of the scar and of any abnormal area within the first 3 months, at 6 and 12 months, and yearly thereafter for at least 5 years. Indications Preferred when Every patient after either operation. This is ESGE's schedule (strong recommendation, low quality evidence), and the recurrence data support the duration rather than only the opinion: in a 136-patient cohort recurrence occurred at a mean of 3.2 years with a range of 0.5 to 9.75 years, 9 of 20 recurrences (45%) appeared after the first two years of surveillance, and the rate was 5.8 per 100 person-years (95% CI 3.6–8.8), with cumulative recurrence 3.2% at 1 year, 8.9% at 2, 11.3% at 3 and 14.5% at 5 years. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not shorten the programme because the margin was negative. In 22 Japanese centres cumulative recurrence after R0 was 4.9% at 1 year, 11% at 3 years and 13% at 5 years, against 20% and 22% overall, and R0 was achieved in only 416 of 798 specimens (52.1%); recurrence rates in the single-centre cohort did not differ by baseline pathology. The schedule itself, though, is panel judgement: ESGE specifies examinations at 3, 6 and 12 months and then yearly to the month, on low-quality evidence, with no derivation, no interval-cancer analysis and no assessment of cost or patient burden, and the 3-month examination mostly detects residual rather than recurrent disease. Evidence & sources At least 5 years is a minimum, not a maximum — recurrences out to nearly 10 years are documented and ESGE's own wording is at least 5 years. Two cautions on the cohort that makes the case for longer follow-up. Its mean follow-up of 2.8 years is shorter than its mean time to recurrence of 3.2 years, so more than half the person-time needed to observe what it describes was never accumulated, and the suggestion of ten-year surveillance rests on one patient recurring at 9.75 years. And its own stratifications run against the usual direction — recurrence in 19.4% after en bloc against 7.0% after piecemeal resection, and 16.5% after an initially complete against 6.1% after an incomplete resection — which is the signature of early residual disease being reclassified out of the recurrence count rather than of a protective effect of piecemeal resection. Whether this programme extends surveillance beyond 5 years is an unresolved local approval item, and the honest basis for extending it is that recurrence after R0 is still running at 13% by 5 years, not the single late outlier. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: 22-centre Japanese cohort: cumulative recurrence after R0 4.9% at 1 y, 11% at 3 y, 13% at 5 y, against 20% and 22% overall R0 achieved in only 416 of 798 specimens (52.1%)

lead: After resection of ampullary adenocarcinoma, follow NCCN's oncological schedule, and record that pancreatoduodenectomy for adenoma needs no surveillance.
text: Standard Evidence D After resection of ampullary adenocarcinoma, follow NCCN's oncological schedule, and record that pancreatoduodenectomy for adenoma needs no surveillance. Indications Preferred when NCCN: surveillance every 3–6 months for 2 years, then every 6–12 months for up to 5 years as clinically indicated, comprising history and examination, CT chest and CT or MRI of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast, and CEA and/or CA 19-9. Patients who have had an adenoma resected by pancreatoduodenectomy do not need surveillance, because the at-risk mucosa has gone. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not over-read the markers. NCCN records contradictory associations between CEA or CA 19-9 and recurrence or survival in ampullary cancer and concludes that the prognostic utility of these markers remains controversial. A rising marker is a reason to image, not a diagnosis. Evidence & sources NCCN's figures: recurrence rates after resection are 28%–55%, with distant recurrence about 80% of events and the liver the commonest site at 38%–65% of distant recurrences. Recurrences are reported as early as under 6 months and as late as 22.5 months, so the front-loaded interval is appropriate. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: In polyposis, set the surveillance interval on the Spigelman stage and on the appearance of the ampulla, taking whichever is shorter.
text: Standard Evidence D In polyposis, set the surveillance interval on the Spigelman stage and on the appearance of the ampulla, taking whichever is shorter. Indications Preferred when Every patient with familial adenomatous polyposis, attenuated FAP or MUTYH-associated polyposis. ESGE in 2019 was the first guideline to build the ampullary appearance into the interval, and BSG adopted it in 2020: 5 years for a normal ampulla, 3 years for adenomatous change under 10 mm and 1 year for adenomatous change of 10 mm or more, applied alongside the Spigelman interval. Start surveillance at 25 for FAP and attenuated FAP and 35 for MUTYH-associated polyposis under the European guidelines, 20–30 and 30–35 under the US ones. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Do not rely on the Spigelman stage alone. It measures duodenal polyp burden and contains no information about the ampulla, yet about 50% of duodenal cancers in these patients arise in the ampullary region, and neither the Spigelman classification nor its individual components predict the development of ampullary carcinoma. An abnormal-looking ampulla was an independent risk factor for duodenal high-grade dysplasia in one series. The original 1989 paper made the point itself and then left it out of its own score: among the 80 polyposis patients biopsied at both sites, the papilla was adenomatous in 81% against 41% for the peripapillary area, and periampullary biopsy found adenoma in 11 patients whose duodenum was otherwise normal. Evidence & sources Downgraded from C to D because neither half of this recommendation has been validated. The Spigelman score was devised in a single cross-sectional screening round of 102 patients, with its four components and their cut-points assigned by expert judgement from known adenoma and cancer risk factors rather than derived from any cancer outcome; no patient in that paper developed duodenal cancer during the study, 11 of 102 (11%) were stage IV, and no formal validation has appeared in the four decades since. Its four components each contribute 1 to 3 points as though equally weighted, its stage boundaries are arbitrary breaks in a 4-to-12-point range, and two of the four require histology, so the modern practice of computing the stage without biopsies does not measure the quantity the score was built from. The ESGE and BSG ampullary intervals of 5, 3 and 1 year carry no citation, no modelling and no stated derivation in the guideline text; they are described there as proposed intervals that seem safe. The stage does still carry information about the duodenum, and the best available support for that is modest: in 77 Japanese familial adenomatous polyposis patients followed a median 8.5 years, high-grade dysplasia arose during surveillance in 5 of 8 Spigelman stage IV patients (63% in the abstract and conclusions, reported as 4 of 8, 50%, in the results and discussion of the same paper) and in none of those at stages 0, II or III, with stage I containing no patients at all. That cohort produced one invasive duodenal carcinoma in total and it was present at the first endoscopy, so it observed essentially no incident cancer; lesions under 10 mm and ampullary tumours under 10 mm were not biopsied by protocol and unbiopsied patients were assigned the minimum histology and dysplasia scores, which pushes them towards the lower stages and concentrates events in stage IV by construction. Refer patients with a duodenal adenoma of 10 mm or more, or an ampullary adenoma of any size, to an expert centre. [EXPERTISE] Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×
tied_results: Cross-sectional, 80 polyposis patients biopsied at both sites: papilla adenomatous in 81% vs peripapillary area 41%; periampullary adenoma in 11 with normal duodenum Single screening round of 102; no patient developed duodenal cancer; score never validated

lead: Compute the Spigelman stage from previous pathology or from optical diagnosis, rather than biopsying duodenal lesions routinely.
text: Reasonable Evidence D Compute the Spigelman stage from previous pathology or from optical diagnosis, rather than biopsying duodenal lesions routinely. Indications Preferred when ESGE discourages routine biopsies of suspected duodenal lesions in polyposis because they interfere with future optical diagnosis and with endoscopic resection, and recommends determining the Spigelman stage from previous pathology reports or from optical diagnosis when resection is unnecessary because the adenoma is under 10 mm and not suspicious for invasive growth. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Note the collision with clinical decision 1: in a sporadic ampullary lesion the biopsy is essential and its false-negative rate is the central problem, while in polyposis routine biopsy of duodenal lesions is discouraged and ampullary biopsy carries a pancreatitis risk. These are different populations with different base rates, and the rules should not be swapped. Evidence & sources A worked example of the modified approach: one centre stopped biopsying duodenal lesions in 2017, computes the Spigelman score from prior histology, performs endoscopic mucosal resection for duodenal adenomas over 10 mm, and raises the Spigelman stage by one in the presence of an endoscopically evident papillary adenoma. That is a local convention, not a guideline. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Endoscopic ampullectomy for a progressive ampullary adenoma in polyposis, understanding the recurrence rate.
text: Reasonable Evidence C Endoscopic ampullectomy for a progressive ampullary adenoma in polyposis, understanding the recurrence rate. Indications Preferred when An ampullary adenoma of 10 mm or more that is growing, or where invasive growth is suspected, at an expert centre. Contraindications & cautions Caution / avoid Recurrence after endoscopic ampullectomy in these patients is reported at 19%–58%, residual or recurrent ampullary disease in 15%–38% of patients across cohorts, haemorrhage 4%–21%, pancreatitis 4%–30% and perforation 2%–3% — and there is no long-term evidence that endoscopic therapy reduces cancer risk, delays surgery or improves survival. A Spigelman stage IV patient downstaged by endoscopic therapy remains high risk and in one cohort had a higher rate of subsequent progression than patients with primary progression. Argon plasma coagulation as primary therapy performed poorly, with persistent or recurrent duodenal disease in 12 of 16 patients (75%) and no regression of the primary lesion at 1 year. Evidence & sources One Dutch cohort reported duodenal surgery-free survival of 71% at 71 months after endoscopic papillectomy and 74% at 89 months after polypectomy. Maximum follow-up for ampullary disease in these studies was 5.9 years against 10 years for non-ampullary disease, so the ampullary figures are the less mature. All of these numbers reach this page through one narrative review, which collates them as unweighted ranges across 7 cohort studies totalling 181 polyposis patients, six of them single-centre retrospective series of at most 49 subjects, with no protocol, no second reviewer, no risk-of-bias appraisal and no pooling; its own authors conclude that the true effect of endoscopic therapy on prevention of duodenal surgery, cancer and survival cannot be determined and suggest it may be time to reconsider its use. Quote the ranges as a reason to involve the patient in the decision, not as a risk estimate. Explanation and evidence i Explanation and evidence Explanation and evidence ×

lead: Do not substitute a forward-viewing gastroscope without a cap for a proper ampullary examination at surveillance.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not substitute a forward-viewing gastroscope without a cap for a proper ampullary examination at surveillance. Why Why Side-viewing duodenoscopy, or cap-assisted forward-viewing endoscopy, with the duodenum and the ampullary site thoroughly assessed and documented at every examination. Additional cautions Additional cautions Adenomatosis of the ampulla is under-reported in endoscopy documentation even in experienced centres, and until 2019 no guideline said what to do when it was found — so an undocumented papilla is the default failure. Chromoendoscopy is not recommended for duodenal surveillance, and EUS is not routine but may be considered for a large or suspicious periampullary lesion to separate benign from invasive growth. lead: Do not treat non-attendance as the patient's problem alone.
text: Avoid Evidence C Do not treat non-attendance as the patient's problem alone. Why Why Counsel on the expected disease course and optimise sedation, and record a named owner for the surveillance programme. Additional cautions Additional cautions Between 20% and 60% of FAP patients are non-adherent to endoscopic surveillance. Patients naive to sedation during surveillance were substantially more likely to be non-compliant (odds ratio 9.23, 95% CI 1.46–58.23, P<0.05) in one patient-reported study, which makes sedation practice a modifiable determinant of surveillance quality rather than a comfort question.
